what changed (no `revision(of:)` or `touched`). A query takes one as it takes up the file and reads
it off the main actor, uninterrupted, whatever commits land meanwhile ([Queries](#queries)).

```swift
let graph = topology.snapshot()                                         // on the main actor, O(1)
Task.detached {
    graph.forEachShape { record, board in … }                          // every shape the app can show, in file order
    graph.neighbors(of: note, .outgoing, types: .within(ArrowEdge.id))  // as the index would have answered
}
```

Beside the index's questions, it reads the file whole:

- **`forEachShape(inFileOrder:)`**: every shape on a board the app can show, kept-aside ones too,
  with its board, in file order, the tree's, depth first: the root's shapes in no container, back to
  front, each followed at once by what's inside it (what it holds, back to front, then, for a shape
  that owns a board, that board's shapes in no container), and theirs, before the next. It's
  iterative, so a chain of boards or containers of any depth is walked, and no board or container
  twice. An error its body throws stops it, and comes out as the body's own type (`throws(E)`: a
  query's cancellation is a `QueryError`).
- **`fileOrderKey(of:)`**: where a shape comes in that order, as a key that sorts lexicographically
  (for each shape it's inside, from the outermost down, then for itself, its place among what's
  directly inside the same shape: its index on its board); nil off the boards the app can show.
  O(its depth): for putting a few shapes in order without walking the file.
- **`topLevel`**, the shapes inside nothing (the root's in no container, in document order), and
  **`isTopLevel(_:)`**, O(1); **`descendants(of:)`**, every shape inside a shape at any depth, in file
  order (O(what's inside it)); and **`container(of:on:)`**, the container a record on a board is
  directly in there, O(1), with no lookup for a shape in none: what a query's walk reads for each
  shape it has, working out what's above each container and each board once.
- **`shape(_:)`**, a record on a board the app can show, kept aside or not (`isOpaque` tells), nil
  elsewhere (O(its depth)); **`presentTypes`**, the types of the edges the file has, declared or
  not; and **`end(_:)`**, as the index's.

**Hold one for a task, never past it.** Nothing is copied while it's held until a commit changes a
table it shares; that commit copies the table, once (a move changes none of the index's; a shape
added or removed copies the file's `locations`). Kept, a snapshot makes every later commit's first
change to a table copy it. And one taken as services take a commit in has the commit: the index is
looked up (`editor.topology`), or kept from the `make` of a service that is hearing it, and either way
has taken the commit in first. One taken off an index that hadn't would hold the commit's file with the
commit before's edges.
TopologyTests' Snapshots suite holds a snapshot to the index on every question, over a seeded run of
every kind of commit, switch and undo, and a snapshot taken a step before to its old answers.

### What it costs

- **As the editor opens**, every board it can show is read (the root, then down through the owners
  of boards it can show, as `canShow` has it: `registry.ownsShowableBoard`), each record's sources
  asked; a kind with none costs a lookup. Each stand-in's rule is asked as it's read; once every
  board is, what each stand-in stands for is worked out, and only the carriers at those whose
  shapes changed are set a second time, so a file with no stand-ins costs what it did. A file or a board put in place (`replaceFile`,
  `replaceDocument`) is read again, and only the carriers whose edges changed touch anything.
- **Each commit** costs what it changed: the records it removed, touched on other boards
  (`ChangeSet.elsewhere`: the boards a deletion took or a paste brought, a write to a board that
  isn't shown), added, or changed other than by moving, each read again from the file as it is now
  (a shape on no board the editor can show carries nothing). Then, where there are stand-ins: what
  each stand-in it read, and each whose record names a shape it read, stands for is worked out
  again (O(the shapes they name)), and only the carriers with an edge at a stand-in whose shapes
  changed are set again (O(that stand-in's edges)). A move reads nothing: no source, rule or
  admission may read where a box is. Undo and redo are commits like any
  other. Showing another board reads nothing: the index is the file's (`boardDidChange` does
  nothing but for a file put in place).
- **Heard first.** A service that reads the index as it hears a commit finds it up to date,
  wherever the two are in the list: looking it up (`editor.topology`) has it hear the commit first,
  and so does a reference kept from a service's `make`, since what a service looked up as it was
  made takes each change in before it ([services hear a change](#services-hear-a-change)): MentionState
  and the relationship index keep theirs. The shipped list has `TopologyPlugin()` right after
  `SelectionPlugin()`.
- **A provide** costs what it changes: the answered stand-ins' rule worked out, and the carriers
  at those whose shapes changed set again, each edge diffed and filed under up to four ends and its
  type (an arrow into a stand-in for 50 is 50 edges; the per-carrier cap holds one between two to
  256).
- **Held.** `./build.sh bench`: Topology's index and Mentions' catalog of 10,000 shapes, built as
  the file opens, within 50 ms (the budget Mentions' own index had); `neighbors(of:)` of a shape
  with 100 edges within 1 ms; and a drag's input, a subboard of 10,000 deleted in a frame, and its
  undo in 100 ms, with Topology hearing them. With stand-ins (`StandInBenchmarks.swift`, the bench's
  own kinds, so a budget holds the mechanism whatever kind stands in): the index opening with 100 of them and 1,000 arrows
  into them within the same 50 ms, what's connected through 100 within 1 ms, re-pointing one with
  100 arrows within 1 ms, a drag of 50 costing a drag event nothing more, a commit while a query
  holds the file among 500 within `queryHeldCommit`, and a provide that fans out (`provideFanOut`). `recordsRead` (debug builds) counts the records
  sources read, so tests hold a commit to what it changed.

Every plugin list with a plugin that contributes to Topology's points (Ports, Mentions) needs
`TopologyPlugin()`, as one with Selection needs `KeyboardPlugin()`: a contribution to a point whose
owner isn't installed is `ownerNotInstalled`.

### What it doesn't do

- **Loose edges.** An arrow with a free end isn't an edge; there's no query for connections
  half-made.
- **Spatial relations.** A shape that happens to lie within another's bounds isn't inside it;
  that's geometry (`editor.paintOrder(in:)`, `shapeContext.bounds(of:)`). What's in a frame is what
  it holds, which the core's in-or-out rule keeps within it, not what its bounds cover (a locked
  shape a frame grows over stays out).
- **Drawing by type.** Agents read the graph with [`canvas query`](#query), through a snapshot
  (`:edge-to`, `:downstream-of`, `"Payments" *`), but `canvas draw` matches an edge it restates by
  its ends, not by its type.
- **Showing it.** Only the ways a light is given for are shown ([Neighbors](#neighbors): outlined on
  hover, listed in a shape's Connections tab, with what it's inside and what it holds); a type of edge no
  plugin gives a light isn't.

## Queries

Queries ([`Sources/Queries`](../Sources/Queries)) finds the shapes of a file a query matches: a
selector in a CSS-like language over every shape on every board the app can show, by kind, title,
id, attributes typed by their kind's schema, text, Topology's containment and typed edges, and the
words plugins add. It's an engine on Selection and Topology, over the core and QueryLanguage
(FuzzyMatching lends it its "did you mean", `Suggestions`), knows no horizontal's meaning, and hears no
commit: the engine every plugin may run, where the language agents write is `canvas query` and the
words their owners give it. Agents ask through [`canvas query`](#query); any plugin may ask too (a
word for a horizontal's meaning comes from the horizontal's own module):

```swift
guard let queries = editor.queries else { return }                 // nil without QueriesPlugin
let result = try await queries.run(QueryRequest(#""Payments" sticky-note:mentions("Auth")"#, limit: 20))
result.count                                                        // every shape that matches, listed or not
result.rows                                                         // the first 20, in file order
```

The language, every form, word and refusal, is taught to agents by the canvas skill
([`reference/query.md`](../.claude/skills/canvas/reference/query.md), whose every block SkillTests
runs on a file of its own, so it can't drift from the app). What a plugin needs of it:

- **A query** is a list of selectors, commas between them, each of compounds joined by a space
  (inside, at any depth) or `>` (directly inside: in a container, or on an owner's board in no
  container); a compound is at most one head (a kind, `*`, a title in quotes, a kind with a title
  right after it, `sticky-note"Checkout"`, as CSS writes
  `div#id`, or `#` and an id) and then tests with no space between them, attributes in brackets
  and `:word`s: `"Payments" sticky-note[text*="retry" i]:mentions("Auth")`. A selector answers with
  the shapes its last compound matches, as in CSS, and a list with those any of its selectors does,
  each once.
- **QueryLanguage** ([`Sources/QueryLanguage`](../Sources/QueryLanguage)), a core module that
  knows no canvas, registry or plugin, reads it: `SelectorList(parsing:)`, a tree whose every part
  knows its place in the text (`QuerySpan`, in characters of the query as sent), and `canonical`,
  the one form it prints (its own words in lowercase, titles in double quotes, one space around `>`,
  no comments), which is what an answer says ran. It refuses what the text alone shows
  (`empty_query`, `syntax`, `stray_space`, `too_long`, `too_complex`, `unsupported` (also `.Name`,
  hinted toward a plugin's word through a `HintPremise` claim, `typeWord`), `not_built` for the
  words people invent that are planned, `not_an_id`, and `bad_argument` for its own words),
  stopping at the first, and knows only its own words (`Word`: `:not`,
  `:is`, `:where`, `:has`, `:inside`, `:top-level`, `:current-board`, the edge words, `:dangling`,
  `:contains`); another's argument it keeps as text for the engine to read as shapes
  (`SelectorList(argumentOf:)`, its spans in the whole query), or to refuse with the rewrite for a
  word people invent (`KnownInventions`: `:parent-of`, `:near`, `:source-of`, and `:neighbor-of`,
  the language's old name for `:connected-to`). `QueryLimits` bounds it: 8,192 characters, 1,024
  in a string, 32 levels of parentheses, 256 compounds, 20 problems said.
- **Queries resolves it** against what this app has (`queries.check(_:)`, into a `QueryPlan`,
  `Sendable`, whose `description` prints it as a tree), refusing what isn't there with the one like
  it (`unknown_kind`, `unknown_attribute`, `unknown_pseudo_class`, `unknown_edge_type`,
  `invalid_value`, `unsupported_operator`, `cannot_contain`, `no_names`; `not_built` for an
  attribute that holds a place and `=` on an object; and the words people write in brackets,
  `[kind=…]`, `[id=…]`, `[board=…]`, with what to write, and `[class=…]`, `unsupported` as `.Name`
  is), every problem that doesn't hang on another
  at once, in the query's order; and answers it, refusing a title or an id no shape has
  (`unknown_title`, `unknown_id`) rather than answering none. Nothing unknown is passed over: a
  query that runs asked what it says, and a hint is most often the query to write instead. A hint
  that is a query is never one the app would refuse for a reason the query it mends didn't have:
  one that takes for granted what only the app can say (that a title is some shape's, that a
  kind's shapes can have titles, that what it puts where a container goes holds shapes) waits for
  it (`HintPremise`, QueryLanguage's, settled by the kinds and ids as the query resolves and by the
  titles as it's answered: `#Checkout` hints `"Checkout"` only where a shape is titled so).
  A plan says three things about itself, for a plugin that keeps an answer past the moment it was
  asked: `editorWords`, the words in it whose verdict reads the editor (`:selected`, `:invalid`,
  `:current-board`, a text read through a format that reads the editor), `readsOnlyTheFile` (none does: what
  it matches is a function of the file as the query takes it up, whoever asks, whatever they have
  selected or shown), and `readsEdges` (it has an edge word, so the edge view and a wait for answers
  still arriving matter to it).

### What a query sees

- **Every shape on every board the app can show** (`canShow`'s), none kept aside: a kept-aside
  shape has no properties to read and carries no edges, and a board the app can't show is the
  file's, not the app's. `#` with such a shape's id is refused `unknown_id`, saying which it is.
- **File order**, for every answer: the root's shapes in no container, back to front, each
  container followed at once by what it holds and each shape that owns a board by that board's
  shapes, all the way down, the order Topology's snapshot walks in (`forEachShape(inFileOrder:)`, or
  `fileOrderKey(of:)` for a few shapes), so the engine never walks boards or containers itself. The
  same query on the same file answers in the same order. Both are Topology's, so without
  `TopologyPlugin` every query is `no_topology`.
- **One instant, but for what only the main actor knows.** An answer is the file as it was when the
  app took up the query, but for titles a shape works out from what it holds (a derived title) and
  validity (`:invalid`, `:warned`), which are as the app has them when the query asks: a shape a
  commit changed while the query ran can answer with its newer title or verdict, never an older one,
  and one gone since has no title and fails the word. So no main-actor code is ever handed a record
  the app has since replaced, and no plugin's cache keeps one. The board shown (`:current-board`) and
  what's selected (`:selected`) are as they were when it started.
- **Titles through the names point** (Titles', through its `TitleQueriesPlugin`). A head
  `"Checkout"` is every shape whose title, folded as Titles folds one, is the literal folded, case
  and all, named or derived; several shapes may share it, and it names them all. A title no shape
  has is refused, so a no always means the shape is there: `[title="X"]`, which folds its literal
  the same way, is how to ask whether one is, its count of 0 an answer (warned `no_title_match`).
  A kind with a title right after it, `sticky-note"Checkout"`, is the kind's shapes with that
  title: a title head beside the kind's (the title's node first, as it finds its shapes), so a
  title no shape has is refused as `"Checkout"` is, one only other kinds have answers none, and a
  kind whose shapes have no titles is `unknown_attribute`, as `[title=…]` on it is. With a space
  between, the title is inside the kind's shapes, and where they hold no board the refusal
  (`cannot_contain`) hints the two together, if they can have titles. Without a names point, a
  title is `no_names`.
- **Attributes through the kinds' schemas** (`registry.schema(for:)`, read with
  [`KindSchema`](#a-kinds-schema)): every property, own or added, but those that hold a place (where
  a shape is isn't in the language yet: `frame`, `not_built`), and the names point's word (`title`),
  read through the names point, so a derived title is an attribute too, on the kinds whose shapes
  have titles. A literal is read by its property's schema as `draw` reads a value, and the test is
  typed by it: a number numerically (`[rank=3]` and `[rank="3"]` alike; one that isn't finite
  matches no number test), a date-time by its UTC day (`[due<2026-10-01]`) or instant, a choice from
  its list (`i`: in any case), a list by its items (`~=`), text as text (`^=`, `$=`, `*=`, `|=`, and
  `i` for any case; `<` refused). An absent true|false is its schema's default, else false
  (`[locked=false]` is every unlocked shape); `[a]` is a value that says something (true, text, a
  list or an object not empty, a number or a date there); `[a=""]` on text (mention text, a choice,
  a date, the names point's word too) is no value, absent or empty (`sticky-note[title=""]` is the
  untitled notes, since a blank title is none; `arrow[channel=""]` a plain arrow), and elsewhere
  `""` is what it always was; `[a!=v]` is `:not([a=v])`; and any other test of an absent value is
  false. With no kind named, a test applies to the kinds that have the attribute, each reading the
  literal its own way. `=` on an object is `not_built`, and a shape's metadata (`ShapeMeta`) is
  never an attribute.
- **Members inside an attribute: `[a.b.c]`.** `AttributeTest.path` holds the identifier members
  after the attribute's name (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-` and `_`; a quoted name has
  none), and the printer writes them bare, `[meta.owner=Ann i]`. Only an attribute whose schema is an
  object or any JSON has members (any other is `unknown_attribute`: "note is text, so it has no
  members"), and the test is **untyped**: an object's members are whatever the shape holds, so each
  test is typed by the JSON value found at the path, shape by shape (`PathTest`, a `.path`
  comparison). A string takes the text operators, `=` and `i`, and `~=` as a word; a number takes `=`
  and the orderings when the literal reads as a decimal number (`[a.b="30"]` is `[a.b=30]`; an
  ordering with a literal that isn't one is `invalid_value`, and the `i` flag on it
  `unsupported_operator`); a boolean takes `true` or `false`; an array takes `~=` for an item; any
  other sort of value matches nothing (`[a.b^=3]` on a number). A member that is missing, null, or
  inside something that isn't an object is no value: `[a.b]` is false, `[a.b=""]` true, and `!=`
  is the `:not` of the test, as everywhere. Typing by the schemas of a shape's types is left for
  later: it would make the vocabulary depend on the file, which today is built once from the
  registry and is `Sendable`.
- **Text as a person reads it.** A string whose schema names a media type a text format reads
  (`contentMediaType`) is tested and shown as that format makes it: mention text as plain text, each
  mention `@` and the name its target has now, or the name it holds while its target is gone, never
  the stored form with its ids. `:contains("x")` is a substring of the title or of any string in the
  attributes, as they read, in any case: a filter, not search.
- **Containment, Topology's one tree.** A space and `:inside()` are inside at any depth, through
  boards and [containers](#containers) on them alike; `>` and `:has(> …)` directly inside, a
  container's own shapes, or the shapes on an owner's board in no container (a shape in a frame on a
  subboard's board is the frame's child, not the subboard's); `:top-level` is inside nothing (on the
  top board, in no container), and `:current-board` on the board shown, in a container or not. A
  kind whose shapes hold shapes, a board of them or shapes on theirs (`containerKinds`), may stand
  where a container goes; any other is `cannot_contain`.
- **What a shape is inside, named.** A row's `inside` is the names of the shapes it's inside,
  outermost first: the boards' owners as the path over the canvas names them (the owner's title,
  else its kind's placeholder, through the board names point, else its label), and the containers
  between them by their titles, else their kinds' labels (an untitled frame is "Frame"), which the
  path doesn't name.
- **A query changes nothing**: no shape, no selection, no step of undo. It never ends typing: a
  shape being typed into reads as the board has it (a note writes each keystroke, so its text as
  typed so far), and an answer that lists it, or read its text, warns that it may still change
  (`editing`).

`run(QueryRequest(text, limit:, countOnly:, properties:, edges:, settle:))` (the last two are
[below](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)) answers a `QueryResult`: `query` (the
plan's `canonical`), `count` (every shape that matches, listed or not), `rows` (the first `limit`,
`QueryBudget.rows` (100) unless it says, at most `maxRows` (10,000), in file order; none with
`countOnly`), `warnings` (`limited`, `editing`, `no_title_match`, `pending`; `QueryWarning.Reason` is open,
and the command line adds `repaired`), `shown` and `shownPath` (the board the window showed as it
took up the file, `:current-board`'s, and the boards from the root down to it: where it ran, which
the command line's `board` says), and `timings` (thread CPU on the main actor and off it, the
slices, the longest, and the costliest record: the longest stretch between two reads of a slice's
clock, the stretch after its last read included). A `QueryRow` is the shape's `id`, `kind`,
`title` (nil for none), `board`, `inside`, `properties` (its attributes as they read: own properties
as a board writes them, added ones when set, text through its format, cut at `QueryBudget.cut` (500)
characters unless `.only([…])` names it, those cut named in `cut`; never where it is, nor its name;
none for `.none`), `connection`, for a shape that carries an edge itself in slot `""` (an arrow: the
edge's type and the shapes it runs `from` and `to`, each by id and title; and, only when an end went
through a stand-in, `via` and `more`, [below](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)), and `editing`; it
encodes itself leaving out what's absent. `titles(for:limit:)` and `whereThePersonIs(selectedLimit:)` are
what [`--ask`](#--ask) sends the model, each run as a query is.

### Where it runs

A query costs the main actor what it reads and one turn, and does everything else off it:

1. **Checked**, on the main actor (`check`): parsed and resolved against the vocabulary
   (`queries.vocabulary`, a `QueryVocabulary`, `Sendable`: each kind with its label, how its shapes
   are named, whether its shapes hold shapes (`holdsShapes`, Topology's `containerKinds`) and
   whether a board of them (`holdsBoard`), what an untitled one's board is called, and its
   attributes with what each takes; the edge types in the tree's order, with their summaries; the
   words, the language's then plugins', each with its form, what it takes, what it means and an
   example; and `text`, the `<vocabulary>` block `--ask` sends: the kinds, the edge types and the
   plugins' words, since the prompt teaches the language's own), made on the editor's first query
   and kept, since the registry never changes.
2. **Taken up**, in one main-actor turn, in O(1) (`QuerySnapshot`): the file
   (`withoutObservingDocument { editor.file }`) and Topology's snapshot in the edge view the request
   names (`topology.snapshot(request.edges)`), shared and not copied; the
   board shown and the path to it; the revision and the shape being typed into; then what each word
   and text format the query uses takes (`prepare`, in word order: the selection's ids, Mentions'
   labels), every text format's when rows list attributes.
3. **Answered off the main actor**, in a task of its own (`Evaluation`), handed the snapshot whole
   (`Handover`), so the evaluation is its last holder and it's freed there, with everything read from
   it. A set at a time: each node of the plan is worked out once into the set of shapes it matches
   among the candidates its compound has narrowed to so far, and kept for the query, so nothing
   recurses per shape; a compound's tests run cheapest first (ids, titles and seeds; kinds; the top
   board and the board shown; containment and edges; attributes and text; words asked of the main
   actor last, on what's left).
   A compound with a one-step edge word (`:edge-to`, `:edge-from`, `:connected-to`, `:starts-at`,
   `:ends-at`, `:start-of`, `:end-of`, `:between`, a plugin's relation) and fewer than
   `QueryBudget.seedFromAnchors` (1,024) anchors starts from their edges' far ends, never a walk of
   every shape: `sticky-note:edge-to(#…)` costs the anchor's degree, and `:end-of(#…)` the edges the
   anchor carries. Containment walks up from each candidate (its ancestors: those of the
   container it's in, from its record, `container(of:on:)`, else its board's, each container's and
   each board's worked out once), or, when nothing narrowed the candidates, down from the
   containers, asking only the shapes of `containerKinds` what's inside them; transitive words go
   breadth first from their anchors.
   Titles and ids are checked here, against the snapshot (`unknown_title` with the titles like it,
   and, for a title standing for an edge word's or a relation's anchor where an edge of the types it
   follows points at a shape the query can't see from a carrier it can, the `:dangling` that finds
   those carriers, of exactly those types: `:mentions("Old ledger")` hints `:dangling(mention)`;
   `unknown_id`, `cannot_contain` for a title that names only shapes of kinds that hold none). The
   rows are made here too, in file order: the walk's, when every shape was walked, else
   `fileOrderKey`'s; a count isn't put in order at all.
4. **Asked of the main actor in slices**, for what only it can say: a derived name (the names point's
   `derived`) and a word's verdict (its `onMain`). `MainFacts` asks them in slices, each a
   main-actor job of its own that lasts `QueryBudget.slice` (2 ms of the thread's CPU) and at most the
   one record that crosses it, one record at least: its clock is read after the first record, then
   every `clockStride` (16) while the pace leaves room before `everyRecordAfter` (1.5 ms), and after
   every record from then on. The evaluation asks for the next slice only once it has the last one's
   answers, so a query never has more than one waiting on the main queue, and input, drawing,
   commits and other queries' slices run between them (the main run loop services its sources
   between one job and the next).
   Each shape is asked about as the app has it when its slice runs: its id looked up in the live
   file, with the board it's on now (`QueryMainContext.shape(_:)`); one gone since, kept aside, or on
   a board the app can't show has no name and fails the word.
5. **Written** as the wire's JSON member by member, off the main actor too, where the result is let
   go of ([query](#query)).

**At once, and bounded.** Queries on one editor run at once: each takes up the file as soon as it's
asked (`--ask`'s titles and where the person is too, and a batch) and is answered alongside the
others, a snapshot of its own for each, with no line to wait in. Each asks the main actor for one
slice at a time, so several queries' slices alternate on the main queue, with the run loop's sources
between one job and the next. A query stops when its caller's task is cancelled (`cancelled`: the
evaluation looks every `QueryBudget.cancellationStride` (256) shapes and before each slice, and
`canvas` hanging up cancels the command's task) or when `QueryBudget.deadline` (8 s, before
`canvas`'s 10 s wait runs out) has passed since it was asked, running or waiting for answers to
settle (`too_slow`: a scheduled action on `editor.scheduler`, armed before the settle wait so the
wait counts against it, cancels it, and is cancelled if the query ends first, so tests reach it by
advancing a `ManualScheduler`), either stopping that query alone, since each has its own task, its
own deadline and its own slices. Every query on an editor stops when the editor goes
(`board_closed`: `QueryState` and `MainFacts` hold the editor weakly, so a query never keeps a closed
file's editor alive).

**Zero upkeep.** `QueryState` keeps nothing per shape or per board, implements no
`documentDidChange`, and overrides `boardDidChange` with nothing: a commit, a drag event's included,
and a switch of board cost queries nothing, ever, and nothing outlives a query but the vocabulary
(`liveSnapshots`, debug builds, is 0 whenever none runs).

**What a held snapshot costs.** While a query runs, its snapshot shares the file's tables and
Topology's, so a commit that lands meanwhile copies each table it changes, once: a drag event the
file's `revisions` (and, off the root, its `children`), a shape added or removed its `locations`, a
change of edges the index's tables it touches, a rename of a mentioned shape Mentions' resolutions
(while a text format holds the labels). At most one copy per table however many snapshots are held
(copy on write: the commit's first change to a table copies it, and every snapshot taken before it
keeps the old one), so queries at once cost a commit no more than one does, and none once the
answers are made, since each snapshot is let go of then; `./build.sh bench` can't tell a commit with
a snapshot held from one without (below).

### Many at once, edge views and waiting

Three additions are for plugins that keep answers and for agents that read what a stand-in makes of
the edges ([stand-ins](#stand-ins-forwarding), Topology's). All are generic: nothing here names what stands in.

- **The edge view.** `QueryRequest.edges` (an `EdgeView`, `.resolved` unless it says: every caller
  that never said keeps reading as it did) is the view of Topology's edges the query's edge words
  see: `:edge-to`, `:connected-to`, `:downstream-of`, `:between`, `:ends-at`, `:end-of`, a relation,
  and a row's `connection`. Resolved, an arrow into a stand-in is an arrow into what it stands for;
  `.recorded` forwards only through stand-ins whose own record names what they stand for and leaves
  one that stands for what was provided at its own end, which is what a stand-in's own query reads
  (it asks what to stand for, so it can't see through itself); `.literal` is as drawn. Taking up the
  file is `topology.snapshot(request.edges)`; evaluation is unchanged, the snapshot answers in the
  view it was taken in.
- **A connection that went through a stand-in** says so. In the resolved view an arrow into a
  stand-in has one edge for each shape it stands for, and a row reads them: `from` and `to` are the
  first pair in file order (by where each starts, then where each ends), `QueryConnection.via` (a
  `QueryVia`, `{from, to}`, each only if that end was a stand-in) says which stand-in each end went
  through (`Edge.origin`), and `more` (`[QueryPair]`) holds the other pairs, in file order. Both are
  nil for a connection as drawn, so a row's JSON is what it was but for these members; `canvas
  query` writes them member by member (`QueryOutput`), a stand-in untitled, so its end is its id
  alone. An arrow into a stand-in that stands for nothing yet stays at the stand-in, as drawn.
- **A batch, ids only.** `queries.matches([QueryMatchRequest])` answers many queries
  (`text`, `edges`, `limit`, `admitting`, `holdingBack`) in one go and returns, in order, each one's
  `Result<QueryMatches, QueryError>`: `canonical`, `ids` (the admitted matches in file order, at
  most `limit`), `count` (all admitted), `heldBack` (of the matches `admitting` turned away, how many
  `holdingBack` takes: what a step of the caller's could admit, so it can say what it left out; 0
  without one) and `revision` (`editor.revision` as the file was taken up, the same for all). The file is taken up once, in one main-actor turn, with one snapshot of
  Topology in each view the requests ask for, and every request is evaluated in one evaluation that
  shares what it reads: the shapes walked, the title index, and the names, so a derived name (asked
  of the main actor in slices) is read **once per batch**, however many requests name titles. Each
  text is checked once however many requests carry it, a query asked in two views among them (debug
  builds count `checks`), over the edge types read once.
  `admitting` is asked of each match off the main actor, before `limit`: the first match is the
  first one admitted, and `count` counts those; `holdingBack`, of each it turned away. No rows are built. A request the engine refuses
  (`check`, then the names pass) is that request's `.failure`, with the reason and message `run`
  would give (a hint that waits on titles is left as it is); a cancellation, the deadline or a
  closed file fails every request that wasn't refused. `checkNames(plan)` is the names pass alone
  (`unknown_title`, `unknown_id`, `cannot_contain`: what `run` does before it evaluates), with
  nothing evaluated and no rows, and takes up nothing for a plan that names no shape: what a plugin
  that translates English to a query checks, beside `check`, before it keeps one.
- **What a word reads** (`QueryReads`, `.file` or `.editor`) is said when it's added, and a plan
  reports it (above). `registrar.queryPseudoClass(…, reads: .file, prepare:, seeds:, matches:)`
  and `queryTextFormat(…, reads: .file, prepare:, read:)` take a `prepare` that is given a
  `QueryFilePreparation`: Topology's snapshot, whose edges are in the request's view, and the
  registry, and no editor; and no `onMain` (its context lends the editor). So the claim "this word
  reads only the file" can't be false by accident: code that reads the live editor, the selection,
  the camera, a service or Validation doesn't compile there. A word added the other way, with a
  `prepare` that takes `QueryPreparation`, reads the editor, as every word did; a relation reads
  the file. What a plugin keeps that is a function of the records alone reaches a file word
  through a **fact of the file**: a type that adopts `QueryFileFact` (`static func current(in
  editor:) -> Self`, `Sendable`, asked on the main actor in the turn the query takes up the file,
  O(1): a value the plugin keeps, shared) is read with `preparation.fact(MyFact.self)`. The word
  still can't reach the editor; the claim that the value reads only the records is made once,
  where the fact type is declared, and reviewed there. Shipped, the words' owners classify each:
  `:selected`, `:invalid` and `:warned` read the editor, as does `:current-board` (the board
  shown, the language's own); Mentions' text format reads the file, through the fact
  `MentionedNames` (`MentionState.labels`: each mentioned shape's name, from its record), so a
  query that searches note text (`[text*=…]`, `:contains`) reads only the file and a stand-in's
  own query may use it. The structural words, attributes, kinds, titles, text and the edge words,
  relations included, read the file.
- **Settling.** `QueryRequest.settle` (a `Duration`, nil: don't wait) makes a query that reads edges
  wait, before it takes up the file, while `topology.isSettling` (answers a stand-in asked for are
  still arriving), at most that long (`QueryBudget.settleWait`, 2 s, what `canvas query` passes,
  `--ask`'s query too). The wait holds no snapshot, and no other query waits for it; a plan with no
  edge word never waits. It counts against `QueryBudget.deadline` (armed before the wait, so the
  evaluation has what's left), which keeps a slow query inside `canvas`'s 10 s: it's refused
  `too_slow`, with its hint, not left to the client's timeout. If the time passes with answers
  still arriving the query runs anyway and adds `QueryWarning.pending(n)` (reason `pending`; `n` the
  stand-ins asked and unanswered), saying that what it reads of edges may change. An agent that
  draws and then queries reads the settled graph, or is told it didn't.

### What plugins add

Queries knows no horizontal's meaning: what shapes are called, what an untitled owner's board is called, words
beyond the language's, how text of a media type reads, and what's selected come through points
Queries declares ([QueryPoints.swift](../Sources/Queries/QueryPoints.swift)), which the modules
that own each meaning fill with this app's words, a plugin value for each (Queries' own for the
selection, Selection being below it; QueriesTests fill them with words of their own). Without one,
a query does without:

| Point | Sugar | What a query gets | Without it | Shipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `QueryNames` | `registrar.queryNames(attribute:source:named:derived:fold:)` | The attribute names are tested by; per kind, whether its shapes are named, derived or neither; a named shape's name, read anywhere; a derived one's, on the main actor; how a title a query writes is folded | No titles: a title head is `no_names`, and rows have none | TitleQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryBoardNames` | `registrar.queryBoardNames(placeholder:)` | What an untitled owner's board is called, per kind | Its kind's label | BoardQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryWords` | `registrar.queryPseudoClass(_:_:example:prepare:seeds:matches:onMain:problems:)` (reads the editor; with `reads: .file` and a file-only `prepare`, no `onMain`), `querySelection(_:_:example:selected:)`, `queryRelation(_:_:example:types:direction:)`, `queryRelation(_:_:example:reads:transitive:namesTypes:prepare:seeds:related:)` | A word: a pseudo-class, the person's selection, a relation over edges of exactly some types, or a relation answered from a fact of the file | The word is `unknown_pseudo_class` | MentionQueriesPlugin, ValidationQueriesPlugin, TypeQueriesPlugin, SelectionQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryPathChecks` | `registrar.queryPathCheck(attribute:_:)` | What the members of an object attribute can be: the first member of a path a query tests that no shape of the file can hold (`[fieldValues.stauts]`), asked on the main actor, once a path | No warning | TypeQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryAskFacts` | `registrar.queryAskFact(tag:_:)` | A block `--ask` sends about the file after the titles, under its tag: made on the main actor from the editor and the question, bounded by its plugin; a tag is a word and none of the request's own (`AskFacts.reservedTags`) | No block | TypeQueriesPlugin (`fields`) |
| `QueryTextFormats` | `registrar.queryTextFormat(mediaType:describes:prepare:read:)` (and with `reads: .file`) | How strings of a `contentMediaType` read, anywhere | Text read as stored | MentionQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryEngines` | none: `QueriesPlugin`'s mark, which only Queries makes | That the app answers queries (`registry.answersQueries`), for what has a registry and no editor | `canvas query` and `query-vocabulary` answer `no_queries` | QueriesPlugin |

`QueryNames` and `QueryBoardNames` take one contribution each, `QueryWords` one a word,
`QueryPathChecks` one an attribute, `QueryAskFacts` one a tag and `QueryTextFormats` one a media type (their report lines: `query names`, `query board names`, `query
word :mentions`, `query path fieldValues`, `ask fact fields`, `query text text/x-canvas-mentions`; `query engine` on queries'). The five
registrations, whole (each plugin's words are its own nested `enum Word: String`, and
`ValidationQueriesPlugin` registers each of its three in a helper, whose `has` is below (`:incomplete`, "it still needs something", is a shape with an issue of the third level, whose rows' `problems` are those issues, `class` `needed`; any rule may say one, and Types' says a field its types need, or a Needed relationship row, left empty); `TypeQueriesPlugin` adds `:is-a(S)`, a transitive `namesTypes` relation over `TypeIndex.graph`, reads a type where `is` is read as its title, and `:misfit`, a `reads: .file` word over `RelationshipFacts` (the relationship graph, taken in O(1)) that is true of an arrow whose ends do not fit its relationship type, by the `fit` the check on an arrow calls, each end judged alone from the arrow's connection in the snapshot)
([TitleQueries.swift](../Sources/Titles/TitleQueries.swift),
[BoardQueries.swift](../Sources/Boards/BoardQueries.swift),
[MentionQueries.swift](../Sources/Mentions/MentionQueries.swift),
[ValidationQueries.swift](../Sources/Validation/ValidationQueries.swift),
[SelectionQueries.swift](../Sources/Queries/SelectionQueries.swift), and
[TypeQueries.swift](../Sources/Types/Engines/TypeQueries.swift)):

```swift
// TitleQueriesPlugin: a shape is called what Titles calls it; a named title read off the record anywhere,
// a derived one on the main actor.
registrar.queryNames(attribute: TitleProperty.key.rawValue,
                     source: { kind, registry in
                         if registry.titleIsDerived(kind) { return .derived }
                         return registry.properties(for: kind).contains(TitleProperty.key) ? .named : .none
                     },
                     named: { TitleProperty.folded($0[TitleProperty.self]) },
                     derived: { record, registry in registry.title(of: record) },
                     fold: { TitleProperty.folded($0) })

// BoardQueriesPlugin: an untitled owner's board is called what the path calls it.
registrar.queryBoardNames { kind, registry in registry.boardPlaceholder(of: kind) }

// MentionQueriesPlugin: Topology's mention edges as two words, and mention text as a person reads it.
registrar.queryRelation(Word.mentions.rawValue, "its text mentions a shape S matches", example: #":mentions("Checkout")"#,
                        types: [MentionEdge.id], direction: .outgoing)
registrar.queryRelation(Word.mentionedBy.rawValue, "a shape S matches mentions it", example: #":mentioned-by("API gateway")"#,
                        types: [MentionEdge.id], direction: .incoming)
registrar.queryTextFormat(mediaType: MentionTextFormat.mediaType, describes: "mentions read as @Name", reads: .file,
                          prepare: { $0.fact(MentionedNames.self).labels },
                          read: { stored, labels in MentionText(stored: stored).plainText { labels.label(of: $0) } })
// MentionedNames: QueryFileFact, `current(in:)` is `editor.mentions?.labels`, a function of the records.

// ValidationQueriesPlugin: :invalid, :warned and :incomplete, which only the main actor can say.
registrar.queryPseudoClass(word.rawValue, summary, example: ":\(word.rawValue)",
                           prepare: { _ in () },
                           matches: { _, _ in .onMain },
                           onMain: { record, board, _, context in has(severity, record, on: board, context) },
                           problems: problemClass.map { name in { record, board, _, context in /* each issue of the level as a ShapeProblem of class name */ } })

// SelectionQueriesPlugin: the person's selection, as the query takes up the file.
registrar.querySelection(Word.selected.rawValue, "the person has it selected", example: ":selected") { $0.selectedShapeIDs }
```

- **An edge names its ends**, so a kind draw can't name (no naming property, no derived title) has no edges to list: `PortEdgesPlugin`'s `sides` is empty for it, though the kind has ports (`registry.drawCanName`).
- **Names are titles.** A kind's shapes are `.named` when it opts into the title Titles keeps
  (`TitleProperty`), read off the record on any thread; `.derived` when Titles works them out (no
  shipped kind's), read through `registry.title(of:)` in slices, which
  wins for a kind that's both, since Titles falls back to it for the shapes nobody named and only
  the main actor can say which; else `.none`. `source` is asked once per kind, as the vocabulary is
  made. The attribute must be a word a query writes bare (`QueryNames.check`), and `[title="X"]`
  folds its literal through `fold`, so it matches exactly what the head `"X"` does. The rule is
  `draw`'s own (Titles' [`TitleNamesPlugin`](#what-draw-takes-from-other-plugins)), so the two name
  shapes alike.
- **Boards are named by Boards' rule**: the owner's name, else `placeholder` for its kind (asked once
  per kind), else its label (`registry.label(of:)`). `BoardQueriesPlugin`'s is `registry.boardPlaceholder(of:)`,
  which [`editor.name(of:)`](#boards) reads, so a row's `inside` says what the path's crumbs say.
- **A pseudo-class** (`:invalid`) takes no argument. `prepare` runs on the main actor in the turn the
  query takes up the file, taking what it needs there, O(1) or O(what it holds) (a set of ids, a
  service's value), and what it returns (any `Sendable`) is handed as it was to the rest: `seeds`, if
  given, the only shapes that can match, which a compound then starts from; `matches`, anywhere (on
  any thread, for several queries at once), `.yes`, `.no` or `.onMain` for each shape the query
  tests (a `QueryShape`: its record, its board and the Topology snapshot); and `onMain`, in slices,
  for those `matches` leaves to the main actor, about the shape as the app has it then, with a
  `QueryMainContext` (the registry, the editor, the revision as the query started, `shape(_:)`, and
  `shapes(on:)`, a board as the app has it now, one `ShapeContext` per board per query, made again
  once that board's revision changes); and `problems`, in slices of the rows a query returns alone
  (none for a count), what each row it matched has to answer for, a `ShapeProblem` (a field, where in
  its value, a class and a message) each, listed on the row as `problems` (`:invalid` gives each
  error, `:incomplete` each thing a shape still needs). A word is lowercase words joined by hyphens, and never one of
  the language's own or one it refuses as invented (`QueryWords.check`).
- **The person's selection** is a pseudo-class of one sort: `querySelection` takes the shapes
  selected, in the selection's order, as the query takes up the file (so a change of the selection
  while a query runs changes nothing it answers), seeds and matches them, and is what `--ask` tells
  the model is selected (`whereThePersonIs`), in that order. At most one plugin says what's
  selected (`QueryWords.check`).
- **A relation** (`:mentions(S)`) is `:edge-to(S, only t)` under a word of its own: `.outgoing`, the
  result has an edge of exactly one of `types` (none under them) to a shape S matches; `.incoming`,
  a shape S matches has one to the result. Its types must be ones an installed plugin declares.
  `MentionQueriesPlugin`'s follow `MentionEdge.id` alone, so a shape that mentions itself counts (Mentions'
  `isMentioned` leaves it out).
- **A relation from a fact of the file** (`queryRelation(…, reads: .file, transitive:, namesTypes:, argumentShapes:,
  prepare:, seeds:, related:)`) is for what a plugin keeps and edges don't say. `prepare` takes the
  fact (`file.fact(Facts.self)`, a `QueryFileFact`, O(1)); `related(shape, fact)` lists the shapes a
  shape is related to directly, and `seeds(fact)` every shape that has any (the only shapes that can
  match). `:word(S)` matches the shapes related to one S matches; `transitive` also those related
  through other shapes, however many. The engine reads `related` forward once per query and word,
  then works backward from the anchors, breadth first, each shape once: a cycle ends where it
  began, and a shape in one is related to itself. It reads only the file (`readsOnlyTheFile`), waits
  for answers still arriving as an edge word does (`readsEdges`: the fact may rest on edges), and
  with few anchors starts a compound as a one-step edge word does. A relation declared
  `namesTypes: true` (at most one) is the word `.Name` is refused toward (`argumentShapes:` says which shapes its argument names, the types: a hint calls a title a type only when a shape so titled is one of them): `unsupported`, hinted
  `:word("Name")` once a shape is titled so (the claim `HintPremise.Claim.typeWord`, settled with
  the titles), else the plain `:contains("Name")` hint, and a refusal that never says "class" or
  "schemas". `[class=Name]` is refused the same way.
  The same word is what a title given where an edge word takes edge types is hinted toward
  (`:edge-to("Bo", "Friendship")`, or the bare word): the parser's `bad_argument` (a comma after the
  shape starts edge types) and an `unknown_edge_type` carry the claim `HintPremise.Claim.titledArgument`
  (the edge word, its anchors as printed, the title), settled with the titles: a shape titled so, and
  no edge type of that name, make the hint `Friendship is a type, not an edge type: write
  :start-of(:is-a("Friendship"):ends-at("Bo"))` (`:edge-from`, `:connected-to`, `:starts-at`,
  `:ends-at` and `:between` each have their form; `:downstream-of`, `:upstream-of` and
  `:component-of` get a sentence that a relationship is one hop), else the refusal's own hint.
- **A text format** makes a stored string what a person reads, anywhere (`read`), with what `prepare`
  took; `describes` says so in the vocabulary, beside the attribute (`text (mentions read as
  @Name)`). Mention text reads through [`MentionState.labels`](#the-service-mentionstate), taken as
  the query takes up the file (a fact of the file, `MentionedNames`), so a gone target reads as the
  name its mention holds.
- **Validity is Validation's cache where it's current, else its rules.** `:invalid` and `:warned`
  leave every shape to the main actor (`.onMain`). There, a shape on the board shown, with nothing
  committed since the query started (`context.revision`), takes
  [`cachedResult(for:)`](#a-horizontal-plugin) while it's `.current`; any other runs its kind's rules
  against the board it's on as the app has it (`registry.validationIssues(of:in:
  context.shapes(on: board))`), which is what Validation will find once that board is shown. A
  query never makes Validation read a board, so Validation's first read (100 ms at 10,000 shapes,
  in one turn) is never a query's.

**What a plugin list needs.** `QueriesPlugin()` needs `TopologyPlugin()` (without it, every query
is `no_topology`). Each of the five plugins needs `QueriesPlugin()` (a contribution to a point
whose owner isn't installed is `ownerNotInstalled`) and its own concern's plugin:
`MentionQueriesPlugin` is refused without `MentionsPlugin()`, whose `mention` edge type its words
follow, while `TitleQueriesPlugin`, `ValidationQueriesPlugin` and `SelectionQueriesPlugin` find
nothing without Titles, Validation or Selection (every kind untitled, no shape invalid, nothing
selected), as `draw`'s words do without theirs. `QueryCommandsPlugin()` needs `AutomationPlugin()`,
and `--ask` `QueryTranslationPlugin` and `LanguageModelsPlugin` (else `no_model`). The shipped
list has them after draw's words: `QueriesPlugin(), QueryTranslationPlugin(),
TitleQueriesPlugin(), BoardQueriesPlugin(), MentionQueriesPlugin(), ValidationQueriesPlugin(),
SelectionQueriesPlugin()`, then `QueryCommandsPlugin()`; the prompt is a text file of the
product's (`Shipped/ask-prompt.txt`), since its examples name the shipped kinds.

### What it costs

`./build.sh bench` holds queries on generated boards of 1,000 and 10,000 shapes and files of nested
boards ([QueryBenchmarks.swift](../Tests/BenchmarkTests/QueryBenchmarks.swift), members of
`extension Budget`): main-actor budgets in the test thread's CPU, off-main ones in the answer's
`timings` (or, for what they don't cover, the answer's JSON and `--ask`'s request, every other
thread's CPU while it runs, `cpu {}`), and only the frames on the wall clock. In release, 1,000 /
10,000 shapes, ms (measured again 2026-10-09, the generated board's types are notes now,
longer notes that query, validation and Find read as notes):

| What | Budget | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| A query's main-actor time (`queryMain`): reading and resolving `sticky-note[text*="note" i]:not(:inside(*))` and taking up the file, also after a drag event that moved every shape | 0.2 / 0.5 | 0.067 / 0.071 |
| The vocabulary, made on an editor's first query (`queryVocabulary`) | 1 | 0.086 |
| That query off the main actor, first after the file opens, 100 rows: every shape walked, every note's attributes written and its text read with live names (`queryScan`) | 5 / 40 | 4.34 / 37.5 |
| A note by its name (`"Title 5004"`), every name read, off the main actor (`queryTitleOffMain`) | 1 / 5 | 0.57 / 3.20 |
| And on it: every derived name asked, in slices, on a board looked at (`queryTitleMain`) | 0.5 / 4 | 0.035 / 0.028, no slices: no shipped kind's names are derived |
| Notes with an edge to a subboard 100 of them mention, `:edge-to(#…)`, brief rows (`queryByID`) | 0.5 | 0.35 / 0.34 |
| And their rows with their attributes (`queryByIDRows`) | 2 | 0.52 / 0.53 |
| `:downstream-of` along a chain through every shape, and `:component-of(*)` over one component of them all (`queryGraph`) | 3 / 30 | 1.18, 1.27 / 9.42, 10.1 |
| Every construct that walks, and a nest as deep as the language allows, on a board and ten boards deep (`queryPathological`) | 25 / 250 | 3.8 / 45.7, the worst |
| `:invalid` over boards not shown, the main actor's time in all (`queryInvalidHidden`) | 15 / 150 | 8.48 in 5 slices / 88.1 in 44 (a type's schema checked too) |
| A slice: 2 ms and the record that crosses it, the longest of any query here (`querySlice`) | 3 | 2.068; the costliest record 0.400 |
| `* --limit 10000` off the main actor: the rows and their JSON, let go of there (`queryRows`) | 15 / 150 | 3.5 / 45.7 |
| That command's main time (`queryRowsMain`: `queryMain` and `queryTitleMain`) | 0.7 / 4.5 | 0.071 / 0.174 |
| Its main time beyond its query's own, making and letting go of the answer (`queryMain`) | 0.2 / 0.5 | 0.063 / 0.141 |
| A commit adding a note while a query holds the file, more than without (`queryHeldCommit`) | 0.1 / 0.5 | none: 0.049 held, 0.064 not / 0.265, 0.412 |
| A drag event's input with the shipped list and a query run first, more than without queries (`queryUpkeep`) | 0.01 | none: 0.0432 with, 0.0431 without / 0.2900, 0.2905 |
| A drag's frames at 60 Hz while `:invalid`'s slices run, the worst (`queryFrame`, wall clock) | 16 | 10.8 / 10.6, none dropped |
| `--ask`'s request without the model, on a board looked at: main (`askAssemblyMain`) | 1 / 5 | 0.105 / 0.115 |
| And off it (`askAssemblyOffMain`) | 3 / 10 | 0.587 / 4.74 |

- **No type is cold.** Types' index reads every type of a file as it opens, and every
  type as it changes, on any board, and a query reads only what's stored, never a type's schema. On a board never shown, as the file
  opens, `queryTitleMain` measures 0.024 / 0.027.
- **Rows of derived kinds cost the main actor their names.** 10,000 rows of the generated board
  hold none today (no shipped kind derives its title; its type notes are named), so the command is held to `queryMain`
  and `queryTitleMain` together, and what it costs beyond its query's own to `queryMain`: the answer
  is made and let go of off the main actor.
- **Mention text is read twice.** Mentions' text format parses each note's stored text again
  (`MentionText(stored:)`, some 6 µs a note) though the record holds it parsed: about half of a full
  row of a mentioning note, most of `queryScan`, and why full rows of 100 notes are held to 2 ms, not
  `queryByID`'s 0.5 ([Not built yet](#not-built-yet)).
- **Frames** are driven by a strict main-queue dispatch timer (`FrameDriver`), each timed from the
  first fire it answers, so a dropped frame counts as late: a run-loop `Timer` in a windowless
  process fires up to 7 ms late on its own. While slices run a frame starts at most one slice late
  (1.9 ms; 0.1 without), and the worst without queries is 9.0 / 9.3.
- **A held snapshot's copy** (the file's `locations`, some 10,000 entries at 10,000 shapes) is lost
  in a commit's own 0.36 ms; debug builds check that the query holds the file at the commit, so the
  case is real.

**No index, on purpose.** An index would cost every commit, a drag event's included (whose input is
held to 1 ms at 10,000 shapes), and a copy of what it indexes kept in step. What it would save is
small and off the main actor: walking every shape and filtering by kind is some 0.5 ms at 10,000;
named titles are a read per titled shape; derived ones their owners keep; edges and containment are
Topology's already. Attributes are written as JSON only for the candidates a test reaches, and text
read only for those a text test reaches. Should a budget miss on queries asked again and again, the
next step is a warm cache ([Not built yet](#not-built-yet)).

### What it doesn't do

- **Where shapes are.** Positions, sizes and overlaps aren't in the language (`:near`, `:left-of`,
  `:within`, and attributes that hold a place, are `not_built`), and inside is containment's (boards
  and containers on them): what's drawn within a shape's bounds isn't inside it unless it's in it
  (`cannot_contain`, for a container side that can only be kinds whose shapes hold no shapes).
- **`.Task` as a selector** (`unsupported`: a type is found by  the word a plugin gives it)  and `=` on
  a whole object (`[a.b]` tests a member).
- **Edges as answers.** A query lists shapes: a connection is asked for as its arrow
  (`arrow:starts-at("A"):ends-at("B")`, whose row's `connection` says where it runs), the shapes it
  runs from and to as `:start-of(arrow…)` and `:end-of(arrow…)` (the source and the target of each
  edge in slot `""` that a shape the anchor matches carries, of the types given, and only a shape the
  query ranges over: a mention's carrier, whose edges are in its text's slot, has none), and a
  mention as the shape whose text holds it.
- **Ranking and meaning.** `:contains` is a substring filter; ranked or semantic search would be a
  horizontal of its own.
- **CSS with no meaning here.** Shapes have no siblings, order or columns (`+`, `~`, `:nth-child`,
  `||`), no pseudo-elements, and a query sees no pointer (`:hover`): each is `unsupported`, never read
  some other way.
- **Acting on what it found.** A query selects, reveals and changes nothing. Its rows' ids name the
  shapes in a later query (`#…`), and in a `draw` script a shape that has no title; a script names
  every other shape by its title.

### Testing queries

- **QueryLanguageTests** hold the language on fixture words only (card, box, disc; rank, status,
  due; wire, hot-wire, pipe; the unknown words glows and stacked): trees and spans, the canonical
  form (a fixed point), every refusal (reason, message, hint, offset, length, line, column), the
  limits at their edges, the words and the inventions, and seeded fuzz: trees generated from the
  grammar round-trip, and random edits never crash, reprint as their canonical form when they parse,
  and keep every span inside the text.
- **QueriesTests** hold the engine over fixtures only: CanvasTesting's `Chore` (`ChoresPlugin`: kind
  `chore`, labelled "Task", holding every schema type, and the added `Flagged`, key `flag`), with
  pockets, tiles and links graded as wires; a `caption` names point, board names, words (`:starred`,
  seeded; `:heavy`, off the main actor, counted by `Tally`; `:audited`, asked on it, counted by
  `MainCalls`; `:wired-to(S)`, a relation) and a text format (`text/x-shout`), all in
  `queryPlugins`; `shelf()` and `hiddenShelf()` (a kept-aside owner, a board the app can't show);
  `yard()` (CanvasTesting's corrals, captioned, nested on the top board and on a pocket's board, one
  holding a pocket: every containment construct through them, from either side, file order, rows'
  `inside`, hints and `holdsShapes`);
  `choresHarness` (every schema type, every operator); `storyHarness` (the design's table of every
  construct, on fixtures: `citesPlugin`'s edges from chores' tags, `pickedPlugin`'s selection,
  `faultyPlugin`'s verdicts); and `wiresHarness` and `danglingHarness` (edges). `answer`, `matched`,
  `refusedAnswer` and `expectMatches` run queries through `awaitResult`, which turns the main run loop
  for the slices, and `plan(_:on:)` reads a plan (`description`, a tree).
- **Stand-ins, batches, reads and settling** are held on fixture stand-ins (StandIns.swift: a `Proxy`
  for the shapes its record cites, a `Lens` for what was provided, `relay()`, wires into them; Topology
  tests have their own): `edgeViewTests` (the three views on the same arrows, standing edges, a
  stand-in with nothing to stand for), `connectionViaTests` (`via` and `more`, in file order, per
  view), `matchesBatchTests` (one capture for all, no rows built, admission before the limit and off the
  main actor, the revision stamp, a refusal that is one request's, names read once for the batch
  by `derivedTitlesAsked`, each text checked once by `checks`, a view per request, cancellation, no
  waiting for a query before it), `checkNamesTests` (as `run`
  refuses, nothing evaluated, nothing taken up for a plan that names nothing), `readsTests`
  (`fileReadsPlugin`: a `reads: .file` word and text format given the snapshot and registry; `editorWords`
  in order and without repeats; `readsEdges`) and `settleTests` (a wait that ends on settling, one that
  ends on the time and warns `pending`, no wait for a plan with no edge word or no `settle`, the wait
  holding up no other query, cancelled waiting, the wait counting against the deadline), with `Working` as a source of busy work. QueryCommandsTests
  write a connection through a stand-in, and wait for answers on a `ManualScheduler`; CompositionTests'
  QueryShippedTests pin each shipped word's reads; BenchmarkTests' `referenceBatch`.
- **What runs where** is held by `QueryState`'s debug counters (`liveSnapshots`, `captures`, `checks`,
  `mainSlices`, `recordsEncoded`, `derivedTitlesAsked`, `verdictsAsked`, `universeWalks`,
  `seededFromAnchors`) and `threadsPlugin` (a name, a text format's `read` and a word's `matches`,
  each off the main thread). `SlowWord`, with `burn(_:)`, makes records cost what a test says: a
  slice's bound with a costly record, the costliest record's stretch after the last read, one slice
  queued at a time, a run-loop `Timer` firing between slices (the run loop's sources run between
  them, not only queue order), cancellation mid-slice, the deadline reached by `h.wait(8_000)` inside a
  slice on the `ManualScheduler`, queries at once (a quick query, and a batch, taking up the file and
  answering while a slow one is mid-slices, each over a snapshot of its own, `liveSnapshots` 2 while both
  are held; a cancelled one, or one out of time, stopping alone), and a closed file (an editor held only in
  a box a word empties). A word whose `prepare` commits lands a commit in the turn the query takes
  up the file: attributes are the capture's, a derived name the live record's. UpkeepTests hold zero
  upkeep.
- **The five owners' query tests** use fixtures only, through `EditorHarness` and `QueryState`:
  TitleQueriesTests CanvasTesting's kinds titled as TitleNamesTests title them (derived names
  asked on the main actor, and read live after a commit lands); BoardQueriesTests a `drawer`,
  which opens its board with a placeholder, and a `crate`, which doesn't and is called by its
  label, and titled corrals between them, which a row names and the path doesn't;
  MentionQueriesTests a `scribble` of mention text, titled pockets to mention, and a `strand` edge
  type its words ignore; ValidationQueriesTests card and tag rules that count their runs (the
  board shown answered from the cache, another board by its own rules in slices, and never
  Validation made to read a board); and SelectionQueriesTests a `:shifting` word that changes the
  selection mid-query. BoardQueriesTests and MentionQueriesTests name shapes with a names
  contribution of their own over `TitleProperty`, since they have no `TitleQueriesPlugin`.
- **QueryTranslationTests** hold the translator on fixture chores and a `ScriptedLanguageModel`: how
  an answer is read (`AskAnswer.parse`, ParseTests), what it answers and asked, each failure's reason
  and message (`QueryTranslationError`), no model or no queries, and the deadline in a model call;
  and `translate` (TranslateTests): the canonical query returned and nothing run, a wrong title and a
  word that reads the editor each repaired once (and refused twice an unusable answer), the 40 s mark,
  the 55 s deadline, a cancelled task, and the `.reference` request (no selection, no word that reads
  the editor, the rule line) against the `.person` one.
- **QueryCommandsTests** run `query`, `query-vocabulary` and `--ask` as the server does (`start`,
  `finish`, `run`, `answered`, `refused`) over chores, pockets and links, captions naming them,
  "Untitled Pocket" boards, and a `Desk`: `:picked`, the selection word, and `:slow`, asked on the
  main actor; with a `ScriptedLanguageModel` (`queue`, `holdsAnswers`, `requests`). The deadline and
  the repair mark are reached with `h.wait(…)` on the `ManualScheduler` (from inside `:slow` for a
  query run, from `onPicked` for the request's assembly), and `QueryOutput.lastBuiltOnMainThread`
  (debug builds) says where an answer was built.
- **CompositionTests** hold the shipped pieces on the story file, `QueryStory`: the design's "Roadmap"
  (a Payments subboard holding a Refunds one, notes that mention each other and a shape that's gone,
  arrows on a channel and on none, and types, one of them invalid), its ids
  `00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000NN` named by letter (`ids("C, Y")`), `fileOrder`, `file(in:)`,
  `harness(pasteboard:model:)` and `document(windowed:)`. Its untitled, invalid type V holds
  `{"type": "object" "title": "Invoice"}`, a comma left out (a type's name is its title, never
  its schema's, so V stays untitled); a type's last reading as an object is
  kept by id for the whole process, so a test that mends V's JSON changes what its highlights
  read in every story after it: mend a copy. QueryShippedTests run the design's table of every construct row for row
  (`StoryQuery.table`: shapes in file order, the count, the canonical form, each refusal's reason);
  QueryCommandLineTests run `canvas` as built against `CommandServer` on the story open in a
  `BoardDocument` (`configureQueryBoards(pasteboard:model:)`, `startQueryServer(for:)`, which holds the
  board weakly so a closed file's editor can be seen to go, and `RunningCanvas`, a `canvas` left
  running, a held `--ask`, while the test does something else: a `draw` answered meanwhile, a
  `--timeout` that lets go of the model's call, a file closed under it answered `board_closed` at
  once); BoardsTests `:current-board` across a switch (no change set worked out, no snapshot left);
  and SkillTests every `query` and `query-error` block ([Testing plugins](#testing-plugins)).
- **The prompt.** QueryPromptTests hold the prompt (`Shipped/ask-prompt.txt`) to the language: each of its
  `runnableExamples` answered on the story, each of its `illustrativeExamples` refused there with its
  reason, every query written after "→" listed, nothing that reads as a query left out of the lists,
  every `:word` the language's, a shipped plugin's or one the prompt says not to invent, the kinds,
  edge types and words it assumes the shipped vocabulary's, in its order, and the skill's
  `query-prompt.md` equal byte for byte; so a prompt change lists each new query-like example in one
  of the two lists. "Query eval board" holds `QueryEvalBoard` (59 shapes on six boards: look-alike
  titles, plain arrows, note and schema links, a mention two boards away) to what it's built with,
  "Query fields board" holds `QueryFieldsBoard` (two types, six notes with field values, links and
  a mention, one note incomplete and one wrong), and "Query prompt, live" checks each case of `scripts/query-prompts/cases.tsv` offline, its
  reference query finding exactly the shapes it expects; with `QUERY_LIVE=1` it asks the model
  ([`--ask`](#--ask)).
- **BenchmarkTests' Query benchmarks** are above; `cpu {}` sums a command's main-actor jobs without
  polling the run loop, and `FrameDriver` drives frames on a strict dispatch timer.

## Boards

A file holds a tree of boards: the root, and one for each shape of a kind that owns one (the core's
`BoardOwning`; [Boards in a file](#boards-in-a-file)). Boards
([`Sources/Boards`](../Sources/Boards)) is the horizontal that gets you around them, whatever kind
owns them. It builds on Selection (opening), ContextMenus (Open),
Keyboard (⌘↑), Titles (what a board is called), TableOfContents (the rows a crumb's menu lists),
and Find and Queries (the board names over Find's hits and in a query's rows), and none of them
learns what a board is.

A board-owning kind opts in with one line, on its own registrar
([OpensBoard.swift](../Sources/Boards/OpensBoard.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(SubboardDefinition()) { sub in                 // SubboardDefinition: BoardOwning
    sub.title(pill: false)                                        // Titles names its board
    sub.opensBoard(placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack")
}
```

or, for another plugin's kind, `registrar.opensBoard(Pocket.self, placeholder:systemImage:)`. The sugar
contributes to Boards' `BoardKinds` point (at most one per kind; its report line reads
`board → subboard "Untitled Subboard"`) and brings, in the same call:

- **Opening**: Selection's `opens("Open")`, which shows the shape's board
  (`editor.showBoard(BoardID(owner:))`), so a double-click, Return, Enter, ⌘↓ and Go › Open Selection all
  enter it ([opening a shape](#selection)), and so does its row in the table of contents: Return
  once the row is picked (in the app's panel, the canvas's Return, since picking a row shows the
  shape's panel and gives the canvas the keyboard), and a double-click only where the list stays
  put, not in the app's panel ([opening a row](#the-table-of-contents)).
- **Open** first in its context menu (`BoardsMenuGroup`, `.before(ShapeMenuGroup.self)`, as Finder's Open is): Selection's
  `.openSelection`, titled Open, so it shows ⌘↓ and does to the menu's shapes what ⌘↓ does: it opens
  one, goes into a group of them selected whole, and is left out for several. The Shape menu leaves it
  out, since Go › Open Selection runs the same command.

`BoardKinds.check` refuses a kind whose definition isn't `BoardOwning` (the form for another plugin's kind can't say so
in its types), and the point takes one kind at a time (`PointScope.kinds`), so the registry refuses
a contribution for every kind or for a scope: only a kind that owns boards has one to open. So
a plugin list with `opensBoard` in it needs Selection and ContextMenus installed.

`BoardsPlugin` itself ([Boards.swift](../Sources/Boards/Boards.swift)) is small:

```swift
registrar.service { BoardCrumbs(editor: $0) }                   // the path, kept for BoardPath
registrar.command(.enclosingBoard, title: BoardsStyle.enclosingBoard, menu: "Go", order: 10,
                  shortcut: KeyChord(KeyChord.upArrow.key, .command), runs: .whenIdle, menuTitle: { $0.enclosingTitle },
                  isEnabled: { $0.editor.selectionEnclosure != nil || !$0.editor.board.isRoot }) { $0.editor.goToEnclosing() }
registrar.command(.goUpBoard, title: BoardsStyle.enclosingBoard, runs: .whenIdle,      // the table of contents' way up
                  isEnabled: { !$0.editor.board.isRoot }) { $0.editor.goToEnclosingBoard() }
```

- **Going up.** ⌘↑ (and Go › Enclosing Board) runs `editor.goToEnclosing()`, one step out: if the
  selection is inside a group, the innermost one, selected whole, as Escape does; else, if the selected
  shapes are all in one container, that container, selected (Selection's `selectEnclosure()`, which
  brings it into view if it is not: [Moving between shapes](#moving-between-shapes)); else
  `editor.goToEnclosingBoard()`: the board above, with the shape whose board it left selected there.
  It's `editor.goUp(to: board)` for the parent: any board above the one shown (on `boardPath`), with the
  owner of the board below it on the path selected, as one step back
  (`showBoard(_:selecting:)`), so ⌘[ comes back down. Enabled while there is a group or a container to
  step out of, or off the root; never mid-press, and not while a shape is being edited, where ⌘↑ is
  the text's; on the root with neither, its key passes. The Go item is named for the step it would take
  (the command's `menuTitle`, which the window controller reads as it validates the item): Enclosing
  Group, "Enclosing " and what the container's kind is called (`registry.label(of:)`: Enclosing Frame),
  else Enclosing Board. `.goUpBoard` is the board step alone, whatever is selected, for a button
  that always means up a board: the table of contents' header.
- **Names.** `editor.name(of: board)` is what a board is called: its owner's title (Titles;
  a blank one is none), else its kind's placeholder, else its kind's label (`registry.label(of:)`);
  the root, which no shape owns, is called what the file is, else "Board". Only the window knows
  the file's name, so it's the core's to hold: `editor.rootName`, observed, empty until the host
  says (`nameRoot(_:)`, host API, which a board's window calls as it titles itself), and Boards
  reads it wherever it names the root. `editor.name(of:root:)` is the same with the root called
  what the caller says. `editor.symbol(of:)` is its kind's symbol (`opensBoard`'s,
  else its label's), nil for the root. The path, the table of contents' heading and Find's
  headings all read them. `registry.boardPlaceholder(of: kind)` is the placeholder a
  kind opens its boards with (nil for a kind that doesn't), the registry's alone, which both read,
  and so does a [query](#queries): its rows name the boards a shape is inside by the same rule,
  through Boards' `BoardQueriesPlugin` (BoardsTests' "A board's placeholder" holds it).
  `registry.containerName(of: record)` is what a shape that others are inside is called in a path of
  where a shape is, "Alpha › Beta" (a `ContainerName`: its `title`, else its `placeholder`, the
  board placeholder of its kind or, for a kind that opens no board, a frame, its kind's label):
  whatever writes such a path names each shape this way ([Jump To](#jump-to)'s rows, a
  [reference](#references)'s row in the table of contents), so they agree with one another and
  with the path over the canvas.
- **Over other plugins' lists.** Boards names a board wherever another plugin lists one, each
  from a plugin value of its own (a face), after `BoardsPlugin` and the list's plugin, so a list
  without that plugin leaves it out. `BoardContentsPlugin` (id `board-contents`) heads the table
  of contents (its `ContentsHeadings` point) with the
  board shown's crumb as a `ContentsHeading` with `up: .goUpBoard`, called Enclosing Board as
  the Go menu calls it, its tooltip the same, without a key (⌘↑ steps out of a group or a container
  first, so it is not always this button's step); on the root the file's name, as the
  window and the path's root crumb have it, else "Board". `BoardFindPlugin` (id `board-find`)
  heads each board's rows in [Find](#find)'s list (its `FindHeadings` point) with the board's name
  and symbol. Boards imports TableOfContents and Find for them.
- **In the window** ([the host's slots](#host-slots), which `BoardsPlugin` fills): the window's subtitle names the board
  shown, nothing on the root, where the title is the file's name (`registrar.windowSubtitle`,
  the last crumb's title, which the window
  controller reads observed, so it follows a switch or a rename);
  the path is over the top of the canvas (`registrar.hostOverlay(alignment: .top, coveredTop:)`
  with `BoardPath(editor:)`, the root's crumb the
  file's display name, which `BoardWindowController.synchronizeWindowTitleWithDocumentName` tells
  the editor); and the Go menu has Back (⌘[), Enclosing Board (named for its step: Enclosing Group,
  Enclosing Frame)
  (⌘↑) and Open Selection (⌘↓), sent to the board's window controller wherever the keyboard is, and dimmed
  while text has it, where the menu bar leaves those keys to the text (`MenuBar`: AppKit's menus
  take a disabled item's key and beep), so they move its caret. Jump To… (⌘K), JumpTo's, will follow
  them after a separator (the command `.jumpTo` is named; nothing claims it yet). The file opens on the board left
  open, with each board's camera as it was left (`BoardViewMemory`; below).

### The path

`BoardPath(editor:)` is where you are, as data-canvas shows it: a small capsule of
crumbs over the top middle of the canvas, root first, the board shown last, in a material pill 8
points below the canvas's top edge (`BoardsStyle`). The host places it over the whole canvas, with
`.overlay(alignment: .top)`, so a crumb's menu can stay inside it; only the pill and the menu take
clicks. It shows nothing on the root. `BoardPath.coveredHeight(on:)` is how far down it reaches on
a board (to the pill's bottom, about 35 points; none on the root), which the window tells the editor
(the path's overlay says it, `coveredTop`, and the window hands the most any view over the canvas
says to the editor's `coveredTop`), so a board's first visit, Zoom to
Fit and `reveal` fit shapes below it, where their titles' pills aren't under it.

```
        ╭────────────────────────────────────────────╮
        │  Plans  ›  …  ›  Kitchen 🔒 ›  **Pantry**  │
        ╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
                           ┌──────────────────────────┐
                           │ › ▤ Groceries            │  the pointer on Kitchen: its rows
                           │   ▤ Spices               │
                           │   ▭ Pantry               │  the way you came, highlighted
                           │   ▭ Fridge               │
                           └──────────────────────────┘
```

- The root's crumb is the file's name (`editor.rootName`; "Board" when that's empty), and follows
  a rename; the others are `name(of:)`. The
  board shown is bold and isn't a button. Each crumb is at most 180 points wide, truncated past it,
  with its name as its tooltip. The crumbs are separated by ›s, and nothing else marks them but the
  lock below (no caret for a crumb's menu, below: the owner found ⌄s beside the ›s busy).
- **A lock marks where the path turns read-only.** Each crumb says whether its board is read-only
  (`BoardCrumb.isReadOnly`: a [locked](#locking) subboard's board, and every board under it; the
  root's never is; from where the path turns read-only, `editor.readOnlyStart`, which the editor
  works out in one climb, as asking each board would cost the path's depth squared), and the path draws a small lock
  (`BoardsStyle.readOnlySymbol`, `lock.fill`, in the secondary color, 3 points after the name,
  "Read-only" as its tooltip and to assistive apps) after the name of the first crumb whose board is
  (`BoardCrumbs.readOnlyStart`), once: the boards below it are read-only too, and the lock above
  says it of them all, so none shows another. It's part of the crumb (a long name is cut short
  before it, and a click on it goes up, as the name's does). Folded into "…", it's the lock on that
  crumb's item in the menu, ahead of its name (an item's attributed title with the symbol after the
  name would put the symbol into its `title`), and a crumb below the fold has none: the menu never
  marks a crumb the first read-only one isn't.
- More than four crumbs fold the middle into "…", a menu of the boards it hides, root side first:
  root › … › parent › current (`BoardCrumbs.layout(rootName:)`). "…" is a button built as a board
  above's crumb is (borderless, in its gray and the pill's type), which shows an `NSMenu` of them
  lined up with its leading edge, starting at the pill's bottom edge, where a crumb's menu starts
  (AppKit puts a menu's first item where it's popped up, and its own padding above that, so it's
  popped up `BoardsStyle.systemMenuTopPadding` lower); `BoardPath.foldedMenu(_:editor:)` makes that
  menu, so a test reads and chooses its items without showing it (shown, it's modal). A SwiftUI
  `Menu` draws as a pop-up button, which takes no style from around it and draws without the pill's
  vibrancy: its "…" was darker than the crumbs on a light pill and near white on a dark one. To
