  assistive apps "…" is a pop-up button, "Boards between", whose press shows the menu and whose
  children are its boards, each a button going up to its board: an `accessibilityRepresentation`,
  a `Menu` with a primary action (a representation without one does nothing when pressed).
- A crumb, or an item of "…", runs `goUp(to:)`: it shows that board and selects there the shape the
  path came through, as data-canvas's crumbs do, one step back.
- **It redraws only when the path does.** The view reads only `BoardCrumbs.crumbs`, which the
  service makes again when another board is shown, and when a commit changes a board above the one
  shown (they hold the owners whose titles name the crumbs, and whose locks make boards read-only: a
  file put in place, a lock landing in a commit on one of them), checking each one's revision, so a
  commit on the board shown (a drag's every event) costs a look at the path's revisions and redraws
  nothing. A crumb's title, or whether its board is read-only, changing is the path changing.

#### A crumb's menu

Every crumb has a menu, as data-canvas's do, though unmarked (data-canvas puts a caret after the
title): the pointer on the crumb shows the menu below it, lined up with it. It lists what's in that crumb's board, as the table of
contents lists it (Boards builds on TableOfContents for it: `ContentsOutline`,
[below](#another-boards-outline)), with the shape whose board is next on the path highlighted: the
way you came. The board shown's crumb lists its own shapes. So from inside a subboard you can jump
into another, or to any shape on any board on the way here, without going up and hunting for it
on the canvas. (data-canvas's crumbs listed their boards' subboards this way at first, and later
the board above instead, VS Code's siblings; the owner chose what's in the crumb's board.)

- **What it lists** is `BoardCrumbs.menu(of: board)`, a `CrumbMenu`: the board listed (the
  crumb's) and the shape highlighted there, nil on the board shown's; the menu is nil for the board
  shown while it has no shapes (kept as commits change it, `shownIsEmpty`, so the path never reads
  the document), and without the table of contents, whose rows a menu shows. The rows are the table of contents' with nothing selected, each as its kind draws
  it, nested rows behind a disclosure triangle, a subboard's its board's rows, so a menu reaches
  any shape below its board too.
- **Picking a row** closes the menu, then follows its shape, `editor.follow(id)`: into it if its
  kind opens its board (`opensBoard`: `editor.goInto`, as following a mention of a subboard does),
  and else to it, shown selected on its board (`editor.goTo`). Either is one step back, so ⌘[
  returns. `follow` is Boards' rule for picking a shape from anywhere in the file, written once:
  the crumbs' menus and Jump To's palette both call it. The highlighted
  row goes back into the board it's the way to, and a row of the board shown's own menu selects
  its shape there.
- **Hover intent**, data-canvas's timers (through `editor.scheduler`, so a test's clock drives
  them): the menu shows once the pointer has stayed on the crumb 150 ms, so a crumb passed over
  shows nothing, and closes 150 ms after the pointer has left it and its crumb, unless it's back on
  one of them by then. Another crumb's menu takes its place once the pointer has stayed on that
  crumb. A click on a crumb closes its menu (the board shown's goes nowhere else), and so does
  another board shown. One menu shows at a time: `BoardCrumbs.openMenu`, which the view drives with
  `pointerEntered(crumb:)`, `pointerExited(crumb:)`, `pointerEnteredMenu()`,
  `pointerExitedMenu()`, `closeMenu()` and `pick(_:)`, and a test headlessly.
- **The panel** is 300 points wide, as tall as its rows up to 360 before it scrolls, 6 points below
  the crumb, on a thick material with data-canvas's shadow, and kept 8 points inside the canvas
  (moved left, and shorter, where the canvas is small). data-canvas's is as wide as its rows,
  from 260 to 380; a lazy list can't measure the rows it hasn't made, so here the width is fixed.
  It opens at the top of its rows. A menu showing or closing redraws only the menu (`CrumbMenuLayer` reads `openMenu`, the pill
  never does), and the menu reads its board's rows, as they are while it shows.
- **The canvas under it.** Where the pill or a menu is over the canvas, the pointer isn't on the
  canvas: `CanvasView` asks the window what's at the pointer, and a view the host put over it has
  it, as the minimap does (the tool hears the pointer leave, so nothing under the path is hovered).

### Subboards

Subboards ([`Sources/Subboards`](../Sources/Subboards)) is the vertical with a board inside: the
`subboard` kind, a card that opens onto a board of its own. It's a whole kind in a handful of lines,
because everything it does is a horizontal's
([Subboards.swift](../Sources/Subboards/Subboards.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(SubboardDefinition()) { sub in                     // SubboardDefinition: BoardOwning
    let place = sub.placement(size: Subboard.defaultSize) { Subboard() }
    sub.tool(label: "Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack", shortcut: "b", placing: place)
    sub.tint(SubboardStyle.border)                                  // the card's indigo, wherever it's listed by its kind
    sub.title(symbolInPill: true)                                   // Titles keeps its name, in a pill after the symbol
    sub.opensBoard(placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack")
    sub.mentionable(following: .opens)                              // Mentions: by its title; followed, it's entered
    sub.contentsRow { _ in                                          // in the card's indigo, as its mentions are
        ContentsLabel("", placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack", color: Color(nsColor: SubboardStyle.border))
    }
    sub.details(header: { $sub in TitleHeader($sub, placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack") }) {
        DetailSection(in: DescriptionTab.self) { $sub in            // its own tab: what it's for, with mentions
            MentionTextArea($sub, \.description, placeholder: "Add a description")
        }
        .named("Description")
    }
    sub.subboardLinks()                                             // Connections: ports on its own channel, then on every other
}
registrar.channel(SubboardLink.self)                                // which this plugin declares
```

(The row and the panel are in files of their own, `SubboardRow.swift` and `SubboardPanel.swift`,
as SwiftUI sugar is, and the channel and the ports in `SubboardLinks.swift`.)

- **Its props are its frame and its description**, 240 × 160 placed: `Properties<Subboard>(title:
  "Subboard") { Property("frame", \.frame).required(); Property("description", \.description) }`,
  the description a `MentionText`, empty until it's written, added by the kind's one migration
  (`PropsMigration("description")`, which rewrites nothing, so a board from before reads each
  subboard with an empty one and records the kind at version 1). What it's called is the title
  Titles adds (`title`, marked `x-canvas-owner` in its schema), and its board is the core's, kept
  under its id, so its props hold neither; its schema is marked `x-canvas-board`. Placing one keeps
  no board: a board with no shapes isn't kept.
- **Its description** says what it's for, and is edited in its panel's own tab, Description
  (`DescriptionTab`, a kind's own, `.first`, before the Connections and Style tabs every
  shape has, and the tab a subboard's panel opens on): one headerless section,
  `.named("Description")`, holding `MentionTextArea($sub, \.description)`, the panel's box of
  mention text, two text areas tall, "Add a description" while it's empty. It is mention text as a
  note's text is ([Mentions](#mentions)), so the box has pills, the `@` picker and, on an empty
  line, the subboard's slash commands, each run of typing one undo step, "Change Description", and
  Return is a new line; a locked subboard's reads, dimmed, and takes nothing. The canvas draws it
  nowhere (the card shows its board), so Find, which marks a hit where text is drawn, doesn't search
  it. Everything else is Mentions' and Topology's, with no code here: each mention is a `mention`
  edge from the subboard (slot `description`), so its Connections tab lists what it mentions, what
  it mentions lists it under Mentioned By with the description around the mention, a hover lights
  them, a mention of what can't be mentioned is warned of, a copy that takes a target along renames
  its mention, queries read it (`:mentions`, `[description*="…"]`), and `canvas draw` writes it
  (`subboard "Payments" description: "Owned by @[Billing]"`).
- **B places one** where the canvas is pressed, following the pointer until release, as every box
  tool does: one undo step, "Add Subboard".
- **The card** (`SubboardDefinition.render`, `SubboardStyle`, world units) is the whole frame, and
  its extent is its box: a card with a 10-point radius, the canvas's shadow and a 1.5-point indigo
  border (`NSColor.systemIndigo`). Its
  colors follow the appearance it's drawn in, each a dynamic `NSColor` resolved in the render: a
  faint indigo over white on the light canvas, a raised indigo-gray on the dark one, since a
  subboard is a place on the canvas, not a sheet of paper as a note is. Its title is Titles' pill
  above it, after the `rectangle.stack` symbol (`symbolInPill: true`), as every
  titled shape's is; an untitled one has none. The card shows what its board holds: its preview,
  the core's rough picture of the board (`context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy:in:maxScale:)`,
  fitted 12 points inside the card at no more than a tenth of its size,
  `SubboardStyle.previewMaxScale`, so a board of one note shows a small note in the middle and one
  of hundreds fills the card; every shape a silhouette in one muted gray, as the minimap draws, a
  subboard inside just its rectangle); until that's built, a few frames, how many shapes, from
  `context.shapeCount(inBoardOwnedBy:)`: "1 shape", "12 shapes" (the shapes on its own board, not
  those further down); and for an empty board the kind's symbol over "Empty", the caption alone
  where there's no room for both. The symbol isn't drawn over a count, so a card about to show its
  preview doesn't flash it. The count is read as the card is drawn, and a preview is of one
  revision of its board, so neither is ever stale: a write to the board while another is shown
  (`transact(on:)`) redraws the canvas as any commit does.
- **Its outline** (the selection's, a hover's, the hint) is the core's, the card's rounded edge
  (`indicatorPath`) [stood off it](#outlines) like every closed shape's: the core strokes every
  outline a constant 1.5 view points wide in the accent color (2.5 and fainter for a hover), and
  drawn on the edge that line would cover the card's indigo border, which it's close to in hue and
  width, so a selected card would barely read as selected; stood off 4 view points, its corners
  growing with it (at 100%, a 14-point radius round the card's 10), a gap of the canvas lies between
  the border and the line. The card does nothing for it: the kind says only its edge. Validation's
  ring, [Validation](#a-horizontal-plugin), stands 3 view points past the outline, and the title's
  pill, 9 points above the top edge, stays clear of both.
- **Zoomed out** the card is its [skeleton](#skeletons) ([SubboardSkeleton.swift](../Sources/Subboards/SubboardSkeleton.swift)):
  fills alone, square (its corners are 3.5 points on screen at most there, so its outline is its
  frame's, as the core draws every rect's: a ring filled on the edge, over the half-point border it
  covers, so a selected card shows there as the accent color three times as wide in place of the
  indigo; no outline stands off zoomed out as it does in full, since stroking each subboard in view,
  which is what a standoff would be, costs far more than the ring, and ⌘A zoomed out outlines every
  one of them),
  with no shadow, symbol or count: its border's indigo, never under
  half a view point (just under 35% the card's own 1.5 is about that, so nothing jumps), the card
  inside it, and its board's preview, asked for as the full card asks for it, in the same rect at
  no more than a tenth of its board, drawn once it's built and big enough on screen, else nothing.
  Two fills and the preview; its title is Titles' [cover](#a-cover-zoomed-out), over it, as there's no pill zoomed out.
- **Opening it** is Boards': a double-click, Return, Enter or ⌘↓ with it the only one selected, Open
  first in its menu, and Return once its row is picked (a
  double-click on the row only where the list stays put, not in the app's panel). ⌘↑ comes back with it selected, and ⌘[ retraces. Its panel's header renames it, a run of
  typing one undo step; its row is its symbol and its title, or "Untitled Subboard".
- **Mentioning it** is Mentions': a note's `@` picker offers it by its title, or "Untitled
  Subboard", with its symbol, and a double-click on its pill (or Go to) enters it
  (`following: .opens`, Selection's `goInto`), from its board or another, one step back.
- **Connecting it** is Connections' ([Ports](#ports)): ports on all four sides, on a channel of its
  own, `subboard-link` (`SubboardLink`, its border's indigo), and then on every channel there is
  (`ports(SubboardLink.self)`, then `portsOnEveryChannel()`), so anything that has ports connects
  to a subboard and a subboard to anything that has them: a note on its own
  channel, either way round, and two subboards on `subboard-link`. A dot is its first channel's
  color, and a drag is drawn on the first of its channels the shape it ends on takes, so a
  subboard's dots are indigo, a drag to another subboard is a `subboard-link` and one to a note or
  a card is theirs. An arrow keeps its channel, so a note's link to a subboard can be re-aimed onto
  notes and subboards only, and a subboard's to another onto subboards only. The top dot is in the
  row its title's pill is in, as a note's and a card's are. A pill that stands for one has the same
  dots and links ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in)). Frames have no ports, so an edge
  between a subboard and a frame, in `canvas draw`, says `channel: none`.
- **Deleting it** deletes its board and every board under it, as one step, like any shape's;
  undoing it brings them all back with every id.
- **Locking it** ([Locking](#locking)) locks what's on its board, at any depth: the core makes a board
  whose owner is read-only read-only itself, and so every board under it, a subboard on it included,
  locked or not. Its card is entered as ever, the card's own lock chip is the card's, and on the
  board no shape changes (each try shakes it) and nothing goes on it; the toolbar dims the tools that
  place shapes, Paste is off, no port dots show, and [the path](#the-path) puts a lock after the
  crumb where it starts. Unlocking it frees every board under it.
- **Turning a frame into one** is Transform's ([Transform](#transform)): Subboards takes the container
  channel after its shape block, `registrar.turnable(into: Subboard.self, through: ContainerChannel.self) { … }`,
  which brings Turn into Subboard to the menu of a shape that holds shapes, and `/turn-into-subboard`. The
  subboard keeps the frame's id and title, sits at its corner at 240 × 160, and holds on its board what the
  frame held.

It ships after the sticky note (the toolbar's Subboard, B), with Boards after Titles, and its props
have a fixture for each version (`Fixtures/kinds/subboard.v0.json`, `subboard.v1.json`) as every
shipped kind's do; a whole file of boards nested two deep, with notes and a bound arrow on each, is
`Fixtures/files/nested-described.v4.json`, read and written back byte for byte (written once
subboards had a description, each empty, and once notes' and arrows' text could hold mentions,
though none says anything that mentions); `nested-arrows-mention.v4.json` is the same file from
before subboards had a description, `nested-mentions.v4.json` from before arrows' text could hold
mentions, and `nested.v4.json` from before sticky notes' could, each read with each board's
subboards, notes and arrows brought up to date; and `nested-described-across.v4.json` is the same
file with a note on the root and one two boards down mentioning each other
(`nested-arrows-mention-across.v4.json` and `nested-mentions-across.v4.json` from before, brought up
to date), read, shown live opened on either board, and written back byte for byte
([Mentions across boards](#mentions-across-boards)).

### The core's part: board previews

A shape that owns a board can show what's on it: `context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy: id, in:
rect, maxScale:)`, in its render, draws a rough picture of that board into `rect` (world units),
fitted (the board's proportions kept, centered, and no larger than `maxScale` times its own size, if
given: a board of little is small in the middle rather than as big as one of hundreds), and returns true; or draws nothing and returns false, while the
picture isn't built yet, for a board with nothing to show, and for a rect under 16 view points
either way on screen (nothing to see, so a board zoomed out over many owners asks for none), and
the render draws something else (the subboard card, its count):

```swift
if !context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy: shape.id, in: SubboardStyle.preview(in: body), maxScale: SubboardStyle.previewMaxScale) {
    drawCaption(context.shapeCount(inBoardOwnedBy: shape.id), in: body)
}
```

A [skeleton](#skeletons) may ask for one too, as the subboard's does, in the same rect and at the
same `maxScale`, so the card shows the same picture either side of 35%; the core's default skeleton
never asks.

The picture is the minimap's kind ([Silhouettes.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Rendering/Silhouettes.swift),
the core's, host API, which the minimap draws with too): every shape on the board as a silhouette of
its geometry (its outline filled, or stroked when it's open, or a container's, a frame's, so what
it holds shows on it; under 4 pixels both ways, its bounds, or a line from its first point to its
last when it's open; under a pixel, the pixel it's in: the rule, `Silhouettes.form`, that the
default [skeleton](#skeletons) goes by too), all in one muted gray, and nothing of what a shape
draws, no text and no colors, so a subboard inside is its rectangle, and a shape costs the same
whatever its kind. It's the core's
`BoardPreviews` ([BoardPreviews.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Rendering/BoardPreviews.swift), host API,
`editor.boardPreviews`):

- **Kept by board and revision.** A preview is of the board as one revision of the file had it
  (`file.revision(of:)`), a mask at most 256 pixels on a side. Asked for once the board has changed,
  by an edit or an undo (a revision never comes back), it's dropped, never drawn, and built again.
  The 64 drawn last are kept, the one drawn longest ago going first, but never one the frame before
  drew: with more owners in view than that, those past the number show their count until there's
  room, instead of each frame building one by evicting another, and asking for another frame,
  forever.
- **Sharp up close.** A preview shown larger than its mask (zoomed in, or on a 2× screen, where
  a card at 100% already is) is drawn as paths instead: every shape its outline, kept with the mask
  in cells of a grid over the board, so only the cells in view are drawn, lines 1.5 device pixels
  wide as the mask's are its pixels. Paths cost a shape each (some 1 to 2 µs), so a frame draws
  1,000 that way at most (`pathShapes`), over every preview it shows; past that, the mask, enlarged,
  as for a board of 10,000 shown whole, until zooming in leaves fewer of its shapes in view.
- **Built a chunk at a time.** A board asked for waits its turn, those asked for longest ago first.
  At the start of each frame the editor builds for 2 ms (`frameBudget`), a chunk of shapes at a time
  (the shapes' geometry, from a `ShapeContext` with no index, then their silhouettes), as many as
  fit at what shapes have cost so far, and at least one chunk (16 shapes); while any wait, it asks
  for another frame (`editor.scheduler`). One finished at the start of a frame is drawn in it. One
  whose board changed before it was built is dropped unbuilt, and so is one no shape asked for in
  the frame just drawn (`endFrame()`: its owner scrolled away, or the board was left; showing
  another board drops them all), so a frame builds only for what's in view. So ten subboards of
  10,000 shapes in view fill in over sixty to a hundred frames, each one a frame's worth
  (`./build.sh bench`).

## Frames

Frames ([`Sources/Frames`](../Sources/Frames)) is the vertical with shapes in it: the `frame` kind,
a region of its board that holds what's put down in it. Holding is the core's
([Containers](#containers)): the definition adopts `ShapeContaining`, with nothing to implement,
and the core moves what a frame holds with it, paints it above it, holds it read-only while the
frame is locked, lets go of it when the frame is deleted, and keeps what's put down from sitting
across its edge. The rest is opt-ins, as a subboard's are
([Frames.swift](../Sources/Frames/Frames.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(FrameDefinition()) { frame in                     // FrameDefinition: ShapeContaining, BrushHitTesting
    let place = frame.placement(size: Frame.defaultSize, minimumSize: Frame.minimumSize) { Frame() }   // what a click and draw place, never under 96 × 64
    frame.tool(label: "Frame", systemImage: "rectangle.dashed", shortcut: "f", placing: place) { _ in FrameTool(placing: place) }
    frame.tint(FrameStyle.tint)                                    // its gray, wherever it's listed by its kind
    frame.title(placeholderInPill: "Frame")                        // Titles keeps its name; untitled, a dimmed pill to grab
    frame.mentionable()                                            // Mentions: by its title; followed, it's gone to
    frame.resizable(minimumSize: place.minimumSize)                // Selection's eight handles, no smaller than it's drawn
    frame.frameRow()                                               // the table of contents, named by Titles
    frame.frameHeader()                                            // renamed in the panel's header
    frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)                 // Transform: turned into whatever takes the container channel
}
registrar.createFrameItem()                                        // Create Frame (⇧⌘F, and the context menu), around what it's for
```

- **Its props are its frame**: `Properties<Frame>(title: "Frame") { Property("frame", \.frame).required() }`.
  What it's called is the title Titles adds, and what it holds is each held shape's own
  `container`, the core's, so its props hold neither; it owns no board, so its schema is a plain
  box's. The kind is spelled as the core's own member every box has, `frame`, which the audit can't
  tell from it, so there it's an ordinary word that no module owns ([The module graph](#the-module-graph)).
- **The look** (`FrameStyle`, world units but for the border's width and reach, which are view
  points): a quiet region, a rounded rect (12) with an opaque surface a step up from the canvas,
  white on the light canvas and a 0.15 gray on the dark, in a hairline border just inside its edge
  (a view point at every zoom, black at 12%, white at 14% in the dark), and no shadow: a place on the
  canvas, not a sheet of paper. The dots stop at its edge, and what it holds sits on it. Its colors
  are dynamic `NSColor`s resolved in the render, as a subboard's are, and its outline (the
  selection's, a hover's, the hint a drag into it shows) is its rounded edge. Zoomed out it's its
  [skeleton](#skeletons) ([FrameSkeleton.swift](../Sources/Frames/FrameSkeleton.swift)): its surface
  and its border's ring over it, square, two fills, in the colors they are in full; what it holds
  draws its own skeletons over it, and its title is Titles' [cover](#a-cover-zoomed-out), over both, at its top left (there's no pill zoomed out). In the minimap and a board's
  preview it's its outline, as every container's silhouette is (`Silhouettes`, `hollow`), so what it
  holds shows there too.
- **Pressed hollow** (its `hitTest`): a frame that holds shapes is pressed and hovered only on its
  border, 6 view points either side of its edge (`FrameStyle.borderReach`, which its `hitMargin`
  declares), so a press inside it is the canvas, where a click deselects and a drag is a marquee,
  and the pointer there hovers nothing; one that holds nothing (`ShapeContext.hasContents`) is
  pressed anywhere inside too, as any box is. Its title's pill grabs it, as every pill does its
  shape ([DecorationHits](#drawn-for-a-shape-decorationhits)), and so does an untitled frame's
  dimmed "Frame", there for that (`title(placeholderInPill:)`). What finds shapes by point
  (`editor.shape(at:)`: an arrow's end) goes by the same test.
- **The marquee** selects a frame when it reaches the frame's edge, or holds it whole, never when
  it's drawn wholly inside it, where it selects what the frame holds (Selection's `BrushHitTesting`);
  with ⌘, only what it holds whole, as ever.
- **The Frame tool** (F, `FrameTool`): a drag draws one from the press to the pointer
  (`DrawingFrameSession`), shown over what it's drawn on with its surface at 30%, so what it will
  take in shows through, and put down at the release; a click places one of 640 × 400
  (`Frame.defaultSize`) centered on it, and so does a press that goes less than 12 view points from
  where it began along either axis (`FrameStyle.smallestDrawn`, a click's jitter). Drawn, it's never
  smaller than its placement's `minimumSize` (`Frame.minimumSize`, 96 × 64, which resizing, Create
  Frame and `canvas draw` read there too), grown from the press toward the pointer; ⇧ draws a
  square and ⌥ draws it about the press, as a resize keeps its proportions and its center, each as
  it's pressed or let go; the canvas scrolls at its edges; Escape puts nothing down, and the tool
  stays. Either way it's put down as a placed shape is, through the core's `editor.place` (a drawn
  one with `place(_:in:)`, the rect it drew): one step, "Add Frame"; settled, so a frame drawn in a
  frame is in it, and it takes in what it's drawn over that's mostly inside it, nudging in what
  hangs over its edge and out what's mostly outside, gliding there; selected, with the default tool
  back. Into a locked frame nothing is put down, and that frame shakes. A click inside a frame too
  small to hold 640 × 400 puts the new one over it, not in it, since it doesn't fit there, and the
  frame under it is settled as anything a frame lands on is.
- **The tool says what it places.** What makes shapes without the pointer places a kind as its
  tool's placement says (`registry.placement(for:)`: `canvas draw`, `canvas kinds`), and a tool of
  the kind's own says it too: `frame.tool(label:systemImage:shortcut:placing:_:)` registers
  `FrameTool`, made per editor by the closure, with `place` as its placement, which the tool puts
  down itself for a click. So `canvas draw` draws a frame 640 × 400 unless `size:` says otherwise.
- **Create Frame** ([CreateFrame.swift](../Sources/Frames/CreateFrame.swift)), a command (`.createFrame`,
  ⇧⌘F, on the selection) that an item in the context menu of any shapes a frame can hold (any with a
  box; an arrow alone has none) runs and shows the key of, puts a frame down around
  them, holding them, through the core's `editor.place(_:around:padding:minimumSize:)`
  ([Containers](#containers)): 32 world units past them (`FrameStyle.padding`), and past an arrow
  between two of them, never under 96 × 64 where the frame they're all in has room, in that frame, just
  below the lowest of them in the stack. They stay where they are; what the new frame lands on beside them is settled as what a drawn frame lands on is
  (mostly inside comes in, nudged fully in; mostly outside is nudged out; gliding there). It's
  untitled and selected, one step named as the item ("Create Frame"). A locked shape among them (or
  one in a locked frame) leaves it all as it was, and shakes. An item for the canvas, as Turn into
  Subboard is, in a group of its own (`FramesMenuGroup`, `.after(TransformMenuGroup.self)`: right after
  Turn into's, before Cut, Copy and Paste), so Frames is on ContextMenus. tldraw's Frame Selection is the model, with three
  intended deviations: the padding is world units, as the model is, where tldraw's is 25 view points
  (zoomed out, that would reach over the neighbors); the frame goes just below the lowest of them,
  not on top of everything, so it covers nothing beside them that was above them, and shows on a big
  shape under them (a zone `canvas draw` drew); and a locked shape among them refuses the whole, as Turn
  into does, where tldraw frames the rest around it. Its key is ⇧⌘F, not tldraw's ⌥⌘G, which is Group's
  here (Keynote's and Freeform's); the step is named "Create Frame" for the key as for the item, and no menu bar
  item runs it, so the Shape menu carries it. Not built: Remove Frame and Fit to Content.
- **Opt-ins.** Titles keeps its name, shown in its pill (untitled, a dimmed "Frame"; no symbol, since
  its look says what it is), and `TitleHeader` renames it in its panel's header ("Untitled Frame").
  Mentions offers it by its title, its symbol in its gray (`NSColor.systemGray`, its row's too), and
  following a mention goes to it (`goTo`), with Show What Mentions in
  its menu; untitled, the picker leaves it out. Selection resizes it, and the core settles, at the
  end of the resize, what it leaves hanging over its edge and what it grows over
  ([Containers](#containers)). Its row is its symbol and "Untitled Frame", named by Titles; the
  table of contents lists what it holds under it. Locking, which opts every kind in, locks it, and
  with it what it holds. No ports: nothing is drawn from a frame's sides. Transform's container channel
  (`frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)`, the last of its opt-ins) makes it something that can be
  turned into whatever takes the channel, a subboard in the app, from its menu ([Transform](#transform));
  Frames only offers the channel, names no kind that takes it, and brings no Turn into item or command of
  its own.

It ships after Subboards (the toolbar's Frame, F, between Subboard and Schema: the two ways of
grouping shapes, a region of the board and a board of its own, side by side), with its fixture,
`Fixtures/kinds/frame.v0.json`; `Fixtures/files/frames.v5.json` is a whole file, read and written
back as read: a frame holding a frame, which holds a note and a subboard, and a schema card (a kind no
longer shipped, kept aside, so its board's write-back moves its version into it as `v`),
beside a locked frame holding a note, and a note on the subboard's board (CompositionTests'
`FrameFile`). FramesTests hold the kind, its hollow test, its marquee, its look, its tool, Create Frame
(CreateFrameTests) and what it offers Transform (TurnTests, with CanvasTesting's pocket taking the channel) over
CanvasTesting's boxes, frozen for read-only (`FreezingPlugin`); CompositionTests' FramesShippedTests
the shipped pieces together: notes dropped in and out, a group across an edge, a locked frame
refusing a drop, a frame moved with a locked note in it, frames in frames, resizing over notes,
deleting one, pressing its inside, its pill, the tool, Create Frame around two notes and the bent
arrow between them, a locked frame's contents, the skeleton, the file, and a note mentioning one in
the app's canvas view; TransformShippedTests turn one into a
subboard ([Transform](#transform)).

## Transform

Transform ([`Sources/Transform`](../Sources/Transform)) turns a shape into another kind: a frame into a
subboard, from its context menu or as a command. It's a horizontal on [context menus](#context-menus) and
[slash commands](#slash-commands), and it exists because the two kinds can't meet any other way. A vertical
imports no other vertical, so Frames can't name Subboards (the audit refuses even the string `"subboard"`
in Frames) and Subboards can't name Frames. What turns into what is a graph, and its edges are
**channels**: a kind *offers* one, another kind *takes* it and says how, and a shape can turn into each
kind that takes a channel its own kind offers. The core knows none of it. It lends two generic things, the
transaction's `turn(_:into:)` and `move(_:toBoardOwnedBy:)` ([Containers](#containers), [Boards in a
file](#the-editor-and-the-file)), which a target turns with.

```
┌─────────┐  offers   ┌───────────────────┐   takes  ┌───────────┐
│  frame  │ ────────▶ │ container channel │ ◀─────── │ subboard  │
└─────────┘           └───────────────────┘          └───────────┘
 Frames imports Transform, and so does Subboards; neither imports the other
```

```swift
// In FramesPlugin.register, last of the frame's opt-ins:
frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)

// In SubboardsPlugin.register, after its shape block:
registrar.turnable(into: Subboard.self, through: ContainerChannel.self) { container, transaction in
    guard transaction.turn(container.id, into: Subboard(frame: CGRect(origin: container.frame.origin, size: Subboard.defaultSize))) else { return }
    transaction.move(container.inside, toBoardOwnedBy: container.id)
}
```

### Offering and taking a channel

A channel is a type conforming to `TransformChannel`
([Transform.swift](../Sources/Transform/Transform.swift)): the `Source` a shape coming through it hands the
target, a `name` (what the registry's report calls it), `admits(_:)`, which kinds may offer it (given a
`RegisteredKind`, the core's: the kind, its definition, so its capabilities, the registry, `holds` and
`adopts`; every kind by default),
and `source(of:in:)`, which reads what the shape hands over in the transaction that turns it, before the
target changes anything. A channel that has nothing to hand over for a shape returns nil: the target's turn
doesn't run, and the shape stays as it is. Conform in an extension, as with every protocol that has a
default (`admits` is the one that could be misspelled). The sugar:

| Sugar | For |
|---|---|
| `x.turnable(through: C.self)` | This kind's shapes can be turned into whatever takes the channel, inside `registrar.shape { x in ... }`. |
| `registrar.turnable(K.self, through: C.self)` | The same, for another plugin's kind. |
| `registrar.turnable(into: P.self, through: C.self, label:) { source, transaction in ... }` | Shapes of the kinds that offer the channel can be turned into `P`'s, and the closure is how: it gets what the channel handed over and the transaction. |

- **Offering is keyed by kind and channel** (`TransformSources`): a kind offers a channel once, and two
  claims are a `conflict` ("corral offering container"). The point's `check` refuses a kind the channel
  doesn't admit (`invalid`: "bad offers the container channel on box, which can't offer it"). Only a
  kind offers one, so there's no sugar for every shape, and the point says so (`scope` `.kinds`: the
  registry refuses a scope or every kind, as it does for the targets).
- **Taking is keyed by the kind turned into** (`TransformTargets`): a shape turns into a kind one way, so a
  kind takes one channel, and a second claim is a `conflict` ("disc"): a second channel into one kind would
  share its menu item and its command. If one is ever needed, that's where it's decided.
- **The graph** is `registry.turnTargets(of: kind)`: each kind whose target takes a channel `kind` offers,
  in plugin order, never `kind` itself.
- **`TransformPlugin()` is the owner.** It registers the service and nothing else, and a list with a kind
  that offers a channel or takes one needs it (`ownerNotInstalled`). A target brings a menu item and a
  command, so it needs `ContextMenusPlugin()` and `SlashCommandsPlugin()` too, and a kind whose id can't be
  typed as a command's name ("odd_one") is refused (`invalid`, from the commands' point).
- **The report** shows each contribution: `offers channel container → frame` on Frames' line and `takes
  channel container → subboard · CanvasContextMenu · /turn-into-subboard → every shape that can turn
  into subboard` on Subboards',
  and `service TransformState` on its own ([The registry](#the-registry)).

### What a target brings

Taking a channel is the whole of a feature: the same call brings its menu item and its command, as an
opt-in does for a horizontal.

- **Turn into `label`** in the context menu: an item for the canvas, as Show What Mentions is, since what
  a shape can turn into is what the registry knows, not the shape. It's in `TransformMenuGroup`
  (`.after(ActionsMenuGroup.self)`, ContextMenus' empty group for what acts on the shapes: after a kind's own items and Mentions', before Cut, Copy and Paste), shown when every shape the menu is for
  can turn into the kind, so a menu for a frame and a note has none. The label is what the target kind's
  schema is titled (a subboard's is "Subboard"), else its id, unless the call gives one.
- **`/turn-into-<kind id>`** on the kinds that offer the channel, the target's own kind apart (it has
  nothing to turn into): a scope's command, by a capability the call makes ("that can turn into
  subboard", whose test reads which kinds offer the channel), taking no arguments.
  Typed on a line of a shape's text, it turns the shape; a frame has no text, so nothing ships that types
  it yet, though it's offered (`commands(for:)`) and runs (`run(_:on:with:)`). Where a kind that offers
  the channel does have text, it lists before `title` and `lock`: the scopes' commands are offered in the
  order of the plugins that contribute them, and Subboards is before Titles and Locking.
- **One undo step**, "Turn into Subboard", named as the item is. Slash commands name their steps in title
  case for this: "Turn Into Subboard" beside the menu's item would read as a mistake
  ([Running a command](#what-a-shape-offers-and-running-a-command)).

### Turning

`TransformState` (`editor.transforms`, nil without the plugin) is the service. It keeps nothing per shape
(each kind's targets are worked out once, the registry being frozen, so `boardDidChange` is overridden with
nothing), and it's what the item and the command call:

```swift
let transforms = editor.transforms
transforms.targets(of: frame)                    // [Subboard.kind]: none for a shape off the board shown or kept aside
transforms.canTurn(frame, into: Subboard.kind)   // true: a read-only shape can too, and turning it is refused
transforms.turn([frame], into: Subboard.kind)    // true: one undo step, "Turn into Subboard"
```

- **`turn(_:into:)`** turns those of its shapes that can, each once, **innermost first** (the deepest in
  containers, then back to front), in one `editor.transact`. A frame inside another turns first and moves
  what it held onto its own board, so by the time the outer one reads what it holds, the inner one is a
  subboard in it. A frame selected with the frames inside it turns them all.
- **It keeps the container it's in, then it's put down as a placement is.** A turned shape comes out a
  different size (a subboard is 240 × 160), so it may hang over the container it's in, or reach into
  another. One that hangs over its container is shifted back inside it, `Settlement.gap` in, where it
  fits, since the in-or-out rule judges by area and would put a shape mostly outside out; then
  `transaction.settle(turned)` is that rule ([Containers](#containers)), nudging it clear of another
  container it reaches, and the editor glides it there.
- **Once one is refused, no other target runs**: the turn will be thrown away. The rest are still checked
  for read-only, so every one that is shakes.
- **All or nothing for read-only shapes.** A shape that's locked, in a locked container, or on a locked
  subboard's board, isn't turned,
  and neither is one that holds a locked shape: the target moves everything, so if anything it would move
  is read-only (`transaction.refusedShapes`), or a read-only container would take the turned shape, the
  whole turn is given up (`editor.transactWhole`). Nothing changes, no step is made, and the refused shapes are
  heard (`editor.refuseChanges(to:)`, so Locking shakes them). A shape that's read-only is refused before
  its target runs. A target that throws turns nothing either. `turn` returns whether it turned any.

### The container channel

`ContainerChannel` ([ContainerChannel.swift](../Sources/Transform/ContainerChannel.swift)) is the first
channel, and the only one that ships: it's offered by the kinds whose shapes hold shapes
(`ShapeContaining`: `admits` is that, so the registry refuses it on a box), and hands the target a
`TurningContainer`: the container's `id` and `frame`, and what is `inside` it. That's the shapes in it at any
depth (read when its turn comes, so fewer by what an inner container that turned before it took onto
its own board). The move takes them along with every shape whose props bind shapes
(`ShapeReferencing`: an arrow) that is bound to some of those and to nothing else (the core's rule for
any move, [Boards in a file](#the-editor-and-the-file)): an arrow between two of its notes goes with them;
one bound to anything that stays, the container included, or to nothing, stays.

### A frame into a subboard

Frames offers the channel and Subboards takes it; each is one line, and neither knows the other. The
turn is the target's: `transaction.turn` makes the frame a subboard, and `transaction.move` puts what it
held on the subboard's board. A turn that took is followed by a move; one that didn't (the guard) leaves
a frame, which owns no board for `move` to move onto (`move` would move nothing and say false).

- **The subboard is a subboard's size at the frame's top-left corner**, `Subboard.defaultSize` (240 × 160),
  whatever size the frame was.
- **It keeps the frame's id**, and with it everything that goes by id: the arrows bound to it and what
  mentions it (a mention is live, its pill shows the subboard now, and following it enters the board),
  its place in the stack, the frame it's in, and its title, which both kinds hold (`TitleProperty`: Titles
  keeps it, and `turn` carries over the added values the new kind holds too). The values it doesn't hold
  go, and what the new kind holds that the old one didn't is a default.
- **What it held goes onto the subboard's board**, under the same ids and in the same places (world
  coordinates are kept) and in the order they were. A frame owns no board, so the subboard's is new to
  the file, or, for a frame with nothing in it, none is kept. Frames inside stay frames there, holding
  what they held, and a subboard inside takes the board it owns with it, as every board goes with its owner.
- **Bindings** are to shapes on the same board, so the turn lets go of those across the edge, as a cut
  does: an arrow bound to a note inside and a note outside keeps its end on the one outside, and the
  other end stays where it's drawn. Arrows between shapes that all move go along, bound (the core's
  `move(_:to:)` takes them, as it does for any move). A name, a mention
  of a note that moved, is kept: it never cared which board the note is on.
- **Undo** puts back the frame, every shape in it and every binding, in one step.
- **What isn't built**: the reverse (a subboard into a frame), a transform in `canvas draw`, and a `/` typed
  on the canvas. A shape with text that offers the channel would get `/turn-into-subboard` for free.

### Testing transform

- **TransformTests** hold the mechanism over fixtures only, since Transform knows no shipped kind:
  CanvasTesting's corrals (they hold shapes, as a frame does) offer the container channel and turn into
  pockets (they own a board, as a subboard does), with a target written as Subboards' is
  ([Support.swift](../Tests/TransformTests/Support.swift): `corralsTurnIntoPockets()`), a `Tagline` added
  property both kinds hold, as both hold a title, and a channel of the tests' own, `BoxChannel` (only a box
  offers it, and it hands over the box's id if the box is narrow), turning boxes into discs, so that the
  mechanism is held apart from containers. They hold registration (the report's entries, the graph in plugin
  order, conflicts, a channel's `admits`, `ownerNotInstalled` and `unknownKind`, a command name that can't be
  typed), resolution (`targets(of:)`, `canTurn`), the menu (a right-click: the item in its band, choosing
  it, nested corrals selected together turning innermost first, a corral and a box showing none, one item
  for each target, a source that says no), the command (offered where it should be, one step named as the
  item is), all or nothing (a frozen box in the corral, a frozen corral, one in a frozen corral, one deep
  in nested corrals, a target never run for a read-only shape, a target that throws), the in-or-out rule
  and bindings.
- **FramesTests' and SubboardsTests' `TurnTests.swift`** hold each end of the edge over a partner of its
  own, since neither can use the other: Frames offers the channel with a pocket as the target (the title
  carried over, a frame inside still a frame holding its box, no Turn into item or command until a kind
  takes the channel, a locked box or frame refusing); Subboards takes it from corrals that offer it (the size and
  the corner, what the corral held on its board, a link inside riding and one across let go, the table
  of contents, Return entering it, `/turn-into-subboard`, an empty corral).
- **CompositionTests' `transformShippedTests`** hold the shipped pieces together, on a pasteboard of
  their own: a frame titled Groceries, holding two notes and a frame that holds a note, a note beside it
  that mentions it, and arrows bound to the notes, turned from its context menu (the item between Show
  What Mentions and Create Frame, before Cut; the subboard, its title, its board; the mention live and the pill, the row and
  the panel of a subboard; one arrow riding along and one letting go; the canvas drawn without what
  moved, and as it was after Undo), as a command, with a locked note or a locked frame leaving everything
  as it was, a frame turned with the frame inside it, a frame on a subboard's board turned there (and Undo
  from the root showing that board), the frames file's Roadmap (a frame holding a frame,
  a subboard with a board of its own and a card kept aside) turned with every board in its place, and the file
  after a turn read back through `BoardCodec`. The registry's report holds `transform`, Frames' `offers
  channel container → frame` and Subboards' `takes channel container → subboard`.

## Jump To

Jump To ([`Sources/JumpTo`](../Sources/JumpTo)) is ⌘K, and Go › Jump To…: a palette that goes to a
shape by what it's called and where it is, as VS Code's file switcher goes to a file. Name a
subboard, skip one, name another two levels down, then the shape, and the list narrows. It looks at
titles and the containment tree and never at contents (that's Find's). It's a thing you do (no kind opts into
it and nothing imports it, as with [Reordering](#many-kinds-reordering)): a shape is listed
when its kind has a title ([Titles](#a-horizontal-plugin), named or derived), and that's all a kind
does for it. It builds on Boards (a pick is `editor.follow`, below), Titles, Topology (the tree),
Keyboard, TextEditing (its field and its list), FuzzyMatching and Geometry. It doesn't import
Mentions: a row's symbol and tint are its kind's label's (`registry.label(of:)`, the core's), the
one color a kind has in the list, the picker and the Connections tab; a kind that declares no tint is
untinted.

```
 ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
 │  alpha gamma check                             │   a capsule at the top middle, below the path
 ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ ▭ Checkout          Alpha › Beta › Gamma      │   the app's caret list, under it, 560 wide,
   │ ▭ Checkout    Alpha › Beta › Gamma › Epsilon  │   10 rows shown: the kind's symbol, the title,
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘   the path, what matched in semibold
```

- **`JumpToPlugin`** (id `jump-to`) registers a service, `JumpToState` (`editor.jumpTo`), and
  `registrar.command(.jumpTo, title: "Jump To…", menu: "Go", order: 100, shortcut: ⌘K, runs: .betweenPresses)`
  (Go › Jump To…, after Open Selection): it ends editing, then opens the palette,
  or, open, asks its field for the keyboard again with its text selected; never mid-gesture. It
  changes no document, so it leaves no step of undo. The menu item is the same command, so ⌘K
  works from a note being edited and a panel's field too, where it's the menu bar's key.
- **The catalog** is every titled shape on every board the editor can show, named or derived, none
  kept aside, each with the container it's directly in (a frame, else the owner of its board), its
  title's folded keys in one buffer, as Mentions' catalog keeps its labels. It's built the first
  time the palette opens, in slices of 2 ms on the main actor (`editor.scheduler`; the first at once),
  so a commit before then costs one test; after, a commit costs what it changed (a
  move reads nothing; a rename reads the shape; shapes on other boards a commit reached, a deleted
  subboard's or a paste's, are taken out or read as well), and a file put in place reads it again. A commit while it's being built is applied to what's read so far,
  the shapes on boards not read yet read when their turn comes, so commits that never stop (an
  agent's draw, a sync) can't keep it from finishing. It keeps no path: a container's rename costs nothing in it.
- **Ranking.** A word names titles alone, `FuzzyMatcher.rank` over the buffer (the `@` picker's
  workload). Several words are pieces placed in order along a path, a group of neighbors to a
  name, names skipped as they like, the last in the shape's own title (`PathMatcher`): the last
  piece is matched against every title first, and only what it matches is scored by its path, a
  container's row (the best score of placing the first g pieces along the chain to it) made once per
  query for everything under it, so a shape costs one match for each group the last could be in. A
  container's name must be a name, never a scatter of its letters (a bare subsequence matches only
  the shape's own title); an untitled container is on the path by what its kind is called, dimmed,
  and is never matched (Boards' `registry.containerName(of:)`, as every path calls a container). Ties go to the fewer names skipped, the shallower path, a recent pick, and
  the file's order.
- **An empty query** lists "Recent" (up to five of this window's picks) and "Nearby" (up to five
  titled shapes in view on the board shown, nearest the middle of the view).
- **The palette** is `JumpToPalette(editor:onExit:)`, which the window places over
  the canvas (`JumpToPlugin` gives it to [the host's slot](#host-slots) for views over the canvas,
  after Boards', so it's over the path): closed it's nothing; open, a scrim (a clear button, so a click lands on it, closes the
  palette and isn't the canvas's), and a capsule below the part of the canvas the host leaves clear,
  taken as it opened (so below the path over a subboard), with an `EditingTextView` in one line. Its
  list is the app's one caret list (`CaretList` in a `CaretListWindow` made with `anchorRect:`,
  [TextEditing](#a-list-at-the-caret)). ↑ ↓ ⌃P ⌃N and Page Up and Down move, Return and Tab pick,
  Escape and ⌘. close; the keyboard goes back to the canvas as the person closes it, and the palette
  closes by itself once anything else takes the keyboard (Find's field, the panel's).
- **A pick** is `editor.follow(id)` ([Boards](#a-crumbs-menu)), one step back: into a shape whose
  kind opens its board, else to it, a frame fitted into view, never forced to a readable zoom.

JumpToTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes, pockets and corrals, titled through Titles' property:
the catalog's laziness, slices and upkeep, the ranking over a story file ("alpha gamma checkout"),
the empty query, picks and the palette in a window; CompositionTests' JumpToShippedTests as the app
wires it. `./build.sh bench` holds a keystroke (one piece ≤ 2 ms over 10,000 shapes, several ≤ 4 ms),
the build's slices (≤ 3 ms) and what a commit costs with the plugin in the list.

## Moving

Moving ([`Sources/Moving`](../Sources/Moving)) is two slash commands that move the shape whose text
they're typed in: `/move-to @Groceries` puts a note in a frame, or onto a subboard's board, and
`/move-near @Checkout` puts it beside a shape, on the first of its four sides that's free, or, with
none free, on the side that frees up nearest. Both reach every board of the file the app can show,
not only the one shown, and the shape each takes is a pill picked with `@` on its line, where the
picker lists only what it takes (for `/move-to`, with nothing typed, every frame and subboard it
takes, on every board, nearest first). It's a thing you do (no kind opts into it and nothing imports it, as with
[Jump To](#jump-to) and [Reordering](#many-kinds-reordering)): on [slash
commands](#slash-commands) for the commands, on the [table of contents](#dragging-rows) for its
drops that move shapes (`ContentsMoves`), and on Draw for where a shape
lands, since it places a shape as [`canvas draw`](#draw) places one (the same solver, the same
obstacles, the same zones) and moves it with the core's own tools, as draw's commit does.
Draw's placement for plugins (`Sources/Draw/Surroundings.swift`) is the solver moved out of Moving, so any plugin
that puts a shape down, not only Moving, places it the same way: `Surroundings(on:moving:in:)`, with
`near(_:within:)` beside a shape, `inside(_:)` in a frame, `between(_:_:growing:)` between two shapes
and `anywhere()`, each answering a `Landing` (the board, the box, the shapes to raise it above);
Moving keeps the glue for its `Block` and the commit. `between` is for a shape two arrows will join
to the two: in the gap the pair leaves along the axis they are further apart on, centered in it and
on their middle across, with `room` (default `PlacingStyle.arrowRoom`, 80; a caller whose arrows carry
names asks for more) kept clear on each side so each arrow shows a body, the two read `growing`
taller (both are about to gain a row); the frames the two are in are regions the box sits on (it is
raised above them), never something in its way; where that spot is taken or no gap holds it, beside
the middle of the two on the nearer side across the line between them, clear of both.

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Ask about the beta           │   a note being edited
│ /move-near @che              │   the command, then @ and what narrows the picker
│ ┌──────────────────────┐     │
│ │ ▭ Checkout           │     │   the @ picker: only what the command takes
│ └──────────────────────┘     │   Return picks it; Return again moves the note
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

```swift
// In MovingPlugin.register: on every kind whose shapes have a box, the kinds a drag moves.
registrar.forShapes(adopting: .box) { boxes in
    boxes.slashCommands {
        SlashCommand("move-to", argument: "@frame or subboard", kinds: { $0.containingKinds.union($0.boardOwningKinds) },
                     shapes: { target, owner, editor in Destination(of: owner, into: target, in: editor) != nil },
                     step: "Move") { id, arguments, editor in
            guard let target = arguments.shapes.first else { return }
            Move(id, in: editor)?.into(target)      // asks its rule again, places, commits
        }
        SlashCommand("move-near", shapes: { target, owner, editor in admitsNear(target, for: owner, in: editor) },
                     step: "Move") { id, arguments, editor in
            guard let target = arguments.shapes.first else { return }
            Move(id, in: editor)?.near(target)
        }
    }
}
```

- **`MovingPlugin`** (id `moving`, the module's one public type) puts both commands on every kind
  whose props are `BoxShapeProps` (the core's capability `.box`, "with a box"), so a link, a tag or an arrow
  offers neither, and fills the table of contents' `ContentsMoves`; the report's line is
  `moving /move-to /move-near → every shape with a box · ContentsMoves`. It's right before
  Reordering in the shipped list, after every plugin with a command for many kinds, so a note's `/`
  list ends `title, lock, public, move-to, move-near`. Both steps are "Move", a drag's name ("Undo
  Move To" would read badly). A list with it needs `SlashCommandsPlugin()` and
  `TableOfContentsPlugin()`.
- **`/move-to` takes a frame or a subboard** (its `kinds`, the kinds that hold shapes or own boards,
  so the picker ranks only those, and only the titled ones, which have names) on any board the app
  can show, but not the shape itself, or what goes with it (what it holds at any depth, and what's on
  a board it, or a shape it holds, owns: the core's `move(_:to:)` traps on those); not one that's
  read-only (locked, in a locked frame, or on a board that takes no shapes: a locked subboard's, at
  any depth, `editor.isReadOnly(inFile:)`, the rule `move(_:to:)` refuses by, so a frame two boards
  under a locked subboard isn't taken though the subboard on the way isn't locked itself); not
  where the shape is already (the frame it's directly in, the subboard whose board is shown); and not
  a frame narrower or shorter than the shape. A frame is a place in it, on its board; a subboard,
  its own board, as draw's `in` takes one.
- **`/move-near` takes any shape** but the shape itself and, for a shape that holds shapes or owns a
  board, what goes with it. The picker asks this of every shape as the person types, so it costs
  next to nothing: a locked target is fine (it doesn't change), a shape on a read-only board too, and
  whether the target's board takes shapes is the move's to say (the move onto one is refused, and
  the owner of that board is heard). Each command asks its rule again as it runs: a target it no
  longer takes (gone, or locked since) moves nothing.
- **Where it lands is draw's** ([draw](#draw), step 3), worked out by Draw's `Surroundings`: the destination board read in place
  (`editor.reading(of:)`), every shape there with a solid an obstacle, filed once in DrawScript's
  `ObstacleGrid`, the shape itself left out on its own board and what it holds carried (never in its
  way), and the shape the problem's one free box, at its size, put down anew. **Near X**: four
  problems, one per side (right, below, left, above), each `<side> of X` at draw's default gap
  (`normal`, 80), centered on X the other way, the solver pushing the box out along that side's axis
  past what's in the way, with draw's clearances (40 across, 64 up and down); the side that lands
  nearest X wins, the earlier on a tie. **Into frame F**: draw's `in "F"` (`inside "F" top-left`, F
  holding it), 40 in, pushed clear of what's in F and kept within it, but held directly
  (`Holder.direct`): a frame in F is in its way like any shape there, never a zone it lands in, so it
  goes in F itself, not in a frame nested at F's top-left; with no room from that corner, from F's
  top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right in turn; with none, at F's top-left, 40 in (half its room,
  where F is barely bigger), over what's there. **Onto a subboard's board**:
  draw's one unplaced shape, at the middle of the view that board would be shown with, or the
  nearest clear spot around it, ring by ring. Zones are draw's too: a frame that holds X is a region
  the shape sits on, not a shape in its way, so a note moved beside a note in a frame lands in the
  frame, and one landing over a zone that paints above it is raised above it.
- **One step, all or nothing.** It's one `editor.transactWhole("Move")`, with the core's tools as draw's
  commit uses them. On the board shown: `translate` (what a frame holds goes along),
  `move(_:above:)` over what it sits on that paints above it, and `settle` (the in-or-out rule: in
  the frame it's mostly over, out of the one it left, [Containers](#containers)). Onto another
  board: `move(_:to:)` first, so an arrow bound to it lets go where it was drawn, as after a cut,
  then `translate(_:by:on:)` there of the shapes and of what the move took along (an arrow bound
  only to them rides along, and its free end goes as far as they do: the core says what rode,
  `rodeAlong`, so Moving writes the rule for none of it) and `settle(_:on:)`
  ([Boards in a file](#the-editor-and-the-file)).
  A read-only shape in the way (a locked frame it would land in, the owner of a board that takes no
  shapes it would go onto, locked or under one that is, a locked note in a frame going onto another
  board) gives the whole move up: nothing changes, no step is made, and the locked shapes shake, as a
  refused [turn](#turning) does. (A shape on a read-only board
  is offered no command at all, as no read-only shape is, so none moves off one.) On the board shown, what moved glides there and a note being
  edited is put down (editing ends, as a `canvas draw` that moves it ends it); onto another board,
  it's gone from the one shown, the window stays where it is, and Undo Move puts both boards back
  exactly. A move that lands where the shape is commits nothing.

- **Rows dropped in the table of contents** ([Dragging rows](#dragging-rows)) where their shapes
  aren't are Moving's too (`Drop`): the shapes move as one block (`Block`: on one board, any the app
  can show, less those another of them holds, placed by the box around them all, keeping where they
  are to each other), into a frame (its row, or among the rows it holds) as `/move-to` puts a shape
  there, if the block fits; onto a subboard's board (its row, or among its board's rows) as `/move-to`
  puts one there; out of the frames they're in (among the rows of a frame they're in at any depth, or
  of the board) beside the outermost one they leave, as `/move-near` puts a shape beside it, kept
  within the frame they go to (with no room beside it there, in that frame as `/move-to` puts one).
  From another board they move off it with the core's `move(_:from:to:)`. The same commit, then, in
  the same step, every shape dropped restacked where the drop says (`ContentsPlace.restack`); Undo
  Move takes it all back. Where the in-or-out rule leaves them out of the place (no room in a frame
  clear of the frame they leave, which takes them back), nothing changes: a drop puts them where it
  says, or nowhere. Refused as `/move-to` refuses: a locked frame, one too small, the locked owner
  of a board, what goes with them.

MovingTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes, corrals, pockets, links, cards and freezing, run
through `editor.slashCommands` and the table of contents' drops: what each takes, every landing, the
step and refusals; CompositionTests' `movingShippedTests` type both into a note's editor in the app
(the picker's list, a pick and the run, a subboard's board, Undo Move), and
`contentsDragShippedTests` drop notes' rows on a frame's, a subboard's and each other's.

## Neighbors

Neighbors ([`Sources/Neighbors`](../Sources/Neighbors)) shows what's connected to a shape at a glance,
which in a dense graph is the point: hover a shape, on the canvas or by its row in the [table of
contents](#the-table-of-contents), and every shape connected to it is outlined in a color that says
how, and the arrows between are colored too. The minimap fills the same shapes in the same colors,
so what's connected off screen shows there (the rest of it dims while anything is lit, and a shape
in two lights shows both, one inside the other), and a connected shape on another board (inside a
subboard) lights the card that holds it. Select a shape and its panel's Connections tab lists what's
connected to it by the same ways, then what it's inside and what it holds. It's an engine: what an
edge's owner shows its edges on. It builds on Queries (which finds the shapes), Selection (the hover,
and the one a list sets for a shape the canvas doesn't show), Topology (when a shape's edges change),
the file (where a shape on another board is drawn), the core's [tinted outlines](#outlines), and, for
the tab, [the detail panel](#the-detail-panel), [FuzzyMatching](#fuzzymatching) (its search) and the
[table of contents](#the-table-of-contents) (what a listed shape with no title is called), and
it knows no kind, edge type or concern: what counts as connected is a **light**, a title, a color
and a query, which the plugin that owns the edges contributes to its point
(`registrar.neighborLight`). Arrows' two are Arrows' own (`ArrowLightsPlugin`), mentions' two are
Mentions' (`MentionLightsPlugin`) and the two for what is of a type are Types' (`TypeLightsPlugin`),
each a plugin value of its own, so a list without Neighbors leaves them out.

| Light | Color | What's outlined, for the shape hovered, and listed, for the shape selected |
|---|---|---|
| Points To | green | the shapes an arrow out of it ends at and the shape a reference stands for; for an arrow, the shape it ends at |
| Pointed To By | purple | the shapes that have an arrow into it and the references that stand for it; for an arrow, the shape it starts at |
| Mentions | teal | the shapes its text mentions |
| Mentioned By | lavender | the shapes whose text mentions it |
| Instances | pink | what is of it, however far, never a type: a note that is it, and what is of a type built on it; a relationship type's arrows |
| Subtypes | pink | the types built on it, however far: a kind of it, and none of it |

The arrows themselves, between a shape and those, are outlined with them and never listed (a light's
`between`).

The colors are their owners' (`ArrowStyle.pointsToLight` and `pointedToByLight`,
`MentionStyle.mentionsLight` and `mentionedByLight`), chosen together in a design audit from renders of
the lights over both canvases: one fixed sRGB value for each appearance
(`NeighborLight.color(light:dark:)`, [Palette](#palette)'s `NSColor(light:dark:)`), never a system color (system pink read as Validation's error red, system purple as
the selection's blue, and the light-mode green and teal fell under 3:1). In the light and the dark:
green #07933B and #2FD359, purple #8C21A4 and #B851FD, teal #0E97B0 and #329AB4, lavender #A76FE2
and #D0B0FE. Each is clear of Validation's red and orange and of Find's orange, at least 3:1 against
the canvas it's drawn over in both appearances, and not the accent; the two purples are close for
some color-vision deficiencies. Types' pink (`TypesStyle.instancesLight`), #C2307A and #F07AB5, came
after, by the same rules; gold, the other hue the four leave, read as a yellow note's own edge on the dark
canvas.

```swift
// A light is a title, a color and a query, given `#id`, the shape hovered or listed, and the edge
// types come from their plugins' ids, never written out. `between` finds what runs between the shape
// and those (the arrows): outlined with them, never listed. `caption` is a line under a listed
// shape's name, from the editor, the shape the list is of and the listed one.

// Arrows (ArrowLightsPlugin, id `arrow-lights`):
let arrow = ArrowEdge.id.rawValue, standing = StandingEdge.id.rawValue
registrar.neighborLight(ArrowStyle.pointsTo, color: ArrowStyle.pointsToLight, query: {
    ":edge-from(\($0), \(arrow)|\(standing)), :end-of(\($0), \(arrow))"
}, between: {
    ":starts-at(\($0), \(arrow))"
})
registrar.neighborLight(ArrowStyle.pointedToBy, color: ArrowStyle.pointedToByLight, query: {
    ":edge-to(\($0), \(arrow)|\(standing)), :start-of(\($0), \(arrow))"
}, between: {
    ":ends-at(\($0), \(arrow))"
})

// Mentions (MentionLightsPlugin, id `mention-lights`):
let mention = MentionEdge.id.rawValue
registrar.neighborLight(MentionStyle.mentions, color: MentionStyle.mentionsLight, query: { ":edge-from(\($0), \(mention))" })
registrar.neighborLight(MentionStyle.mentionedBy, color: MentionStyle.mentionedByLight, query: { ":edge-to(\($0), \(mention))" },
                        caption: { editor, subject, mentioner in editor.mentions?.quote(of: mentioner, around: subject) })

// Types (TypeLightsPlugin, id `type-lights`):
let isA = IsAEdge.id.rawValue, schema = TypeSchemaProperty.key.rawValue
registrar.neighborLight(TypesStyle.instances, color: TypesStyle.instancesLight, query: { ":\(isA)(\($0)[\(schema)]):not([\(schema)])" })
registrar.neighborLight(TypesStyle.subtypes, color: TypesStyle.instancesLight, query: { "[\(schema)]:\(isA)(\($0)[\(schema)])" })
```

- **`NeighborsPlugin()`** (id `neighbors`, `PluginID.neighbors`; with `NeighborLight`, the titled,
  colored question, and `NeighborLight.color(light:dark:)`, a color given as one sRGB value for each
  appearance; its point `NeighborLights`, filled with `registrar.neighborLight` and read as
  `registry.neighborLights`; and `NeighborState`, the service; the lists have their own, below)
  registers the service (`editor.neighbors`), which takes the lights from the registry,
  and `registrar.outlines { $0.neighbors?.outlines ?? Outlines() }`; the report's
  line is `neighbors service NeighborState · outlines`, arrows' and mentions' faces'
  `neighbor light · neighbor light`, and types' `neighbor light`. It's after the query plugins in the shipped
  list, and the lights' plugins are after it, and the tab's after theirs. It lights nothing without `QueriesPlugin()` and
  `TopologyPlugin()` (a hover asks nothing then), has nothing to hover without `SelectionPlugin()`,
  and nothing to light without a light; none of them is refused, since it
  contributes to none of their points. A light in a list without Neighbors is refused, as any
  contribution whose point's owner isn't installed is.
- **A light is a title, a color and a question.** `registrar.neighborLight(_:color:query:between:caption:)`
  contributes a `NeighborLight` to the `NeighborLights` point (owner `neighbors`): `title` is what the
  panel heads the light's list with, and `query` is given the selector that names the shape hovered
  or listed (`#`, then its id, as the query language writes one) and returns the query whose matches
  are outlined in that color and listed. `between`, if given, is a query for what runs between the shape
  and those (the arrows): hovering outlines it with them (`NeighborLight.lit` is the two as one
  query), and the panel never lists it. `caption`, if given, is a line under a listed shape's name,
  from the editor, the shape the list is of and the listed one, asked of the rows in view as each is
  drawn, so it reads what's kept, never a board (Mentions': a mentioner's text around its mention).
  Lights are in plugin order, and a plugin's in the
  order it gives them: a shape's first light is its first ring, so the shipped list has arrows' before
  mentions', and types' last. They are the query language's
  ([Queries](#queries)): `:edge-from(X, arrow|stands-for)` is the shapes X has an arrow to, or
  stands for; `:starts-at(X, arrow)` the arrows (connections) that start at X; `:end-of(X, arrow)`
  the shape X ends at, where X is an arrow (and nothing for any other shape), so hovering an arrow
  lights its two ends; the `|` joins edge types, and a type takes in those under it (`arrow` is every
  channel's too). Another
  way to be connected, a new kind of edge, is another light from the plugin that owns the edge, with
  nothing in this module, or in the shipped list's code, changing.
- **The subject** is the shape hovered: `editor.hovered` (the select tool's, or any plugin's where it
  shows shapes), else the shape whose row the pointer is on when the canvas doesn't show it
  (`editor.hoveredElsewhere`, [Selection](#selection): a row of a board nested under its owner's in
  [the table of contents](#the-table-of-contents) sets it). Both are watched with Observation,
  re-armed after each change, and the look at a change is a turn of `editor.scheduler` later, never
  inside the `willSet` Observation tells it in.
- **Asking.** When the subject changes to a shape, any ask still running is let go of (the engine
  looks every 256 shapes, so it stops), and one batch asks the engine
  (`editor.queries.matches`, [Many at once](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)) for every light in
  the view `.resolved` and, where some shape stands in for others, `.literal` too, ids only, up to
  `QueryBudget.maxRows`: one capture, run alongside whatever else is asking the engine, and each text
  checked once. Each light keeps the union of its views. The answer lands a frame or so later, and
  only for the shape asked about (every change of the subject lets go of the ask); a request the
  engine refuses (a shape gone since) lights nothing, and the others still do. From one shape to the
  next, the lights of the first stay until the second's land; when the subject goes, they go at
  once. Without the engine, or Topology, or any light, nothing is asked and nothing is lit.
- **Asking again.** `topology.follow` tells it when a change to the edges touches the subject or a
  shape the last answer matched (a commit's, so an arrow drawn from the hovered shape lights as it's
  drawn, an undo, a file read afresh; or a provide's, a dynamic reference's answer arriving), and it
  asks again, which lets go of an ask under way. A change lists the ends of the edges it changed,
  never the arrow that carries one, so an arrow hovered is asked about again by where it was matched:
  the end it's re-aimed away from, or the pill a provide re-points at its end. A commit asks again
  too when it names the subject other than by moving it (an arrow bound at an end it had none at,
  the undo of a re-aim: the commit changed the arrow's record, and no end of its edge was matched
  before) or adds a shape the answer didn't match: a mention outlives the shape it names, so one of a
  shape deleted before the hover left its edge as it was, and the shape back changes no edge, but is
  what the answer left out (the lights are queries; a new shape may be what one finds). A commit
  whose change to the edges asked already asks no more. A commit that changes the edges of shapes
  the answer didn't match, or only moves shapes, asks nothing. Another board shown clears it: the
  hover is let go of with the switch.
- **Both views.** A reference is a [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding): an arrow into its pill is, in
  the resolved view, an arrow into the shape it stands for, and in the literal view one into the
  pill. Asking each light in both means the pill's own arrows count and so does what it stands for.
  Hovering a note with an arrow into a pill lights the shape (as the graph reads it), the pill (as
  drawn), and the arrow; hovering the shape lights the pill (it stands for it), what has an arrow into
  the pill, and the arrows; hovering the pill lights what it stands for, and, as drawn, what has an
  arrow into it. In a file where nothing stands in the two views are the same edges, and only the
  resolved view is asked.
- **What shows**, worked out when an answer lands and again by a commit that names a shape matched
  or one a match is drawn as (other than by moving it), reaches another board or replaces the
  document, never per frame; any other commit, a drag's every event or a keystroke in an unrelated
  note, costs a look at its change set and a few set intersections. A match on the board shown is
  outlined itself. A match on another board is outlined as the shape on the board shown that holds
  it (`file.shape(on:holding:)`: a subboard's card, the pocket it's in, however many boards down),
  once however many of its shapes match, with one walk up the boards for each board the matches are
  on; one on a board above, which no shape on the board shown holds, is left out. The subject is never
  lit, nor, where the subject isn't on the board shown (a row of another board), the card it's on:
  Selection outlines that card faintly, as a hover is, since that is where the subject is.
- **Rings.** A shape in two lights has a ring for each, in light order: the first light it's in is
  its first ring, the next light's the next, `TintedOutlines.ring`. A group is made for each light and
  ring that has shapes (an arrow is in one light; a note that's both pointed to and pointing back is
  in two, green first, then purple a ring further out), and the core, which knows no meaning, strokes
  them as the outline says ([Outlines](#outlines)): under every other outline, so a selected shape's
  line shows over the tint. A ring is 4 view points further out than the one before (a line 2 wide
  and a gap 2), so their centers are 4, 8 and 12 off a note's edge, whole pixels at 1× and 2×.
  The rest of how it looks is the core's too, for any group: a shape that's selected too has its
  tint one ring further out, clear of the selection's line, which would cover most of ring 0; a lit
  arrow is covered in its color, as wide as its line and a point more, not striped; the hovered
  shape's faint outline is stronger (85%) while anything is lit, so it reads above the lights; and
  Validation's ring stands outside the rings. Nothing is outlined while a session runs, a drag, and what was lit shows
  again when it ends. What's kept is one `Outlines` the core is handed as it is, and the canvas is asked
  for a frame only when a new one differs from the old: an answer that lights nothing, after one that
  lit nothing, draws nothing.
- **What it costs.** A hover is one batch: the main actor reads and resolves its four queries (eight
  where a shape stands in; some 0.02 ms each) and takes up the file in one turn, O(1); the answer is
  off the main actor (some 10 ms for a shape with 10,000 neighbors); the landing joins the views,
  keeps the set of what matched and places each match, O(what's lit and the boards it's on), a hash
  lookup or two each (some 0.8 ms for 10,000). It keeps nothing a commit must follow but what it
  matched and where that is drawn. A frame costs handing the core what's kept; the core strokes only
  what's in view, and looks at the rest's kept extents (10,000 lit in view at 10% add some 7 ms to
  a frame, as ⌘A's rings do; all out of view, some 0.35 ms), and the minimap fills them (some 4 ms
  for 10,000). `./build.sh bench` holds them.
- **The lists.** `NeighborList` (`editor.neighborList`, a service `NeighborDetailsPlugin` registers)
  holds what's connected to the shape a panel shows, in lists: one for each light, in the lights'
  order, each its light's `query` (not `between`: the arrows aren't listed), then two it gives itself
  in the query language's own words for [Topology's](#containment) one tree, Inside (`:has(#id)`: what
  the shape is in, outermost first) and Contains (`#id > *:not(:starts-at(*))`: what's directly in it,
  a frame's shapes or a subboard's board's in no frame, less the connections among them: no list has
  what runs between). So it lists what hovering the shape outlines, less what runs
  between, and knows no kind, edge type or concern. A pointer (Types' `field-link`, a child of
  `mention`) is a mention to the lights, so it's listed under Mentions and Mentioned By as it is lit.
  The **subject** is the shape whose lists are on screen: the panel's view tells the list as it
  appears and goes (`watch`, `unwatch`), so nothing is asked while no list shows (another tab, a hidden
