  inspector, a takeover). One ask for the subject, an ask under way let go of: every folded list is
  only counted (ids, one batch), and every open one is run for its rows (`queries.run`: id, kind,
  title, board and what it's inside, as the engine names them, so Neighbors imports no Titles), all at
  once, each in `.resolved` and, where some shape stands in, `.literal` too, the views' rows merged a
  shape once, as the hover's are; the subject is never listed. A request the engine refuses (a note
  asked what it holds) is an empty list. No list is cut: an open one has every row, up to
  `QueryBudget.maxRows`. The answer lands whole, and until it does the shape before's stays.
- **Asking again** after any commit that did more than move shapes (a name, an edge, a container
  joined or left), once commits have stopped for 100 ms (`NeighborStyle.settle`, on `editor.scheduler`:
  a resize's every event is a commit, so they're one ask), and at once for a change no commit made (a
  provide). A drag costs a look at its change set. An answer that reads as the one shown shows
  nothing (a shape watched again), unless a change to the file asked for it: then every row is drawn
  again, since what a row is called and what its caption quotes are read as it's drawn, from shapes
  the commit may have changed.
- **A row's name** is its title, as the query engine names it. A shape with none is called what the
  table of contents calls it (`ContentsState.name(of:)`: an untitled note's text on one line, "Empty
  Note", a pill by what it stands for), read once for an answer as the row is drawn, and for every row
  by a search's first keystroke; with no table of contents, its kind's name. So Neighbors imports
  TableOfContents, a horizontal in the window, and no Titles.
- **Folding and searching.** Each list folds (by its place among the lists, kept while the editor
  lives, for every shape); a folded list is only counted, and unfolding one whose rows weren't read
  asks. Typed text keeps, in every list, folded or not, the rows whose names match, ranked as every
  list ranks what's typed (FuzzyMatching's `FuzzyMatcher.matches`, the best first, ties in the list's
  order); another shape clears it.
- **The tab.** `NeighborDetailsPlugin()` (id `neighbor-details`) is a plugin value of Neighbors' own,
  after Neighbors and the detail panel in the shipped list, so a list without the panel leaves it out
  and keeps the lights, and one with it and no panel is refused (`ownerNotInstalled`); it needs no
  light and no `NeighborsPlugin()` (the lists are then Inside and Contains). It registers the service
  and one headerless section on every shape (`forEveryShape { $0.details { … } }`,
  `enabledWhileReadOnly`: going to a shape changes nothing of this one) in `NeighborsTab`
  ("Connections", which says no order: it goes where it first appears, after a kind's own tabs and the
  feature tabs of the plugins before it, before Style and a type's Schema). It's always there: a
  tab that came with its lists would come a turn late, so with nothing connected it says "No
  Connections" once the answer is in. The view is a search field once the lists hold 20 shapes in all
  (`NeighborStyle.searchFrom`: more than a panel shows without scrolling), or while something is typed
  (`DetailSearchField`), then, in one `LazyVStack`, each list that has
  shapes: its head (`DetailGroupHeader`: a disclosure triangle, a dot in the light's color, the title and
  the count), which folds it, and its rows (`DetailShapeRow` in a borderless button: the kind's symbol and
  tint, its name, the board it's on when that is neither the board shown nor the shape's own, and the
  light's caption under it), made as they scroll into view, so a list of thousands draws the rows
  in view. A search that finds nothing says "No Matches". A click on a row goes to the shape
  (`editor.goTo`, on the scheduler's next turn: its board first, one step back); the pointer on a row
  hovers the shape (`editor.hovered`, or `hoveredElsewhere` for one the canvas doesn't show, as the
  table of contents' rows do), so it lights that shape's own neighbors. What mentions a shape is under
  Mentioned By ([What mentions a shape](#what-mentions-a-shape)); what stands for a public shape is
  among what points to it, which is where a refused Make Private sends the panel
  ([Publishing](#publishing)).
- **Testing.** NeighborsTests use fixtures only (CanvasTesting's boxes, links as wires, memos as
  what quotes, pockets and corrals, a `Pill` that stands for what it cites and a `Lens` for what's
  provided, and four lights of the tests' own in pure colors, given by a plugin of the tests' own,
  `lightsPlugin`, over a `Star` and a `Nest`); they read
  `editor.outlines.tinted` after `settle()` (a turn of the scheduler, then the run loop until
  `isAsking` says the answer landed): each light's matches in its color, one view asked where nothing
  stands in and two where a shape does, an arrow hovered lighting where it ends and starts, a shape in
  two and three lights in rings, the subject never, a pocket's card for what's on its board and two
  boards down, nothing from a board above, a shape hovered elsewhere (its card faint, never lit), the
  canvas's hover over it, the answer before staying until the next lands, a changed hover letting go
  of the ask (the engine takes up the file once), a switch clearing it, nothing during a session, and
  nothing without the engine; and what keeps it right: asking again when the subject's edges change
  or an edge of what's lit does (a commit, an undo, a provide), when an arrow hovered is re-aimed,
  let go of and bound again or has its end deleted, when a pill is re-pointed at its end, and when a
  shape no answer matched comes (a deleted mention's shape back); not for others' edges or a move;
  working out what shows again, asking nothing, only for a commit that names what's lit or reaches
  another board (a lit shape moved down a board and back, deleted and undone), never for an unrelated
  edit, a restack or a drag; and the canvas drawing again only when what's outlined changed.
  CompositionTests' NeighborsShippedTests hold the four shipped lights as the registry has them
  (arrows' from Arrows, then mentions' from Mentions; none in a list without the three plugins,
  and a list with a light and no Neighbors refused; each face's two queries, and its refusal without
  Neighbors, are held in its owner's tests too, ArrowPortsTests' and MentionsTests' `LightTests`),
  the shipped table of
  contents' rows, a reference and a subboard, an arrow re-aimed while hovered, the colors (each
  appearance's value, 3:1 against its canvas), a lit arrow covered, and the rings drawn at 4 and 8
  points in the app's own editor. BenchmarkTests' NeighborBenchmarks hold a hover on a shape
  with 10,000 neighbors and with ten, and the frames and the minimap with them lit.
  NeighborsTests' `listTests` (`ListTests.swift`) hold the lists over the hover's harness with the panel
  and the tab added, on a small town of notes, memos that quote, a pocket and corrals, driven with
  `watch` as a list appearing does and read with `settleList` (the `ManualScheduler`'s 100 ms, then the
  run loop until nothing is on its way): each light's shapes under its title with the links left out,
  one ask for the six lists, and nothing asked before a list is on screen; Inside outermost first and
  Contains a corral's shapes and a pocket's board; a row's symbol, name, board and caption; a folded
  list counted with no rows read, for the next shape too; searching (the best first, folded lists
  too, cleared with the text and by another shape); upkeep (two commits 60 ms apart one ask, a rename
  in the row, moves asking nothing, an answer a commit asked for shown though it reads the same, a
  deletion and its undo, a provide asking with no commit); a shape with no title called what the table
  of contents calls it; the shape itself never listed; a stand-in listed with what
  it stands for; a row's click (the next turn, across boards, one Back step) and hover; the tab on every
  kind and its refusal without the panel; and, in a `DetailPanelView` in an unshown window, a list
  watched as it appears, a search field from twenty shapes, and 3,000 shapes all there with under 300
  rows drawn. DetailPanelTests' `listRowTests` hold `DetailGroupHeader` and `DetailSearchField`.

## References

References ([`Sources/References`](../Sources/References)) is the horizontal that makes [stand-ins](#stand-ins-forwarding)
something a person can place: the `reference` kind, a pill that stands for another shape anywhere in the
file, so that a shape too many others point at needs no arrow from each. An arrow drawn into the pill is,
for everything that reads the graph (queries, the table of contents, Topology's readers), an arrow into
the shape it stands for; as drawn, it's still into the pill. Only a [public](#publishing) shape can be
stood for. A reference stands for one picked shape (**direct**) or for what a query finds
(**dynamic**): the first match in file order, or with All every one. Words typed that already read as a
query are that query; others are turned into one by the model, live while they're typed
(Natural language, below).
Its registration ([References.swift](../Sources/References/References.swift)):

```swift
registrar.service { ReferenceState(editor: $0) }          // what each stands for now (which name which shape is Topology's)
registrar.overlay(ReferenceButtonOverlay())               // the leading symbol's hover and pressed looks
registrar.canvasButtons(at: { editor, point in … }, click: { button, editor in … })   // the leading symbol goes to the original
registrar.command(.goToOriginal, title: ReferenceStyle.goToOriginal, isEnabled: { … }) { … }  // the panel's button, the menu's item
registrar.command(.interpretReference, title: ReferenceStyle.interpret, isEnabled: { … }) { … }   // the panel's Interpret
registrar.contribute(DetailStatusContribution { shape, context in … }, to: DetailStatuses.self, for: .kind(Reference.kind))   // a warning line where an attached arrow's channel isn't taken
registrar.contextMenuForCanvas { … }                      // Go to Original (direct), Show Matches (dynamic)
registrar.shape(ReferenceDefinition()) { reference in     // ReferenceDefinition: NeverPublic, Editable, CustomSkeleton, DerivedProps
    let place = reference.editingPlacement(size: Reference.defaultSize) { Reference() }
    reference.tool(label: "Reference", systemImage: "arrow.turn.up.right", shortcut: "r", placing: place)
    reference.portsOnEveryChannel(sides: [.left, .right])  // what it takes is what it stands for ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in))
    reference.standsIn(maxTargets: 50, admitting: { target, registry in registry.isPublic(target) },
                       needs: "public",                // a message says "only a public shape can be stood for"
                       fulfilling: { record, registry in registry.makePublic(&record) },
                       calls: { shape, _ in shape.props.target?.label ?? (shape.props.mode == .dynamic ? shape.props.text : nil) },
                       makes: { props, target, label in ReferenceEdits.pick(&props, ReferenceTarget(id: target, label: label)) }) { shape, _ in
        if let target = shape.props.target { return .shapes([target.id]) }
        if let query = shape.props.query { return .provided(ReferenceState.key(query: query, all: shape.props.all)) }
        return nil
    }
    reference.referenceRow()                               // the table of contents
    reference.referencePanel()                             // its header; Go to Original, or the Query and Matches sections
    reference.contextMenu { … }                            // Match All, Match First: a step each
    reference.validate(ignoringMoves: true) { shape, context in … }   // a query the engine can't read: a warning in its words
}
```

- **The props** (`Reference`): `frame` (32 tall, the width stored and fitted), `target: ReferenceTarget?`
  (`{id, label}`, a [name](#values-that-name-shapes), not a binding: it crosses boards, outlives its shape,
  is kept by cut and paste and by a copy that doesn't take the shape along, and renamed by one that does),
  `words`, `query: String?` (format `x-canvas-query`, so `canvas draw` refuses one the engine can't read)
  and `all`. `target` and `words` are `readOnly()`, so a script can't write them, and the kind has no
  title, so `canvas kinds` lists it with no edges. The mode is derived, never stored: a target makes it
  direct, words or a query make it dynamic, else it's empty. `ReferenceEdits` writes it: each of `pick`,
  `find(words:query:)` and `clear` keeps one mode and refits the width to what the pill now says. The
  v0 fixture, `Fixtures/kinds/reference.v0.json`, pins every member.
- **Made by name.** `makes` is how `canvas draw` makes a direct reference (`registry.standIns.make`): the
  pill's own writer, `ReferenceEdits.pick`, with the shape's id and the name its title folds to, so it's
  fitted to its label as a picked one is. An edge to a public shape on another board puts one beside the
  shape on this board ([draw](#draw)); a script still can't write `target` or `words`, nor name the pill.
- **What it stands for** (`ReferenceState.state(of:)`, a `ReferenceCondition`, derived from the props and
  the file, never stored; the render works it out through its own context, and the service keeps a
  direct pill's from frame to frame until a commit changes it or what it names): live (the shape is there,
  public and mentionable), not public (there, but not public: nothing is forwarded), missing (in no
  board: the name it holds), not available (in the file on a board the app can't show), and, for words,
  not interpreted, interpreting (the model is being asked), failed, or nothing to interpret them with; for a query, being found, found (`ReferenceFound`: all or first, the count, the
  matches given, the first's appearance), no matches, refused (in the engine's words), failed (past
  the deadline: Retry), or nothing to ask (no engine installed). Which references name which shape is
  Topology's, which keeps it for every board the app can show (`standIns(naming:)`, the references
  among them by `standInKind(of:)`), so a rename, a change of publicness or a deletion remakes the right
  rows, and a commit of thousands of shapes and no reference costs a dictionary hit each. The state
  keeps which shapes each row read its path from (below, the table of contents), noted as the
  row is made, so a frame or a board's owner renamed or put somewhere else remakes the rows whose
  paths it's in, and no other.
- **What a dynamic reference finds** (`ReferenceAnswers.swift`). `ReferenceState` keeps every reference
  with a query on a board the app can show (from `ChangeSet`, other boards and boards added and removed
  included; read afresh for a file put in place; Topology takes no answer for one on a board it can't
  show) and asks the engine for them: one `queries.matches` batch, on one
  snapshot, for every one whose answer may be out of date and that isn't being typed into, each on the
  **recorded** view (what direct references forward, never another dynamic one's answer), admitting
  public shapes alone (`editor.publishing.admitting`) and counting apart those that would be once
  made public (`holdingBack: editor.publishing.admittable`), eight matches for a first-match one (what All
  would add, for its panel) and fifty for an All one. When: its own question changed (its query or flag,
  a gesture or an undo), at once, on the scheduler's next turn; any other commit but a move, after
  250 ms of quiet (`ReferenceStyle.settle`, each commit waiting again, on `editor.scheduler`); a commit
  that only moved shapes, never (one test). A plan that reads the person (`editorWords`) isn't asked:
  it's refused, “`:selected` can’t be used here.” (`queries.checkStored`, Queries' one gate for a
  stored query, which the reference's draft, its warning and `canvas draw` go through too). An answer lands only for the question the record
  asks now and only if no older than the latest that landed for it (kept per key), and goes to Topology
  in one `provide` (the first match, or up to fifty), then, if it says something new (every quiet asks
  every reference again, and most answers are what they were), the pills (`setNeedsDisplay`), panels
  (observed per reference) and rows (`contentsDidChange(for:)`) are told. A title or id no shape has,
  or a container that can't hold shapes, is no matches, saying why; the deadline is a failure that
  Retry asks again. The last four answers of each reference are kept by key, so an undo, a redo or an
  All toggled back shows its answer at once (provided from a hop of the scheduler, exempt from the
  stale rule, then asked again). They are kept past the reference's deletion (for its undo), but for
  at most 256 references (`ReferenceStyle.memosKept`): the least recently landed or used gives way, so a
  long session's deleted references don't pile up. It's one of Topology's settle sources (busy while a wait is armed, a
  hop is due or a batch is out), so `canvas query` right after a draw waits for it, and "Finding…"
  shows only once a batch has been out 250 ms.
- **The pill** (`ReferenceStyle`): a capsule 32 tall, a leading symbol (the kind's, tinted, or a
  magnifier for every dynamic one, or a dashed square for what's gone), the label (14 medium, one line;
  a dynamic one's words, never its matches' names), and what trails (the eye of a shape gone private,
  and of a query whose every match isn't public;
  the first match's kind symbol in its tint, an All one's count in a capsule, "50+" past fifty, a "0"
  for none or a refusal, the warning for a failure); filled and bordered, or, when it stands for
  nothing, a dashed border with no fill and the label in italic at two thirds; while it's looked for,
  solid with its words at half. A pill whose shape is on another board than its own says that board's
  name after the shape's, gray, in what room the width leaves (`ReferenceEdits.pick(_:_:board:)` fits
  the width to it for a pick from another board's list; written without, the width is the name's
  alone). Its width keeps room for what may trail it (a dynamic one's count, a
  direct one's eye or warning), so nothing that comes and goes refits it or cuts a short name short.
  Zoomed out it's one square fill. Labels and symbols are memoized, symbols as bitmaps, so a frame of a
  thousand pills builds none.
- **Typing** (`ReferenceEditor`): the Reference tool places an empty pill and edits it, in a step named
  "Add Reference" (an existing pill's is "Edit Reference", `Editable.editingStepName`): one line over the
  pill, in an `NSView` framed in view points with its bounds in world units, as an arrow's label editor is,
  its text where the render's label is (so nothing moves when editing starts) and the render drawing no
  label meanwhile. Each change is written as words with the width refitted (64 to 280, growing rightward,
  room kept for a count whenever it's words); Return, ⌘Return and a click away end it, ⇧Return does
  nothing, pasted newlines are spaces and the text is at most 200 characters. Under the field, a list of
  the public shapes (`ReferencePicker`, a headless model on TextEditing's `CaretList`, in a
  `CaretListWindow` like every caret list: `PublicShapes: MentionScope`, so the candidates are the `@`
  picker's, ranked as it ranks them, with the recent picks and the shapes nearby for nothing typed) with
  the words as typed always the last row, set off by a line (`CaretListItem.separated`); the first shape is
  highlighted, but the one a pill already stands for while the text is as the field opened. Return or Tab
  on a shape's row, or a click on it, picks it (`ReferenceEdits.pick`: it stands for the shape, the words and
  query let go of, the width fit to its name) and ends editing; Return on the words row, or ⌥Return on
  any, commits the words (words that read as a query, `queries.check`'s, are that query, canonical, in
  the same step: no model asked; a query the model wrote for exactly these words while they rested is
  written in the same step too; for others the model is asked, below); Escape closes the list and a second leaves the field,
  where changed text is kept as the pill's words (nothing is picked implicitly), and typing opens the list
  again. Once only the words row is left (the hand-off to natural language) the pill leads with the
  magnifier while it's edited. A new pill left empty is discarded inside its step
  (`Editable.discardsWhenEditingEnds`), and unchanged text makes no step. A scope that admits few shapes
  ranks only its members (`MentionState` keeps each scope's members as entries are read), so a keystroke
  costs what matches, not the board.
- **Natural language** (`ReferenceInterpreting.swift`, design 7.3, decision D9): live, once only the
  words row is left (`ReferencePicker.isHandoff`) and the text has rested `ReferenceStyle.interpretDelay`
  (600 ms on `editor.scheduler`, every keystroke starting the wait again and cancelling a call that is out),
  `editor.queryTranslator.translate(words, about: .reference)` is asked, so the query is one a reference
  can run (reads only the file, titles right, repaired once). Its answer is the reference's **draft**
  in `ReferenceState`, never in the document: the panel shows the words, the query, its status and its
  matches as they arrive (one extra `matches` request, which provides nothing, so nothing is forwarded);
  text that already reads as a query is a draft at once, with no model. At commit (Return on the words
  row, ⌥Return, or leaving with text) a draft that has landed for exactly these words is written in the
  editing step itself, no second call; a call still out when editing ends is not cancelled by it: it
  lands later as an undo step of its own, "Interpret" (`editor.transact(on: board, "Interpret")` in a
  task continuation, never inside undo), only if the reference is still there with the same words and no
  query and isn't read-only (a locked one is let be: no step, no shake, not interpreted, and Interpret
  is offered once it's unlocked); words committed before they rested are asked about when editing ends.
  Nothing asks on undo, redo, paste, `canvas draw` or open; undoing "Interpret" leaves the words,
  not interpreted, with Interpret offered in the panel (a borderless `DetailCommandButton(command:
  .interpretReference, systemImage: "sparkles")`, titled as the command is, in the status line's place,
  dimmed while it's locked). Editing the pill again,
  a keystroke, deleting it, undoing past its words, or the file closing cancels the call (`ReferenceState`
  goes with its editor and cancels what it has out, the model's call, the draft's request, the batch and every
  timer, as an `isolated deinit`; the editor goes while a call is out because `QueryTranslator` holds it only
  weakly across the call). A failure
  is said quietly (the pill dashed with a warning, "Interpreting" solid with its words dimmed): "No API key"
  or "Key rejected" with "Open Settings…" (`AnthropicSettingsView.showSettings()`, as a type's sync's),
  "Rate limited", "Can’t reach Anthropic", "Timed out" or any other of the model's own with "Retry", "No
  query for these words" (declined or unanswerable) with "Retry", "Unusable answer" (a repair that still
  refused); a key saved in Settings (`languageModelKeyDidChange`) asks again what failed for want of one.
- **Ports.** A reference has ports on every channel on its left and right, but what a person drags
  from and what ends on it is what it stands for ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in)): a drag
  from a note ends on a pill that stands for a note and not on one that stands for a frame, and
  an arrow re-aimed onto one obeys the same rule. A pill that stands for a subboard has a subboard's
  dots and links: indigo, and a `subboard-link` to a subboard. A pill that stands for nothing has no
  dots and takes nothing. Arrows keep their bindings when it is re-pointed; if an arrow attached to it is on a
  channel the new targets don't take, a warning triangle trails the pill (where a dynamic one's count
  will be) and the panel says `“Order” doesn’t take note links.` (`ReferenceState.channelMismatch(of:)`,
  kept for each reference until its edges change, never worked out per frame).
- **Going to the original**: the leading symbol is a [canvas button](#canvas-buttons) (hovered, an accent
  arrow; a click goes as following a mention does, one step back, the pill not selected first), and the
  same command is the context menu's first item and the panel's plain "Go to Original" button, which work
  on a locked reference too. A dynamic one's symbol goes to what it stands for, and its menu has Show
  Matches (every match its header counts, selected: a reference given fewer, eight for a first-match
  one or fifty, asks its query for every one first) and Match All or Match First.
- **The panel of a dynamic reference**: the header's line says how many it found ("First of 7", "12
  matches", "50 of 73", "No matches", "Not public" when what it found is all not public; nothing while
  it's looked for). The Query section has the query,
  read-only and colored as code, one line per line, scrolling sideways (`DetailCodeEditor`), a status
  line only when there's something to say ("Interpreting…", "Finding…", a refusal, "Too slow" or a failed
  interpretation with its action, "Unavailable", or what it found that isn't public, "12 not public",
  with Make Public, which makes every one public, on whichever board, in one step), the Interpret button
  for words nobody has asked about, and `LabeledContent("Match") { DetailCheckbox("All", …) }`, a step of its own. The
  Matches section, while it found shapes (its draft's too, while its words are typed), is a
  `DetailShapeRow` per match (the board's name where it
  isn't the board shown; in first mode the rows after the first dimmed, what All would add) and "and
  42 more" past eight; a click goes to one, the pointer hovers it on the canvas.
- **Validation**: a query the engine can't read (pasted, or written into a board by hand) is a warning
  in the engine's words, on `query`; what it finds or doesn't is the pill's to show, never an issue.
- **The table of contents**: its row is what it stands for (a dimmed placeholder where it stands for
  nothing), remade when the shape it names changes. A reference to a shape that's there (public or
  not) says where it is before its name, "Draw › Points › DrawPoints.swift" (`ContentsLabel`'s
  `path:`): the shapes its original is inside, outermost first (Topology's `ancestors(of:)`: the
  frames it's in, the owner of its board, the frames that one is in, and so on up, the root never
  one), less those the reference is inside too (`ReferenceState.rowPath(of:to:)`), so a row says
  only where the shape is from where the reference is: nothing for a shape in the same frame or on
  the same board, or above it, and rows for shapes from the same place read alike. Each is called
  as Boards calls a container in a path (`registry.containerName(of:)`, which is why References
  imports Boards), an untitled one by what its kind is called, fainter. The reference's own row is where it is, as any shape's: in a frame, under the
  frame's row. `rowsAffected(by:)` names the rows whose path was read from a shape a commit
  changed (`pathSources`, the core's `ReverseIndex`, O(what changed); a move names none), and PathTests hold it. An arrow that starts at a reference nests under the
  shape the reference stands for when that's on the same board ([Arrows' arrow row](#the-table-of-contents),
  generic over stand-ins), else under the reference.
- **Tests.** ReferencesTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes and tiles as what it stands for (its `makes` too, through `registry.standIns`: a reference made for a public shape, fitted, standing for it once inserted, and for nothing where the shape isn't public); CompositionTests'
  `referencesShippedTests` the shipped pieces (an arrow drawn by hand into a pill, in the graph and a query, nesting, a drag
  ending on a pill for a note and not on one for a frame, copy, cut and paste, `canvas draw`, a drawn query read through by a
  query that waits for it); `ReferenceBenchmarks` a frame of a thousand pills, a keystroke in the list
  over a board of ten thousand shapes of which twenty are public, and twenty dynamic references answered after a commit.

## The command line

`canvas` is the app's command line, for agents first and people too: it runs commands on the
boards open in the app, which must be running, and each change shows in the board's window as it's
made. Agents never read or write a board's file; they go through `canvas`, so the file stays the
app's to change.

```
canvas status                           whether the app is running: its version, protocol and boards
canvas boards                           the open boards: each one's id, name, file, which is in front, and what it shows
canvas new <file>                       a new board's file, made and opened
canvas draw <script>|- [--dry-run] [--reveal] [--board <board>]
                                        shapes, and the edges between them, made, changed or deleted by a script, all at once
canvas kinds [<kind>] [--schema]        what a script can draw, and with what
canvas measure <script>|-               how big a script's shapes would be, and what the placement is done with, drawing nothing
canvas query <query>|- [--limit <number>] [--count] [--brief] [--fields <attribute>]… [--board <board>]
                                        the shapes of a file a query matches, on every board, in file order
canvas query --ask <question>|- […]     the same, the query written by the app's language model
canvas query-vocabulary                 what this app's queries can name: kinds and their attributes, edge types, words
canvas help [<command>]                 what a command takes (--format json: what the app says, schemas too)
```

The modules, one job each:

| Module | Layer | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| CanvasRPC | core (the wire) | What the app and `canvas` say to each other: JSON-RPC 2.0, a message a line, over a Unix-domain socket (`~/Library/Application Support/InfiniteCanvas/canvas.sock`, or `CANVAS_SOCKET`) only this user can reach; what a command is (`CommandSpec`, its params a JSON Schema) and how its params are spelled as arguments; the client, and the listener, which answers each request as a main-actor task of its own (one that waits holds up neither the main actor nor another connection), each connection's answers in the order its requests came, and cancels the requests still running (not notifications) once its client hangs up. Knows no canvas, plugin or AppKit. |
| CanvasCLI | app | `canvas`: reads its own options, asks the app what it runs (`describe`), reads the rest as one of those commands, runs it, and prints what comes back. Knows only the wire. |
| CanvasUI's `CommandServer` | app | The app's end: it listens, describes the app, and answers each request on the main actor. `status`, `boards` and `new` (a new board's file, saved as Save As saves one, `BoardDocument.newFile(at:)`, then opened) are its own; it runs the rest on the board a request names (`--board`: an id, a file or a name), or the one in front, on the board inside that file its window shows, each in a task kept against its board, and a board command's result, when it's an object, gains `board: {id, name, shows, showsPath}`, as `boards` lists it, read in the command's own job just before it runs, so an agent sees which board it worked on (a command that knows better says `shows` and `showsPath` in a `board` object of its own, which the server completes: a query's is the board shown as it took up the file). A client gone is answered `cancelled`, and a board closed (`BoardDocument.close()`) answers its running commands `board_closed`, at once, their tasks cancelled and what they return later dropped. |
| Automation | platform | The commands plugins give the command line (`AutomationCommands`), its own four, `draw`, `kinds` and `measure` (each resolving its board, calling the draw engine (Draw) and saying its `DrawError` as the wire's `AutomationError`) and `show`, which borrows Draw's naming. The app's server takes them from [the host's slot for them](#host-slots) (`registry.hostCommands`, async), which this plugin fills. |
| Colors | platform | The color a shape of a kind that opted in holds ([Colors](#colors)): the property, the built-in names and a file's own, the book that says what every color looks like, the panel's row, `/color`, Color ▸, and the words draw and queries take; what a color looks like is [Palette](#palette)'s. |
| Draw | platform | The engine of `canvas draw`, `measure` and `kinds` ([draw](#draw)), and the nine points it takes what it doesn't own from (`DrawNames`, `DrawLabels`, `DrawEdges`, `DrawEdgeIdentities`, `DrawChecks`, `DrawTextFormats`, `DrawValueWriters`, `DrawReports`, `DrawGroups`): an engine, so any plugin may run it, and it knows no horizontal. Its placement for plugins is here too (`Surroundings`, `Landing`: where a box of shapes lands on a board, beside a shape, in a frame or anywhere, placed as `draw` places one ([Moving](#moving)); Moving's solver, for any plugin that puts shapes down). It checks a query a property holds with Queries, reads which kinds stand in for others with Topology, and how far a title row reaches with Adornments; its error, `DrawError`, is not a wire type (Automation says it as the wire's `AutomationError`), and its mark is `draw engine`. |
| DrawScript | core | The language `draw` reads (`Script(parsing:)`), the solver that places what it says (`LayoutProblem.solve()`), and the grid its obstacles are filed in (`ObstacleGrid`: boxes only, which any plugin may use to place a shape among others): pure, it knows no canvas, registry, kind or plugin. |
| FuzzyMatching | core | What's typed matched against text ([FuzzyMatching](#fuzzymatching)): `FuzzyMatcher` (every list's tiers), `TextSearch` (Find's, over folded texts) and `PathMatcher` (Jump To's, over containment paths): pure, it knows no canvas, registry or plugin. |
| JumpTo | platform | Jump To (⌘K, [Jump To](#jump-to)): a palette that goes to a shape by its title and where it is, over Titles' titles and the containment tree; no kind opts into it, and nothing imports it. |
| Moving | platform | `/move-to` and `/move-near` ([Moving](#moving)): the shape typed in moved into a frame, onto a subboard's board or beside a shape, on any board, placed with Draw's placement for plugins (DrawScript's solver, over `ObstacleGrid`) as `draw` places a shape; no kind opts into it, and nothing imports it. |
| Neighbors | platform | Hover a shape and what it's connected to is outlined by how ([Neighbors](#neighbors)), and select one and its panel's Connections tab lists them by the same ways, then what it's inside and what it holds (`NeighborDetailsPlugin`, on DetailPanel, its search ranked by FuzzyMatching, a shape with no title called as TableOfContents calls it): its lights are titles, colors and the queries that find their shapes, each contributed by the plugin that owns the edges (Arrows' `ArrowLightsPlugin`, Mentions' `MentionLightsPlugin`, Types' `TypeLightsPlugin`), asked of Queries, placed on the board shown by the file's boards (`shape(on:holding:)`), hovered on the canvas or in the table of contents (Selection's `hovered` and `hoveredElsewhere`). |
| Palette | core | The color math ([Palette](#palette)): a color as sRGB and OKLCH (`RGB`, `OKLCH`), the seven roles one color is drawn in on the light canvas and the dark (`Swatch`, each a `Tone`), contrast, and the one test for a dark appearance: pure, it knows no canvas, registry, plugin or named color. |
| QueryCommands | platform | `query` and `query-vocabulary`, and `--ask` as a call to QueryTranslation's translator, its errors said as the wire's (on Automation, Queries, QueryTranslation and the wire; it declares no point). |
| QueryLanguage | core | The language `query` reads (`SelectorList(parsing:)`) and its canonical form: pure, it knows no canvas, registry or plugin. |
| Queries | platform | The engine that answers a query about a file ([Queries](#queries)), and its points: an engine, so any plugin may run a query; it gives the selection's word itself (`SelectionQueriesPlugin`, `:selected`), as Selection is below it. |
| QueryTranslation | platform | English into a query: `AskStyle`, `AskRequest`, `AskAnswer`, and the translator (`editor.queryTranslator`, `QueryTranslationPlugin(prompt:referenceRule:style:)`) that `--ask` and the app both ask, `ask` (run what it wrote) and `translate` (only check it, for a query stored to be run later); it declares no point (on Canvas, LanguageModels, Queries and QueryLanguage). |

**The commands are the app's, so `canvas` never changes for one.** It knows no command but `help`:
each run asks the app to describe itself, and makes its commands, their arguments and their help
from what comes back. A plugin that adds a command adds it to `canvas`, help and all, and the two
can't disagree about what a command takes. The app carries the `canvas` it was built with
(`Contents/Helpers/canvas`; `build/canvas` links to it), along with the skills that teach agents to use it (`Contents/Resources/agents`, a Claude Code plugin marketplace; `canvas install` puts them in `~/.agents/skills`, for the agents that follow the Agent Skills standard, and links `canvas` onto the PATH), and `canvas` refuses an app that speaks
another version of the protocol (`RPC.protocolVersion`: 2, in which text may be read from standard
input, and an error may say where in a script it is).

**A command is a name, its params, and what it does**, registered with Automation, as `draw` is
([Commands.swift](../Sources/Automation/Commands.swift), its params in
[Params.swift](../Sources/Automation/Params.swift), over the engine in
[Draw.swift](../Sources/Draw/Draw.swift)):

```swift
struct DrawParams: SchemaDefined {
    static let properties = Properties<DrawParams>(title: "draw") {
        Property("script", \.script).required().keywords(["x-stdin": true, "x-value-name": "script"])
            .description("What to draw: one statement a line (a shape, an edge, a delete, a group or a style), in quotes for the shell.")
        Property("dryRun", \.dryRun).description("Work everything out and say what would happen, changing nothing.")
        Property("reveal", \.reveal).description("Then ease the view to what was drawn.")
    }
    var script = ""
    var dryRun = false
    var reveal = false
}

registrar.automationCommand("draw", "Draw shapes on a board, and connect them, from a script.", discussion: "…",
                            params: DrawParams.self, positionals: ["script"],
                            examples: [CommandExample(#"canvas draw 'edge "API" -> "DB"'"#, "Connect the two.")]) { params, context throws(AutomationError) in
    let editor = try context.board()    // the board --board names, or the one in front
    do throws(DrawError) {
        return try draw(script: params.script, dryRun: params.dryRun, reveal: params.reveal, program: "canvas", in: editor)
    } catch {
        throw AutomationError(error)    // the engine's error, as the wire's
    }
}
```

- **Params are a list of properties** ([Properties](#properties)), whose JSON Schema is what
  `canvas` reads the arguments by: a string as it's typed, a number or an integer read as one, a
  boolean a flag (`--dry-run`, `--no-dry-run`), a fixed number of numbers (the core's point and
  size) as `x,y`, an array of any of those by giving the option again, and anything else as JSON
  (`-` reads it from standard input). Text whose schema says `"x-stdin": true`, as `draw`'s script
  does, is read from standard input when it's given as `-`, and help writes it `<script>|-`: a
  script quoted for the shell breaks at its first apostrophe. Each property is an option (`dryRun`
  is `--dry-run`), those in `positionals` also take their places in order, and help shows each
  one's `description`, its default, and what `x-value-name` calls its value. A param whose schema
  says `"x-timeout": N` (`Property(…).keywords(["x-timeout": 60])`, `--ask`'s) makes `canvas` wait
  up to N seconds for the answer when it's given (`CommandArgument.waits`): a call waits
  `--timeout`, else the longest such wait among the params given, else 10 s, and help says "(waits
  up to N s)". Text whose schema says `"x-path": true` (`new`'s file) is a file named from where
  `canvas` runs, which it sends whole (`CommandArgument.isPath`), since the app runs elsewhere. The app checks what comes against the schema and decodes it, so `run` gets its
  params typed.
- **A board command** (the default scope) runs on a board: `context.board()` is its editor. An app
  command (`scope: .app`, as `kinds` is) runs with the registry. A board command with `boardOptional: true`
  (`measure`) runs on the board named, in front or the only one open, else on none (`context.editor` is
  nil), and help says its `--board` defaults to the board in front, if any. `board` is the server's param, and
  `canvas`'s own options (`socket`, `format`, `timeout`, `help`, `version`) are `canvas`'s, so the
  registry refuses a command that declares one; a name the command line can't type (words of
  lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: `draw`, `board list`) or one that's kept
  (`RPC.reservedCommandNames`: the protocol's `describe`, the server's `status`, `boards` and `new`,
  `canvas`'s `help`); a positional that isn't a param; and two commands of one name.
- **An error says why, and what to do**: `AutomationError(message, reason:, hint:)`, where `reason`
  is a word an agent can branch on (`unknown_kind`) and `hint` is often the command, or the line,
  to write instead; a name that's nearly one gets a "did you mean". An error about a script or a
  query says where: `line:` (from 1), `column:` (from 1, in characters) and `length:` (in
  characters) of what's wrong on it, and `statement:` (that line as written: `draw`'s trimmed, its
  comment left out; a query's whole, so the column counts from its start); and a command that finds
  several problems at once throws the first, with every one in `errors:`. Anything else an agent
  can use goes in `details:` (`--ask`'s `transient`, the `query` a model wrote), under names of the
  command's own: a detail named like one of the error's members (`reason`, `message`, `hint`,
  `line`, `column`, `length`, `statement`, `errors`) is left out, whether the error has that member
  or not. They reach `canvas` as the error's data (`line`, `column`, `length`, `statement`, the
  details beside them, and `errors`, each `{line, column, length, statement, reason, message,
  hint}` and its details), which it prints beside its own members in JSON, never over them, and as
  text as `canvas: line 3, column 12: <message>`, the statement indented, carets under the columns
  it names, as a terminal draws them (a tab before them stays a tab, and an emoji or a CJK character
  takes two cells: `Invocation.caret(under:column:length:)`), the hint, then
  a line for each further problem. `canvas` prints a result on standard output (JSON when that isn't a terminal,
  which is how agents run it, or text, whose tables lead with `line`, `did`, `id`, `name`, `kind`
  and `title`, those a table has, end with sentences
  (a warning's `message`), which they never cut, and list what a row has that isn't a value (a
  kind's attributes) under it; `--format` says which), an error on standard error, and exits 0
  when it's done, 1 when the app couldn't do it, 2 when the command line is wrong (standard input
  that can't be read, or isn't UTF-8, included), and 3 when the app couldn't be reached or didn't
  answer in time. The app doesn't drop a request it's slow to answer: after a timeout
  (`timed_out`) it may still do it, so check before running it again.
- **A command changes a board as anything does**: through `editor.transact`, on the main actor, so
  the window shows each change, the board is edited and saves itself, read-only shapes refuse, and
  services hear the change set; its commit is an undo step of its own, named as the command names
  its transaction (`transact("Draw")`). Who made a change is recorded only as whether an agent did:
  a command that changes the board for one says so (`transaction.byAgent = true`, as `draw` does),
  and its commit carries it (`ChangeSet.byAgent`), so a service that acts on a person's edits
  leaves it be (a type's sync, which would ask a language model, takes what an agent wrote
  as in step). An agent's name on its commits is still to come.

**A file's boards.** A file can hold boards inside its shapes ([Boards in a
file](#boards-in-a-file)); a command works on the one its window shows, `editor.board`, as the
window does: `document`, `transact` and the undo step its change makes are that board's (a `draw`
is one step, Draw, there, and undoing it from another board shows that one first). `canvas boards`
says which, for each open file: `shows`, the board shown (`"root"`, or the id of the shape that
owns it, as a `BoardID` is written), `showsPath`, the boards from the root down to it, `shapes`,
how many it holds, `fileShapes`, how many the file holds, on every board, and `view`, the room its
window has for a board fit into it (`[width, height]` in points: what a first visit fits the root
board's shapes into, whichever board the window shows, so what a tool that lays a board out shapes
it for; left out while the window has no size); `canvas status` names the front file's as
`frontmostShows`; and a board command's result names it in its `board` (`id`, `name`, `shows`,
`showsPath`, as `boards` has them), read in the command's own job as it starts: a command that
doesn't wait (`draw`) runs in that job, so no switch of board comes between the two. A
[query](#query) says where it ran itself, the board shown as it took up the file
(`QueryResult.shown` and `shownPath`, `:current-board`'s), which may be later than its request (it
waits for answers to settle, and `--ask` waits on the model), and the server completes that
`board` with the file's `id` and `name`. A query reads every board of the file the app can show,
whichever the window shows, and names each row's board (`board`, and `inside`, the path's names
for the boards it's inside). A `draw` never names a board either: it works out the one it draws on
from what its script names (Draw's `Drawing.board(for:in:)`: a title names a shape on any board of
the file the app can show, the board shown's first; a new shape goes on the board of what it's
placed against, or the one `in "X"` names, the board X holds, or, for X a [container](#containers)
on its board (a frame), the board X is on; with neither, the board shown), reads that board
through the core's `editor.reading(of:)` (a `BoardReading`: its shapes, a `ShapeContext` and paint
order over them, and the view it would be shown with, a first visit's fit included), and commits
there with `transact(on:)`, the window staying where it is; a script that lands on two boards is
`several_boards`, since a run is one transaction and one undo step, made on one board, but for an
edge between shapes on two, which goes through a [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding) for the end
that a kind can be made to stand for ([Edges through a stand-in](#draw)): such an end claims its
board only softly, so the run draws on the first hard claim, else on the board of the first such
edge's start; one already drawn through a stand-in claims the board the stand-in is on, hard, and
a shape the script draws, which is on the board the run draws on, claims none. One that would put
a shape or an edge on a board that can't change (a locked subboard's, and every board under it) is
`read_only`. Its result's `on` says which (`board`, that shape's `title`, `shown`). `canvas show
"<title>"` (or `--root`) moves the window, through `editor.showBoard`, and says where it is in a
`board` of its own, which the server completes.

The app that holds the socket's lock (`canvas.sock.lock`, beside it) is the one listening: a second
copy of the app gives up and runs without the command line, and a socket that one that crashed left
behind is taken over. A command's options may also come before its name
(`canvas --board 2 draw - < plan.txt`), as agents often write them.

### A command may be async

A command that waits on something (a language model's answer, a query answered off the main actor)
answers later: `runAsync:` in place of `run:`, its output `Encodable & Sendable`
([Automation.swift](../Sources/Automation/Automation.swift)), as [`query`](#query) does
([QueryCommands.swift](../Sources/QueryCommands/QueryCommands.swift)):

```swift
registrar.automationCommand("query", "Find the shapes of a file that a query matches, …", discussion: "…",
                            params: QueryParams.self, positionals: ["query"], examples: […],
                            runAsync: { (params: QueryParams, context: AutomationContext) async throws(AutomationError) -> JSON in
                                try await query(params, in: context, asking: asking)   // its answer built as JSON, off the main actor
                            })
```

- **It runs on the main actor, awaiting**, and the main actor is free while it waits: the listener
  answers each request as a task of its own, and `CommandServer` runs each command in a task kept
  against its board, so a command that waits holds up neither drawing nor another connection's
  commands. On one connection only the answers keep their order: a `draw` sent after a query may run
  before the query's answer comes.
- **Its output is written as JSON off the main actor** (`AutomationCommand.encoded`, `@concurrent`,
  handed the output whole, `consume`), where it's freed too, so a large one costs the main actor
  neither its writing nor its freeing. One that's the wire's `JSON` already passes through as it is
  (what the core writes is one: its `JSONValue` is the wire's `JSON`; `query` builds its answer
  member by member, off the main actor).
  `run:` is unchanged: it never suspends, and answers in the turn it's asked in, as `draw` and
  `kinds` do. Write the `runAsync:` label out: a trailing closure that doesn't await picks `run:`.
- **It may be cancelled.** `canvas` hanging up (its timeout, ^C) cancels the request's task,
  answered `cancelled`, which nobody reads; closing its file answers it `board_closed` ("The board
  was closed before the command finished.") at once, and cancels it. What a cancelled command
  returns later is dropped, so a long wait looks at `Task.isCancelled` (a query does every 256
  shapes and before every slice; a model's call is cancelled at once). Every command, `draw`
  included, runs one main-actor hop after its request, so one cancelled, or whose file closed, before
  it starts never runs.
- **`canvas` waits as long as its params say**: the longest `x-timeout` among those given (`--ask`'s
  60 s), else 10 s, unless `--timeout` says ([above](#the-command-line)). The protocol stays 2: a
  param's `x-timeout`, and an error's `column` and `length`, are what an older `canvas` passes over
  (it waits 10 s, and says `timed_out`). `Registry.runAutomationCommand(_:params:editor:)` and
  `registry.hostCommands`' `run` are async, and a test awaits them with TestKit's `awaitResult`.

### draw

`draw` is how an agent puts things on a board. It reads a script in a small language whose idea is
[reladraw](https://github.com/reladraw/reladraw)'s (Apache-2.0; the attribution is in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), and the language isn't called that): each
line says what a shape is, what it's called and where it sits against shapes already named, never
at coordinates, and the app works out only the distances.
A shape has two sizes in a run: the one it stores (what `size:` writes and what a run compares, so a
shape grown by a type is not settled again) and the room it takes, the frame its kind lays it out in
(`LaidOutBox`). The layout places the room, a row's `at` reports it, and the record is written at the
size it stores.

```
sticky-note "Web" text: "Browser app"
sticky-note "API" right of "Web" text: "Public HTTP API"
subboard "Payments" below "API"
edge "Web" -> "API"
```

A shape's title is its name. A statement about a title the board has changes that shape (only what
it says, and it moves only with a placement), and one about a title it doesn't makes a new one. A
shape that has no title is named by its id, in the query's spelling (`edge "Checkout" ->
#7C1E2A04-4B9E-4E0C-9D8C-5B0E7F3A2C11`), wherever a statement names a shape the file already has:
an id never makes a shape, and a run's rows say the ids of the shapes the file has (`id`, and
`fromId` and `toId` for an edge's ends named so). A
gap is a minimum among the shapes the script places; shapes already on the board stay put, and
are kept clear of; and whatever is ambiguous (an axis nothing settles, two shapes with nothing to
hang on, two that would overlap with nothing saying which side either sits on) is refused rather
than guessed. A placement is worked out once: the board keeps positions, never `right of "API"`.
The language itself, every construct and every refusal, is written for agents in the canvas skill
([`.claude/skills/canvas`](../.claude/skills/canvas/SKILL.md): `SKILL.md`, a tour, and
`reference/language.md`, the whole of it), and CompositionTests runs every example in it and
holds its tables of kinds to `canvas kinds`, so the skill can't drift from the app
([Testing plugins](#testing-plugins)).

How it's built ([Draw.swift](../Sources/Draw/Draw.swift) and the files beside it, Draw being the
engine that Automation's `draw`, `measure` and `kinds` run), in four steps, the first three
against the board as the run starts:

1. **Read.** DrawScript's `Script(parsing:)` cuts the script into statements, one a line: shapes
   (any first word but `edge`, `delete`, `group`, `ungroup` and `style` is a kind word, left for Draw to resolve),
   edges (`from:`, `to:`, `via:` and `share:` are the language's own keys, `EdgeKey`; `via:`'s
   value is a kind word, found by Draw, and `share:`'s is `true` or a name, `EdgeShare`; placements
   and `in` on an edge, read as a shape's, are where the stand-in it goes through goes),
   deletes, groups and ungroups (`group "A" and "B"`, two shapes or more, `ungroup "A"`, one or
   more: a `GroupStatement` of names joined by `and` or commas), and styles, which it merges into the
   statements that name them. Where a statement
   names a shape the file has (an edge's ends, a delete, a placement's target, `in`, a shape's own
   name, `share:`'s host) the name is a `ShapeName`: a quoted title, or a word that starts with `#`,
   an id, kept as text and checked only for its shape (`not_an_id`); what it names is Draw's. An attribute that
   isn't the language's own is a key and a value, left for Draw to check against the kind. The
   language's own words are enums with implicit raw values (`Keyword`, `LanguageKey`, `EdgeKey`,
   `Direction`, …), never string literals, so the id audit never sees another module's id there
   (Connections' `channel`, Titles' `title`). Every line that can't be read is reported, up to 20.
2. **Resolve** (`Drawing`): each kind word against the registry (a kind is drawable when a tool
   places it, `registry.placement(for:)`); each title, through DrawNames, to the one board shape
   it names (restated) or to none (made); each id to the shape the file has with it, on any board
   the app can show (`FileNames.place(ofID:)`, the file's own index by id, a lookup and not a pass),
   and to none is `unknown_id`, never a new shape, and one a title could not name (an arrow, a
   pill) `invalid_value`; both found into one set of items, so a shape named by its title and by
   its id in one script is one shape; each attribute by the kind's schema, own and added
   properties alike (`KindVocabulary`, over the core's [`KindSchema`](#a-kinds-schema): a value
   read as its property's type, in draw's own words when it can't be, and JSON held to the schema
   before it's read, `registry.schemaViolations(of:kind:)`, since reading drops a member its type
   doesn't have without a word: an unknown member, or a value of the wrong type anywhere in it, is
   `invalid_value`, with a "did you mean" over the object's members; a property the schema marks
   `readOnly` is no attribute (`unknown_attribute`; `kinds` leaves it out), and a string whose
   `format` is `x-canvas-query` is checked by `editor.queries?.checkStored` (syntax and vocabulary,
   and no word that reads the editor, `:selected`, since the query is stored to run later; so a bad
   one is `invalid_value` with the engine's message and hint; unchecked without QueriesPlugin; Draw
   uses Queries), and a string whose `contentMediaType` is one a plugin writes
   (`DrawTextFormats`: mention text's) is written by that plugin, wherever it is in the value,
   `DrawTexts.swift`; the naming property and coordinates refused); each placement's targets; each
   edge's ends and attribute keys; and each delete's shape, with the connections on it (those
   DrawEdges' `ends` joins to it, and any other of the edge kind bound to it,
   `record.boundShapes(in:)`: one with an end left free) and the boards it owns (a subboard's, and
   every board under it, `file.subtree(ownedBy:)`: refused, `read_only`, if one holds a read-only
   shape, as a transaction would refuse the delete; else said in a warning); and the shapes each
   group and ungroup names, found as a placement's target is, once a run each (`duplicate`). A new shape starts as
   what its tool places (`placement.shape(at:)`), and every shape's attributes are set by the core
   (`registry.shape(_:setting:)`), so the registry builds every record, and what the kind derives
   from them (a note's height, from its text, `DerivedProps`) is the size it's
   placed at, unless the statement gives one; given a width alone (`size: 300x`, a `Size` with no
   height), the shape is built at that width and what the kind derives is put in step there,
   whether any property is set or not (`registry.derived(_:)`), so a note is that wide and as tall
   as its text in one run, and a kind that derives nothing keeps its height; a `size:` under the
   smallest the kind's placement draws (`Placement.minimumSize`: a frame's 96 × 64, its tool's and
   resizing's too) is `invalid_value`, as one too big is, and `kinds` says it (`smallest`). What a
   shape is bound to (`ShapeReferencing`) must be on the board as the script leaves it, or it's
   `invalid_value`; what it only names (`ShapeNaming`, a note's mentions) needn't be. A kind whose
   titles are only derived (no shipped kind's) takes no title in its
   statement (`untitlable`), and a restated one whose derived title changes is renamed (`renamed`,
   held to a rename's rules), where one that's named too (no shipped kind is) keeps its derived
   title or is refused (`renames`). Problems that don't depend on one another are all reported, up
   to 20, each statement's first.
3. **Place** (DrawScript's `LayoutProblem.solve()`, from a problem built in DrawLayout.swift): the
   shapes that move are free boxes (new ones, and those restated with placements); what their
   placements name that stays put is fixed (board shapes, `board`, `view`); and every board shape
   with a solid that the script doesn't move or delete is an obstacle. What has a solid is the
   core's to say (`ShapeContext.solidBounds(of:)`: a shape's bounds where its geometry is closed,
   finite and not flat; none for an arrow or a line, or a shape kept aside), so a placement of any
   plugin keeps clear of the same shapes. The obstacles are filed once a run, in paint order, in a
   grid of cells about a shape's size (DrawScript's `ObstacleGrid`, boxes only, which Draw's
   `ObstacleIndex` fills in a pass over the board, keeping each obstacle's shape beside it), and
   the solver asks for them by region, each answer kept for the run: it asks again after every
   push, mostly about boxes that haven't moved, so however often it asks, a question costs what's
   near the box it's about (`./build.sh bench` holds a draw of 20 notes, each pushed along a row
   of the 10,000-shape board to its end, to 150 ms). DrawScript knows only boxes: a part on an
   outline (a round shape's corner) is worked out by Draw from the shape's `ShapeGeometry`, and
   handed over as a rect. The solver's first problem is the one reported. A zone isn't in a box's
   way (`Solver.isZone`): an obstacle that wholly holds a restated box where it already sat,
   however snug; a shape the box is placed against, at twice that one's area; the box where it
   lands and another shape too, at twice the box's area, so a region that frames what's in it
   takes a legend in any corner of the view or the board on it; or the `view` the box is placed
   against, or its drawing with nothing to hang on is drawn in, whatever its size (that drawing's
   spot isn't kept clear of it). A shape held is a board shape, or a free box the zone counts
   (`Solver.counted(by:in:)`, once a solve for each zone asked about): one on it for a reason of
   its own, `inside` or `on` it, a zone for it without counting any free box, or placed against
   one that counts, worked out from those up until nothing is added, so two new shapes can't hold
   each other on an empty note. What holds only the box where it lands is a neighbor, and in the
   way: an empty note or card next door, or a lone shape that's the whole board, for a box inside
   `board` (a note holding a badge of its own is a container like any other). A box held where it
   lands wholly on such a region at twice its size is `unordered`, its hint saying what the region
   holds (nothing yet, or no shape wholly: one hangs over its edge) and offering first to place
   the box elsewhere, since the region may be a note whose words it would cover, then, if the
   region is meant to hold shapes, to place a first one inside it. With the boxes placed, it says
   which obstacles each sits on as zones (`LayoutSolution.zones`, never what it's `inside` or
   `on`), which it's raised above and warned about hanging over.
4. **Apply**, in one `editor.transact("Draw")` (DrawCommit.swift), one undo step, which says an
   agent made it (`transaction.byAgent`: a type's sync takes what it wrote as in step, and
   asks the model nothing): the deletes; the shapes, each after
   every script shape it's drawn inside or on, new or restated, so that shape is in place first
   (new ones inserted on top; restated ones updated in place, and raised above a shape they're
   moved inside or on, or a zone they sit in where they land, while they're writable: before a
   change that locks one, after one that unlocks it, and not at all for one read-only throughout,
   which placing left as it was); the edges, through DrawEdges, against `transaction.shapes`, so either
   end may be new, each one's channel and sides checked as it's made, the first that's wrong
   ending the run (before the shapes are put down, so what puts them down judges by a transaction that holds
   the edges: the room a shape takes can depend on an arrow, and the layout made the same arrows, laid in,
   to give it: `Drawing.layOut()`); the groups and ungroups, last of the writes, in script order, so
   they may name a shape the script draws ([below](#groups-in-draw)); then the result, read back from `transaction.document`
   in one context taken after the last write, and the warnings. Anything wrong throws out of
   the body, and a body that throws commits nothing, and makes no undo step
   ([the document](#the-editor-the-document-and-drawing)).
   A dry run is the same transaction, whose body throws its finished result (a private error
   `draw` catches), so on the same board a dry run and a real run say the same.

**Containers** (a frame, [`ShapeContaining`](#containers)) are where the in-or-out rule meets the
language:

- **`in "X"`, for X a container**, draws on the board X is on and puts the shape in X: it's kept
  within X, 40 in from each side, as `inside` keeps a box (the layout problem's `Free.holder`,
  checked as `inside` is, `no_room` when it can't be), wherever its placements put it there; with
  none, and not in X already (where a restated shape stays), it's placed as `inside "X" top-left`
  places one, a clause written `in "X"`, so several make a list down from there. X must be on the
  board as the run starts (`unsupported` for one the script draws: draw it, then what's in it),
  writable (a read-only one, a locked frame, is `read_only`: nothing goes in it), and neither the
  shape nor one it holds (`circular`).
- **What a run puts down settles as by hand**, one by one, once every shape is where it goes, so
  each is judged against where the others land, never where a shape the run moves was
  (`transaction.settle`; the shapes that hold none first, then the containers, so what's put down
  in one goes along if it's nudged): a new shape, and a restated one it places or resizes, over a
  container's edge goes wholly in or
  out by most of its area, nudged, said in a warning (`"N" was over the edge of "Pen", so it was
  nudged in`), and glided after a real run (`editor.glide`); a container put down takes in what it
  lands on, and what it holds over its new edge goes in or out, said too (`a shape over the edge of
  "Pen" was nudged wholly in or out of it`); a read-only container it would go into refuses the
  run (`read_only`). So `inside`, `on` and landing on a zone put a shape in a container too, and a
  container's edge is never a zone's to warn about.
- **A restated container placed elsewhere takes what it holds along** (`translate`), which is
  never in its way (`Free.carries`), and which every other shape the run places meets where the
  container takes it, never where it is now: kept clear of it there, as of a part of the
  container (a shape `in` the container is; one placed over where it was isn't), so containers
  can trade places in one run. A placement against what it takes along is `unsupported`, since
  the layout has that where it was. Containers are applied before what they hold.
- **Read-only is inherited** (`transaction.isReadOnly(_:)` and `BoardReading.isReadOnly(_:)`, which
  read a shape through the board it's on): a shape in a locked frame, or on a locked subboard's
  board, refuses a real change and a delete (`read_only`), as a locked shape does.
- **A board that can't change takes nothing new**: a locked subboard's board, and every board under
  it (`reading.isBoardReadOnly`). `in` the subboard is `read_only` as `in` a locked frame is
  (`"Plans" is read-only (locked, say), so nothing goes in it`, the same hint), and so is a new
  shape that would land there by its placements or by the board shown (`"N" would go on "Plans"'s
  board, which is read-only (locked, say)`, named as `several_boards` names a board, by the shape
  that holds it), and a new edge (`edge "A" -> "B" would go on …`), the first thing wrong with each
  statement in a script, found as the run starts, or, for an edge, as it's applied; nothing is
  drawn, a dry run says the same, and no step is made. A restatement that changes nothing still
  goes through (`unchanged`).
- **`delete` of a container** leaves what it holds where it is, now in what held the container
  (the core's), a locked shape too, and says nothing more.

**Edges through a stand-in** ([DrawStandIns.swift](../Sources/Draw/DrawStandIns.swift),
[DrawBoard.swift](../Sources/Draw/DrawBoard.swift)). An arrow can't leave its board, and a shape
that many arrows point at needn't be pointed at from everywhere, so an edge may go into a
[stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding) for one end, put beside the other. Draw knows no kind of
stand-in and nothing of publicness: it asks `registry.standIns` which kinds stand in, which of
them can be made to stand for a shape (`makers`) and which shapes each admits (Topology's [`makes`
and `needs`](#stand-ins-forwarding)), and References' `reference` is what answers.

- **Whether.** A statement says so with `via: <kind>`: a kind word that must be one of `makers`
  (else `invalid_value`, with the one it's like and the kinds there are) and admit the end it stands
  for (else `invalid_value`, saying what the kind `needs`: "only a public shape can be stood for", and
  to ask the user, since `public:` is theirs to set and a script never makes a shape public to get an
  edge across). Otherwise **`Drawing.goesThroughStandIn(from:to:)` decides, the one function that
  does**, and the place to grow: today an edge goes through a stand-in when its ends are on different
  boards, and nothing else decides (a rule about distance or kinds would go there, and nowhere else).
  It goes through the first of `makers` that admits the end stood for (`standInKind(for:)`), and only
  the edge's row says so (`via`), as where `via:` asked: a warning for each edge between boards would
  bury the warnings that need reading in a run of many. Where no kind admits it, the edge is `several_boards`, with a hint that only such a shape can be stood for and to
  ask the user (`Drawing.standInHint`); where nothing stands in at all, the hint is the old one.
- **Sharing** (`share: true`, `share: "A"`; `sharedStandIn`). Each edge through a stand-in makes one of
  its own, so a hub with many users has as many, and `share:` makes them one. `share: true` draws the
  arrow into a direct stand-in of the kind for the same end that is already in the innermost container
  of the end that stays (the frame it is in, or the board outside frames: `containerOfEnd`), the
  board's first in document order (`StandInRoute.existing(… sharing: .any …)`, over the board's pills
  found in one pass, deleted ones left out) or one an earlier edge of the run made (`madeStandIns`);
  with none, it makes one, as without. `share: "A"` takes the one A's own arrow goes into, A (a shape
  of the script or the board) being in that container, from A's edges above it in the script and then
  the board's (`existing(… sharing: .host(A) …)`), and never makes one: A with none is `invalid_value`, naming A and the end, and so is A in another
  container, or the edge's own end. On an edge that goes through none (both ends on the board, no
  `via:`) it is `invalid_value` too, unless the edge is drawn through a stand-in already. The row of
  an edge that reused one says `shared: true` and `sharedWith` (the title named); an edge drawn
  already says `unchanged` with the same flags, `shared` then meaning that an arrow from another
  shape runs to the same stand-in (`Connected.shared`, `sharing(of:match:among:)`). Nothing else
  changes: a shared stand-in is deleted like any, once no arrow is on it. An edge that writes an
  identity key (an arrow's `is:`) and is not drawn yet reuses without `share:`: a second typed edge
  from Ann to the same far Acme goes into the stand-in Ann's other arrow already runs into for Acme
  (`hostStandIn`), its row saying `shared: true`, so two relationships between Ann and Acme are two
  arrows into Ann's one stand-in; an edge that writes no identity key makes its own, as before.
- **Which end.** The one off the board the run draws on; with `via:`, the arrow's end (however the
  edge is written, `<-` too), put beside the start. Either end may be the far one: a stand-in for the
  start, the arrow running out of it.
- **The board** (`Drawing.board(for:in:)`, `DrawBoard.swift`; `BoardClaims` reads the statements).
  An edge between shapes on two boards claims a board only softly with an end some stand-in can be
  made for (`makers`, `admits`) and hard with one that can't; the run draws on the first hard claim,
  else on the board of the first such edge's start (`via:`'s start claims hard, since the stand-in is
  put beside it), and each such edge needs one end on it (`several_boards` otherwise, naming the end
  it can't reach). `delete edge` claims the same way. Two edges claim otherwise:
  - One that's **drawn through a stand-in already** (an arrow on one of its two boards between the
    end there and a direct stand-in for exactly the other, by `edgeMatches`, the one rule for
    which arrows are an edge, whichever board it's asked of) claims that board, the start's first,
    hard, and its other end claims nothing, whether or not that end can be stood for still. The
    run draws where the stand-in is, so a run again, a `via:` over it and a `delete edge` find the
    edge there, rather than make a second stand-in for it on the other board. Each board's arrows
    are read once a run, and only for an edge between boards (`DrawPlugin.boardConnectionsRead`,
    debug builds, counts them).
  - One that joins **a shape the script draws** (a title no board has: it's on the board the run
    draws on, whichever that is) to a shape the file has: the script's end claims nothing, and the
    file's claims as an end of an edge between boards does, softly if a stand-in can be made for it
    (with nothing else to say, the run goes to its board, and the edge is straight there), else hard
    (and the hint asks for it to be made so, as it does for any end).

  A script with no edge between boards reads none of this (a board's arrows are read only when one
  shows up). `Drawing` reads `standIns` for a script with any edge or delete: a delete's arrows may
  run into stand-ins.
- **The stand-in is a shape of the run.** `registry.standIns.make` makes the record (the kind's
  tool's shape, standing for the end, called as the end's title folds), and `routeEdge` adds it to
  the run as a `ShapeItem` (`standsFor` set), placed as any new shape is: right of the start where
  that's the end that stays, left of the end where that is, or on the side `from:` or `to:` names for
  the end that stays, at the normal gap, kept clear of what's there, and settled into the containers
  it lands on. It has no placement of the script's, so where it clashes with another free box that
  nothing orders it against (two stand-ins beside notes side by side) it's the one that moves,
  past the other, on the axis its own placements leave free (`LayoutProblem.Free.implied`,
  `Solver.yielding`), where a box the script wrote would be `unordered`; its push warns, naming `from:`
  and `to:` as the fix. The stand-ins beside one shape on one side are a list of their own, 16
  apart (`LayoutProblem.impliedListStep`: a pill has no title above it to leave room for), never with
  a shape the script places there, which stays where its placement puts it while they give way past
  it (`Solver.findLists` keys implied boxes apart, and lists by what placements say, not their
  text). A list moves as one, down the page or across (`Solver.listHolds`, each member held where the
  first solve puts it from the one before), and is as free to move as all its members are, so a push
  never splits a column. Beside a shape the run doesn't move, a stand-in joins the column a run
  before left on that side (`StandInRoute.spot`, an answer `StandInSpot`: of the stand-ins an arrow
  joins to it, those wholly that side of it, in line as a list lines them, on the nearest line whose
  stand-ins reach across from its middle, so one dragged off elsewhere isn't beside it), 16 past its
  end and in line with it, its placements said in words (`Clause.written(_:naming:gap:)`), rather
  than centered on the shape and pushed past the column. It's inserted before the arrow, in the run's
  one transaction. `StandInRoute` (public, over a registry; `kind(for:fulfilling:)`,
  `existing(for:kind:sharing:near:in:)`, `spot(beside:edgeIs:side:in:excluding:staying:)` and
  `landing(of:at:in:avoiding:)`) is that making, for a writer that is not a script: it lands a pill
  of its size at a spot against `Surroundings`, in the rect a run gives the same pill.
- **An edge may place it** (`EdgeStatement.clauses` and `container`: placements and `in`, written on
  the edge as on a shape). Then the stand-in it makes is placed by them, as a shape statement's
  placements place a shape (`addStandIn` asks `contain` and `resolveTargets`, as `complete` does, and
  what they name claims its board as a shape's does), and it's a box the script wrote, not an implied
  one (`ShapeItem.implied` false): it doesn't yield, it lists with no stand-in beside a shape, and its
  push says to place it elsewhere. `in "F"` is the container `share: true` finds it in. An edge that
  makes no stand-in (it shares one, or is drawn already) places nothing; `share: "A"`, which never
  makes one, refuses a placement as it's read, and an edge drawn straight refuses one as it does
  `share:`. It's how a tool that lays a board out (canvas-digest) puts a stand-in several shapes share
  between them, at an exact offset in their frame, the others `share:`-ing it.
- **Its channel and sides** are the edge maker's: `EdgeRequest.fromStandsFor` and `toStandsFor` say
  the kinds of what an end stands for (none for a shape itself), and `PortEdgesPlugin` judges the end
  as those kinds would be, on the stand-in's own sides
  ([below](#edges-and-their-channels-portedgesplugin)).
- **Matching**, for a run again and for `delete edge` (`edgeMatches`): an arrow between one end and a
  stand-in whose record stands for exactly the other, by `.shapes` (a `.provided` answer can change,
  so it never matches), is the edge, straight or through, on one board too without `via:`; the
  stand-in the edge would make is then skipped, so a run again makes none. An arrow through a
  stand-in is looked for before anything else is decided about the edge (`routeEdge`), so it's the
  edge whatever the shape it stands for can be stood for now (it may have stopped being public), with
  `via:` or without; one drawn straight is looked for after `via:` is checked against the end. `via:`
  written over an edge drawn straight, or through a stand-in for its start, is `invalid_value` (`the
  edge "A" -> "B" is drawn straight to "B"`), the hint saying to `delete edge` it above the line; two
  matches are `ambiguous_edge`, as two straight ones are. A pill stands for a shape for the near shape,
  not for a type: an edge that writes an identity key and is not drawn yet goes into the pill the near
  shape's other arrows already run into for the far shape, and makes one if there is none
  (Sharing, above); one that writes no identity makes a pill of its own (`share:` reuses one).
- **Deletes.** `delete edge` takes what matches, either way round for `<->`, and `delete "X"` every
  connection bound to X; then each stand-in at the other end of one (a direct one, as matching reads
  them, never one whose answer can change) that the run leaves with no arrow at all, loose ones
  included, goes too (`standInsEmptied`): it has no title for a script to name, and it stood for its
  shape for those arrows alone. One that's read-only is `read_only` (`the reference that delete "X"
  leaves with no arrow is read-only (locked, say)`), and nothing is deleted. A stand-in for X with
  arrows from elsewhere stays, which is what a stand-in several edges share does until the last of them goes.
- **The result.** An edge's row has `via` (the stand-in's kind) whenever its arrow goes through one,
  `unchanged` and `deleted` rows too (a `delete "X"`'s among them, naming the shape a stand-in stands
