  for, as an edge's row does); the stand-in has a row of its own on its statement's line: `created`,
  with its `kind` and `at` and no title, before the edge's; `deleted`, with its kind alone, after its
  arrows'. A dry run says the same, and one undo takes the stand-in and the arrow back together.

<a id="groups-in-draw"></a>
**Groups** ([DrawGroups.swift](../Sources/Draw/DrawGroups.swift)). `group "A" and "B"` puts shapes in
one group, `ungroup "A"` takes them out of every group; shapes in a group are selected as one in the
app. Draw owns the statement and no meaning of a group: it finds each shape named as a placement's
target is (a title or an id; a shape the script draws, restates or renames counts, by the title its
statement calls it; one the script deletes, or an arrow or a reference by its id, is refused), on the
board the run draws on (a name claims its board as a target does, so shapes on two boards are
`several_boards`), refuses a shape named twice in a run (`duplicate`), and, once every shape and edge
the script draws is in the transaction, hands the shapes of each statement, in the order written, and
the transaction to what groups shapes (the `DrawGroups` point, below), which writes and says whether
it changed anything. A write a read-only shape refused is `read_only`; a statement that writes
nothing goes through. A row has `did` `grouped`, `ungrouped` or `unchanged` and `shapes`, the shapes
as the statement called them, and no `kind`; `measure` leaves both statements out; a list without the
point refuses them, `no_groups`.

Before any of it, a run is refused while a drag is under way on the board (`editor.session`,
`busy`: its Escape would put back what the script moved), or a press is held
(`undoHistory.isPressHeld`: whatever commits during a press is part of its undo step, so the run
would be taken back with it). Once it's placed, a
real run ends an edit under way on a shape it changes or deletes (`editor.endEditing()`), and works
the script out again if ending it changed the board, so what's typed lands first. It applies the
run once and throws it away before it does, since some of what a run can fail on (an edge that
can't be drawn) is found only as it's applied: a run that fails, or leaves that shape as it is,
leaves the typing be. The view the script's `view` and its unplaced drawing go by is where the
camera is headed (`editor.cameraTarget`), so a draw just after a `--reveal` goes where that one's
glide ends. The selection is left alone, and so is the camera,
unless `--reveal` asks to ease it to fit what the run made or changed
(`editor.animateCamera(to: Camera(fitting:…))`, as selecting a row of the table of contents does).

What comes back (`DrawResult`, with the server's `board`) says what each statement did, in line
order, and never by id, since titles are the names:

```json
{"board": {"id": 2, "name": "Architecture", "shows": "root", "showsPath": ["root"]},
 "changes": [{"line": 2, "did": "created", "kind": "sticky-note", "title": "API", "at": [[620, 350], [200, 200]], "inView": true},
             {"line": 4, "did": "connected", "kind": "arrow", "from": "Web", "to": "API", "channel": "note-link"}, …],
 "warnings": [{"line": 3, "message": "\"Ship v1\": Blocked: say why in the notes.", "severity": "warning", "attribute": "notes"}]}
```

A row's `did` is `created`, `moved` (its bounds changed), `updated`, `renamed` (with `was`),
`unchanged`, `deleted`, `connected`, `reconnected`, `grouped` or `ungrouped`. A shape's row has its `kind`, `title` and
`at` (`[[x, y], [width, height]]`, world units), `inView` while the board is in a window, and
`pushedPast`; an edge's has `from`, `to`, `via` where it goes through a stand-in, and the attributes
DrawEdges declares (`channel`; not its kind's, which are as written), but a
deleted connection with an end left free has neither end to name. A
warning (`line`, but none for one about the whole run; `message`; `severity`; and the property
it's about, `attribute`) is an issue DrawChecks finds on a shape made or changed (an `error`
too: the shape is drawn, invalid; without DrawChecks, a bound of its schema it breaks), an issue the
run brought to a shape it did not write (named by its title, on the line of the statement that brought
it: a second relationship drawn at a note whose row allows one; at most 20 shapes, then a count), a push
past another shape (or a move along with a shape pushed, which isn't in `pushedPast`: that's
only what the shape was kept clear of itself; what a shape went past is said once each way it
went, so a list's members, pushed past a wall in turn, aren't also said to have gone along with
one another past it), a named side facing away from the
other end, a new title nearly one the board has, a shape hanging over the edge of a zone it
sits in (a zone isn't in its way, but doesn't keep it in), how many shapes
landed out of view, a shape resized where it stays that now overlaps another, a name a shape
drawn holds (a mention in its text) of a shape that isn't in the file or is on a board the app
can't show (by id, since the script wrote it: `"Plan": text names shapes that aren't in the file:
…; they show as missing`), or a deleted subboard's boards and what was on them. A dry run's
result says `dryRun: true`. The result's `board` is the server's: the board the run worked on,
read as it began.

### measure

`canvas measure <script>|-` is for a tool that lays shapes out before it draws them, and needs
what only the app knows: the size `draw` would make each shape of a script (a note as tall as its
text at its width, a note that is a type or one of a type as tall as its words and rows), how far its title row
reaches above
it, how wide a reference to a shape is for its title, and the constants placement is done
with. It
is a board command whose board is optional (`boardOptional`: `--board` defaults to the board in
front, if any, and with none open it runs with no editor), [Measure.swift](../Sources/Draw/Measure.swift):it reads the script as `draw` does (the same messages), leaves out every placement, `in` and delete, and
the arrow of an edge that says `via:` (a pill is sized, never drawn here, so an edge `via: reference` to a
note that is not public still measures), and runs the shape statements and the other edges through `Drawing`
itself on a board of its own, made empty and thrown away (`CanvasEditor(registry:)`), so it changes no board
and opens no undo step, and the sizes are the ones a draw makes (`Drawing.complete`, then
`registry.derived`). The scratch board is empty,
so every title is new as on a new file, but a board that ran it lends its names and records
(`namesBeyond:`): an `is: "Order"`, or an edge's end, finds the type of the open file as draw finds one, on any
board, and the note is measured with the rows the type gives it: the script is laid out over that
editor's own context (`namesBeyond.shapeContext.layingOut(…)`, which reads the file's types and ends and writes
nothing), and a script that draws the types, a relationship type, its ends and the notes together measures
as a draw of it does. A name it can't find (a title nobody has, two shapes
called alike, a shape that isn't a type) is a warning (`measured without it`, or `measured as written` for a kind that takes the value as written) where a draw refuses it; a
format's own refusals (a blank `@[]`) still refuse. It answers

```json
{"shapes": [{"line": 1, "title": "Checkout v2", "kind": "sticky-note", "size": [300, 200], "above": 27}],
 "references": [{"line": 4, "for": "Hub", "size": [91, 32]}],
 "constants": {"gaps": {"none": 0, "tight": 40, "normal": 80, "wide": 160}, "defaultGap": 80, "listStep": 64,
               "referenceStep": 16, "horizontalClearance": 40, "verticalClearance": 64, "frameInset": 40,
               "smallest": {"frame": [96, 64]}}}
```

`warnings`, `[{line, message}]`, is there only when something was measured without a name, and `board`,
the server's as in `draw`'s answer, only when a board ran it.

The `size` of a shape is the room it takes once drawn: the frame its kind lays it out in
(`LaidOutBox`, a note that shows rows no record holds), which is the size it stores for any other
kind, and the same size `draw`'s `at` reports for the statement. It is worked out by one function
(`Drawing.layOut()`) both share, with the script's own shapes read as the file's and the arrows its edges
draw laid in beside them (`provisionalConnections()`, made by the function `connect` draws them with, a
stand-in's shape found among the run's own shapes, a pair's next arrow bent beside the arrows already joining the pair as
the commit will bend it; none at all when the run has no shape to lay out), so a
note whose size depends on an end the same script draws has the row that end gives it. A board shape the
script does not restate keeps its size from before the run. A draw makes its edges
before it settles what it put down, so the settle judges by a transaction that holds them, and reads its
reports from one context taken after the last write.

`above` is `editor.adornmentExtent(of:)` (Adornments, a horizontal Draw uses): how far the adornments
the shape would show reach above its top edge at 100% zoom, where they keep their size in view
points (`AdornmentLayout.extent(of:in:)`, pure over the layout, so text left out for want of room
reaches nowhere); asked of a record that is not on any board, nothing is kept for it. A reference
row is the size of `registry.standIns.make(kind, standingFor:, label:)` for the end's title, for
each edge that says `via:` (the kind it names): Draw knows no kind of stand-in, and a bare edge's
goes through one or not by the boards, which it does not read. The constants are read from the
source and never copied: the gaps (`GapName`), the step between references
(`LayoutProblem.impliedListStep`), the inset of what `in "F"` holds (`LayoutProblem.insideGap`),
the default gap, the list step, the clearances, and each kind's least size
(`Placement.minimumSize`).

### What draw takes from other plugins

Draw knows no title, port, validity, mention or group. `draw` takes each from a point Draw declares
([DrawPoints.swift](../Sources/Draw/DrawPoints.swift)), keyed so it takes at most one contribution
(one for each media type, for text), which the horizontals give, a plugin value of its own in each
(AutomationTests make their own, over fixtures). Without one, `draw` does without:

| Point | Sugar | What `draw` gets | Without it | Shipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DrawNames` | `registrar.drawNames(name:namingProperty:isDerived:fold:)` | What a shape is called; the property of its kind's schema a title is written to (nil: its shapes can't be named); whether the kind works names out itself; how a title a script writes is folded | No titles: a titled statement is `no_names` | TitleNamesPlugin |
| `DrawLabels` | `registrar.drawLabels { record, registry in … }` | What a shape with no title is called for the reference `draw` puts beside the shape an edge ends at on another board (the label the maker is handed): the name where it is named in words, its first line or its values | The kind's name (`Untitled sticky note`) | MentionTextsPlugin |
| `DrawEdges` | `registrar.drawEdges(kind:attributes:sides:ends:make:)` | The kind edges are (nil while nothing makes them); the attribute keys an edge takes beside `from:` and `to:`; what an edge may leave a kind on, by side (for `kinds`); which shapes a connection joins; a connection made or changed | No edges: an edge statement is `no_edges` | PortEdgesPlugin |
| `DrawEdgeIdentities` | `registrar.drawEdgeIdentity(IsAProperty.key)` | A property of the edge kind that tells two edges of one pair apart, named by the plugin that owns it (one a key) | The pair alone: two connections of one pair are `ambiguous_edge` | TypeNamesPlugin (`is`) |
| `DrawChecks` | `registrar.drawChecks(touched: { changes, shapes in … }, rest: "canvas query …") { record, shapes in … }` | What's wrong with a shape made or changed, as the script leaves the board: `DrawIssue`s (a message, its level: a warning, an error, or `incomplete`, that the shape still needs something; the property it's about). And `touched`: of what the run wrote (`transaction.pending`, with its shapes), the other shapes to look at, on any board; the run checks each as it found it and as it leaves it and warns of each issue it brought (`rest` is the command that lists them all, an error, a warning or what a shape still needs, said after the twentieth shape) | Each shape checked against its kind's schema (`registry.schemaViolations(of:)`); with no `touched`, a run says only what's wrong with the shapes it wrote | ValidationChecksPlugin |
| `DrawTextFormats` | `registrar.drawTextFormat(mediaType:describes:write:)` | Each string a script writes whose schema says `contentMediaType` of that media type, as `write` gets it (its string's escapes undone) with a `DrawTextContext` (the registry, the string's schema as its kind declares it, and `shape(called:admitting:)`, which finds the shape a title names as the script finds one, `admitting` taking the record and the keys the script writes on it, for a shape drawn in the same run: what to keep, or a refusal. `describes` is said after the attribute's type in `canvas kinds`. A list whose schema is `uniqueItems` is written with each once, the first, after its strings are written (two titles of one shape are one id) | Text kept as written; `kinds` says nothing after its type | MentionTextsPlugin, TypeNamesPlugin |
| `DrawValueWriters` | `registrar.drawValueWriter(for:write:merge:)` | The value a script writes for a property, as `write` gets it (JSON, strings still as written, with the same `DrawTextContext`) and returns what the property stores, or a refusal said on the statement's line; then `merge(written, held)`, with what the shape holds now (nil for a new one; for an edge, the connection as its maker left it), is what the shape is set to, so a script run again changes nothing. One writer a property key | A value replaces what the shape holds | FieldValuesPlugin |
| `DrawReports` | `registrar.drawReports(members: ["is"]) { record, written, shapes, bothHeads in … }` | Each shape and edge row of the run, once every statement is in the transaction, with what its statement wrote for each property that has a value writer (nil for an `unchanged` row) and the board as the script leaves it: a `DrawShapeReport` of warnings (`DrawIssue`s, said with the statement's line) and `problems` (Queries' `ShapeProblem`: `field`, `path`, `class`, `message`) that go on the shape's row, and `members` (a `[String: JSONValue]`) that go flat beside the row's own, only the keys it declared in `members:` (the registry refuses one that is a row's own key, an edge attribute, blank or declared twice); `bothHeads` is whether the statement of a connection wrote `<->`; it is asked of each connection the run deletes too, with the record as it was (gone from `shapes`, `written` nil for a `delete edge` that names no identity key, `[:]` for any other), for its members and warnings only | No `problems`, no warnings, no members from it | FieldValuesPlugin |
| `DrawGroups` | `registrar.drawGroups(group:ungroup:)` | For a `group` or `ungroup` statement, the shapes it names (resolved: each once, on the board the run draws on, in the order written) and the run's transaction, once every shape and edge the script draws is in it: `group` puts exactly those shapes in one group of their own, `ungroup` leaves each in none. Each writes through the transaction (a read-only shape refuses the write, and the run says `read_only`) and answers whether it changed anything, else the statement's row is `unchanged` | No groups: `group` and `ungroup` are `no_groups` | GroupDrawPlugin |

`TypeNamesPlugin` ([TypeNames.swift](../Sources/Types/Engines/TypeNames.swift)) writes `is: "Employee card"`, on a shape and on an edge, as the id of the type that title names (`TypeLink.mediaType`), admitting what `TypeIndex.canBeNamed(_:registry:writing:)` says, a pure function of the record and the registry (a type that is no pill), and refuses any other shape "which isn't a type or a shape", and the shape itself (`DrawTextContext.owner`); a quoted value for a list of text is a list of that one item (Draw's, `KindVocabulary.value(of:)`), several are JSON.

`FieldValuesPlugin` ([FieldValuesDraw.swift](../Sources/Types/Engines/FieldValuesDraw.swift)) writes `fieldValues: {…}` as a note's or arrow's own value joined with what it holds, member by member at every depth: a list is replaced whole, `null` clears the member it is written at, an object left empty is pruned (`FieldValuesMerge.merged`, pure, then `FieldValues.pruned`), and an object that sets nothing over a text or a list held leaves it, as the one writer does, and reports on each shape a run draws: its row's `problems` (what its values still need and what's wrong, by the check of the run, over types the script draws too) and each member of the written object no field of its types names.

`GroupDrawPlugin` ([GroupDraw.swift](../Sources/Grouping/GroupDraw.swift)) writes Grouping's groups (a shape's `groups`, outermost first), read from the transaction's shapes by `BoardGroups`, which counts a group while it holds two parts or more on the board: `group` writes exactly the shapes named one new group (a fresh id), flat, each leaving the groups it was in, unless they already are one group that counts and nothing else (nothing is written); `ungroup` clears the `groups` of each shape named that is in a group that counts, at every level. A shape that holds only the id of a group that no longer counts is in none.

The other four registrations, whole but for `PortEdgesPlugin`'s policy and the clauses
`MentionTextsPlugin` says ([TitleNames.swift](../Sources/Titles/TitleNames.swift),
[PortEdges.swift](../Sources/Connections/PortEdges.swift),
[ValidationChecks.swift](../Sources/Validation/ValidationChecks.swift),
[MentionTexts.swift](../Sources/Mentions/MentionTexts.swift)):

```swift
// TitleNamesPlugin: a shape is called what Titles calls it, and a title is written to the one Titles keeps.
registrar.drawNames(name: { record, registry in registry.title(of: record) },
                    namingProperty: { kind, registry in
                        registry.properties(for: kind).contains(TitleProperty.key) ? TitleProperty.key.rawValue : nil
                    },
                    isDerived: { kind, registry in registry.titleIsDerived(kind) },
                    fold: { TitleProperty.folded($0) })

// PortEdgesPlugin: an edge is the connector's connection, on the channel this plugin picks.
registrar.drawEdges(kind: { registry in registry.makesConnections ? registry.connectorKind : nil },
                    attributes: [ChannelProperty.key.rawValue],
                    sides: { kind, registry in EdgeChannels.sides(of: kind, in: registry) },
                    ends: { record, registry in registry.connectionEnds(of: record) },
                    make: { request, existing, shapes throws(DrawError) in
                        try EdgeChannels.connection(for: request, existing: existing, in: shapes)
                    })

// ValidationChecksPlugin: what's wrong is what Validation finds, schema bounds included, and what a run's
// writes reach is what the rules say they touch.
registrar.drawChecks(touched: { changes, shapes in
    shapes.registry.validationTouched(by: changes, in: shapes)
}, rest: "canvas query \":invalid\"") { record, shapes in
    shapes.registry.validationIssues(of: record, in: shapes).map { issue in
        DrawIssue(issue.message, level: issue.severity.drawLevel, field: issue.field)   // Draw's words for the same three levels
    }
}

// MentionTextsPlugin: in mention text, `@[Title]` is the whole mention of the shape called Title.
registrar.drawTextFormat(mediaType: MentionTextFormat.mediaType, describes: "@[Title] mentions") { text, context throws(DrawError) in
    let scope = context.schema[MentionTextFormat.annotationKey]?.objectValue
    return try MentionTextFormat.resolvingNames(in: text) { name throws(DrawError) in
        let shape = try context.shape(called: name) { record in clause(context.registry.mentionAdmission(of: record, scope: scope)) }
        return (shape.id, shape.title)
    }
}
```

- **Names are titles.** A kind is named when it opts into the title Titles keeps (`title()`, or
  `registrar.title(K.self)` for another plugin's kind), derived when Titles works its titles out
  (`title { … }`), and may be both (no shipped kind is): a derived name names a shape only while
  it's the only one so called, and a statement that would change it is refused (`renames`). The
  board's names are read once a run, from the shapes that aren't kept aside.
- **An edge statement is an upsert.** `ends`, over the transaction's document, finds the
  connections already drawn from one shape to the other (either way round for `<->`; one drawn the
  other way round is asked for its own way). None: `make` gets `existing` nil, and draws one
  (`connected`). One: `make` changes it, or hands back `existing` itself when nothing would
  change, which is how `draw` tells `unchanged` from `reconnected` (`==`). More is
  `ambiguous_edge`. With `identity` (below), which of the pair's connections a statement is about
  is narrowed by what it writes of those keys. `make` gets an `EdgeRequest`: its ends by id, the sides named
  (`EdgeRequest.Side`, Draw's own, since Connections imports Draw, not DrawScript), whether `<->`
  puts a head at its start too, the attributes it declares as written, its ends' names and the
  edge as written, for messages, and, for an end that's a [stand-in](#draw) the run put beside the
  shape it connects, the kinds of what it stands for (`fromStandsFor`, `toStandsFor`: the end is
  judged as those shapes would be, on its own sides). It returns the connection, not inserted, and
  throws `DrawError(message, reason:, hint:)`, which `draw` gives the statement's line; its
  closure says `throws(DrawError)`. `draw` checks what comes back (the edge kind, a new id or the
  existing one, naming only shapes on the board) before it inserts or updates it.
  `DrawEdges.check` refuses an attribute key the language keeps (`from`, `to`, `via`, `style`),
  one a result's row has of its own (`line`, `did`, `kind`, …: a row carries an edge's attributes
  beside its own members), one a script couldn't write before a colon, and one declared twice.
- **Identity: which connection of a pair an edge is.** `drawEdgeIdentity(_:)` names a property
  of the edge kind that tells two connections of one pair apart, and the plugin that owns the
  property names it, not the one that makes edges (Types names `is`, so two arrows of one pair of
  different types are two edges, and Connections, which makes them, knows no type). A statement that writes none of them is
  about the pair, as above. One that writes some is about the connections of the pair that hold
  what it writes (a list as a set; absent, `null` and `[]` are one "none"): one is that connection
  (`unchanged` or `reconnected`, its identity not written again), two are `ambiguous_edge`, and
  with none, a pair with exactly one connection with none of the keys gives it what the statement
  writes (`reconnected`), else a new connection is made (`connected`); written as `none`, it is the
  plain connection alone. Two statements for one pair in a script are `duplicate` unless both write
  a key, differently. `delete edge "A" -> "B" is: "T"` takes the connections that hold it; Draw
  refuses every other attribute there (`unknown_attribute`), and `DrawEdgeIdentities.check` refuses
  an identity key that is empty, one of the maker's `attributes`, or one the language keeps (the
  registry, one named by two plugins). A key
  the edge kind has no property for tells nothing apart. Which board a pair is on never depends on
  its identity.
- **A connection by id, from any plugin.** `registry.drawsConnections` (something
  makes edges) and `registry.drawConnection(from:to:in:standingFor:beside:)` make a connection
  between two shapes of a board by their ids, with the maker `canvas draw` makes `edge "A" -> "B"`
  with and the channel policy that statement would get (a bare edge's), so a later run restates what
  the app drew as `unchanged`. It returns the new record, not inserted (`in` is the board's
  `ShapeContext`, either end in it, a transaction's `shapes` for one the transaction made), or nil
  where nothing makes edges or the maker refuses the pair (an end it cannot connect, no channel
  they share). `standingFor` is the kinds each end stands for when it is a stand-in
  (`EdgeRequest.fromStandsFor` and `toStandsFor`: the ends are connected as what they stand for
  is); `beside` names the connections already joining the pair, carried on the request
  (`EdgeRequest.beside`; nil, the default: the maker reads them) to a maker that draws a second apart
  from the first (Arrows' connector bends a new arrow aimed at both centers). A run sets it for each
  edge it draws, listing the board's connections of the pair (those it does not delete) and its own so far, in
  statement order: the arrows it lays out before the layout are made beside the same list, over a document that
  holds them, so the arrow laid out is the arrow drawn.
- **An edge's other attributes are its kind's**, as a shape's are: any key DrawEdges doesn't
  declare is one of the edge kind's attributes (its schema's, read by `KindVocabulary`: an arrow's
  `text`, `labelPosition`, `bend`, `locked`), or `unknown_attribute`, read as a shape's value is.
  `make` never sees them: `draw` sets them on what it returns (`registry.shape(_:setting:)`), then
  hands that to `make` again as `existing`, and refuses one `make` changes back (`invalid_value`,
  "… isn't what the edge as written says": an arrow's heads are its arrow's, `->` or `<->`). So
  an edge restated without one keeps it, as a shape does, and `PortEdgesPlugin` never learns what
  a kind says.
- **Checks see the board as the script leaves it** (`transaction.shapes`), so a rule that looks up
  another shape sees the ones drawn with it. Each issue is a warning on the statement's line.
- **A text is written by the format of its schema's media type** (`DrawTexts.swift`). `KindVocabulary`
  reads which of a kind's properties may hold such a string anywhere inside (`textKeys`: a `$ref`
  followed once, so a schema that holds itself ends), so a property that can't is passed over at
  once. A value that can (a string, a list, an object) is walked beside its property's schema,
  `properties`, `additionalProperties`, `prefixItems` and `items`, `$ref`s followed, members in
  name order so the first refusal is the same each time, and each string whose resolved schema
  says a media type some plugin writes goes through its `write`, as the script wrote it, with
  the string's schema as declared. It's after the value is read and held to its schema (`fits`), for
  a shape's attributes, a style's among them, and for an edge's own. A refusal is the statement's, said
  on its line as `"Plan": remark: …` (a shape's subject, the attribute, what the format said, and
  `(from style x)`), or `edge "A" -> "B": remark: …`, with the reason and hint it was thrown with;
  a title whose own statement couldn't be resolved adds no error of its own (`Drawing.skipped`, as a
  placement against it adds none). `canvas kinds` says what a format takes after the type of a property whose
  strings it writes (`KindVocabulary.compactType`: `text (@[Title] mentions)`, `JSON [text] (…)` for a list
  of them), so a refusal's hint says it too.
- **A format asks for a shape by title** (`DrawTextContext.shape(called:admitting:)`,
  `DrawTextLookup`), made once a run after every title the script draws is known, among the shapes
  `admitting` takes (a closure over the shape: nil takes it, a string says why it doesn't, as the
  clause that follows its kind). The places, in order, the first with a shape called that (folded
  as DrawNames folds) that is taken deciding: a shape the script draws, restates, or renames to it
  (`title: "New"`, known before the attributes are read, so a text earlier in the script finds it;
  the old title finds the same shape, as a placement does), also one drawn further down; the board
  the run draws on; the board the window shows (if another); then every other board of the file
  the app can show (the last two are `FileNames.beyond`, which finds an edge's end on another
  board too: the window's board if it has one, else the one other board that has one). Two or more
  in one place are `ambiguous_title` (those on the board by their kinds and where they are, as a
  placement's are; on other boards, by the boards); shapes the script deletes, and those on boards
  its deletes take, don't count, and a title only they have is `unknown_title` ("names "Old",
  which this script deletes"); a title some shape has and none is taken, `invalid_value`, saying
  what the first is and the format's clause; none at all, `unknown_title` with
  `Suggestions.closest` over the file's titles and the script's own that are taken. It never
  decides the board: `Drawing.board(for:in:)` reads statements' titles alone. The file's names
  (`FileNames`, a walk of every board) are read when a lookup first asks, and shared with
  `board(for:)` where the script names titles, so a script whose texts name nothing reads none
  (`DrawPlugin.fileNamesRead`, debug builds, counts them). Without DrawNames a lookup is
  `no_names`.

### Edges and their channels: `PortEdgesPlugin`

An edge is a connection the connector makes [without a drag](#connecting-without-a-drag), on a
channel `PortEdgesPlugin` picks from Connections' [port table](#a-kinds-ports) as a drag from a port would: a
connection runs only from a shape with a dot on its channel to one that takes it. The policy,
`EdgeChannels`:

- **`channel: <id>`** is that channel, which some installed plugin must declare (else
  `invalid_value`, listing the channels). The start's kind must have a dot on it, and the end's
  kind take it as a target (else `no_channel`, saying what each end has, by side); a side named
  without such a port is `invalid_value`.
- **`channel: none`** is a plain connection, on no channel, from and to any side.
- **Unwritten**, it's the first of the start's dot channels (on `from:`'s side, if named; else all
  its dots', in the table's order) that the end takes as a target (on `to:`'s side, if named):
  `registry.connectionChannel(from:fromSide:to:toSide:)`, Connections'. With none, it's plain if neither kind has ports on anything (two frames), and
  otherwise `no_channel`, whose hint says `channel: none` draws one anyway; a named side narrows
  the channels, so one without a port leaves none.
- **A connection on a channel never ends where it starts**: a shape joined to itself on one is
  `no_channel`.
- **One already drawn keeps its channel**: another written is `invalid_value`, with the hint to
  write `delete edge "A" -> "B"` above the line and draw it again, and a side named must have a
  port on its channel.
- **A stand-in at an end** (`EdgeRequest.fromStandsFor`, `toStandsFor`: a reference `draw` put beside
  the shape the edge connects, [above](#draw)) takes the channels of what it stands for, on its own
  sides, as a drag from that shape's port to it would find them: the lookups' `standingFor:`
  ([A kind's ports](#a-kinds-ports)), through `EdgeChannels.End`. An edge to a reference for a note is
  on `note-link`; a `channel:` written still wins where both ends take it. A side named for it that it
  has no port on at all (a reference has them on its left and right) is `invalid_value`, whatever the
  channel (`to: top: a reference has no ports on its top`, with the hint `a reference takes arrows on
  its left and right: to: takes left|right`); `channel: none` leaves and arrives by any side, as ever.
  A message that names an end says what it stands for (`a reference for a sticky-note has note-link
  ports on its left and right`).
- **Before any of it**, the connector must be able to connect both ends in the board as the script
  leaves it (`registry.canConnect(_:in:)` with `transaction.shapes`), and afterwards to make the
  connection (the binding rules allow it): otherwise it's `cannot_connect`, naming the end.
- **What edges are** is the connector's kind only while it makes connections without a drag
  (`registry.makesConnections`): a connector that only draws from ports leaves `draw` with
  `no_edges`.

### query

`query` is how an agent reads a file: which shapes are there, what they're called, what's inside
what and what connects to what, answered by [Queries](#queries) about every board of the file
`--board` names, whichever board its window shows. It changes nothing.

```
canvas query --board 2 - <<'EOF'
"Payments" sticky-note:mentions("API gateway")
EOF
```

The language is taught by the canvas skill: SKILL.md's "Reading the board" tours it, and
`reference/query.md` is the whole of it, where every block is a query run on the story file
([Testing queries](#testing-queries)). The commands are QueryCommands'
([QueryCommands.swift](../Sources/QueryCommands/QueryCommands.swift)), for agents, on Automation,
Queries, QueryTranslation and the wire (the answer is the wire's JSON), which declares no point and
knows no shipped kind: its help writes `<kind>` and `<title>`, and `--ask`'s prompt is
`QueryTranslationPlugin`'s, which reads it from the product's files (`Shipped/ask-prompt.txt`).

- **Params** (`QueryParams`): `query`, positional, read from standard input as `-` (`x-stdin`: a
  query is full of what shells mangle, so a heredoc with a quoted delimiter); `--ask <question>`
  instead (up to 2,000 characters, `-` too; given, `canvas` waits up to 60 s, its `x-timeout`);
  `--limit` (1 to 10,000; 100 unless it says, and `count` is always of all);
  `--count` (no rows); and `--brief` (rows without their attributes) or `--fields <attribute>`,
  given again for each (only those, whole). Exactly one of a query and `--ask`, and not `--brief`
  with `--fields`, else `invalid_params`. `--fields` naming an attribute a shape hasn't leaves it out
  of that row.
- **The answer** is `{board, query, count, rows, warnings?}`: `board` where it ran, `shows` and
  `showsPath` (the board shown as it took up the file, `:current-board`'s), which the server
  completes with the file's `id` and `name`; `query` as the language writes it, `count`, the rows
  as `QueryRow` writes itself ([What a query sees](#what-a-query-sees)), `asked` with `--ask`, and
  no `rows` with `--count`, and `warnings`, `pending` among them (below). It's built as the
  wire's JSON member by member, off the main actor, where the result is let go of too
  (`QueryOutput.json`, handed the result whole), never written through `JSONEncoder` and read back,
  and `runAsync:` passes it through. As text, the rows are a table (`id`, `kind`, `title`, `board`,
  `inside`), each one's attributes under it.
- **Edges are read settled, as the resolved view reads them.** A query that reads edges counts an arrow
  into a stand-in (a shape that stands for others, Topology's) as an arrow into what it stands for,
  and waits, up to `QueryBudget.settleWait` (2 s), for answers a stand-in asked for that haven't come
  (`QueryRequest.settle`, [Queries](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)); past it, it answers
  anyway with a `pending` warning. A row's `connection` that went through a stand-in also has `via`
  (the stand-in at each end that was one, by id) and, for a stand-in for several shapes, `more` (its other
  pairs), each written member by member, and only then.
- **A refusal** carries the query's reason, message and hint (most often the query to write), and
  where it is:
  `line`, `column` and `length` in characters, and `statement`, the line as sent, whole, so the caret
  `canvas` draws lands on what's wrong (`AutomationError(error, in: text)`); several problems that
  don't hang on one another come at once, each where it is, in `errors`. A line longer than 200
  characters (`QueryOutput.quoted`) is quoted around what's wrong, `…` where it's cut, the column and
  length counted in what's quoted (`QueryError.located(in:quoting:)`). Beside the language's reasons
  (`QueryError.Reason`, [Queries](#queries)), `no_queries`: the app has no `QueriesPlugin`.
- **`canvas query-vocabulary`**, an app command (it reads the registry, on no board:
  `QueryVocabulary(registry:)`), is what this app's queries can name: `vocabulary`, the block
  `--ask` sends the model (the kinds, the edge types and the plugins' words); `kinds`, each `{kind,
  label, naming, holdsShapes, holdsBoard, attributes}` (`naming` is `named`, `derived` or `none`, and
  not `titles`, Titles' plugin id, which the id audit keeps a module that doesn't depend on Titles
  from writing; `holdsShapes`, whether shapes can be inside its shapes, a board of them or shapes on
  theirs, which may stand where a container goes, and `holdsBoard`, whether by a board of their own;
  each attribute with what it takes, `KindSchema.compactType`, and how a text format reads it: `text
  (mentions read as @Name)`);
  `edgeTypes`, each `{type, under?, summary?}`, in the tree's order; and `words`, each `{word, takes,
  summary, example, from}`, the language's own first (`from: queries`), then plugins' in plugin
  order. Without `QueriesPlugin` it answers `no_queries` too (`registry.answersQueries`, which looks
  up `QueriesPlugin`'s mark, since an app command has no editor to ask).

#### `--ask`

`canvas query --ask "which notes mention the gateway?"` has the editor's language model write the
query, runs it, and answers as a query does: `asked`, the question, and `query`, what the model
wrote, for the agent to check it asks what the person meant. The translator (`QueryTranslator`,
`editor.queryTranslator`, [QueryTranslator.swift](../Sources/QueryTranslation/QueryTranslator.swift);
QueryTranslation is an engine, so the app may ask it too) runs `ask` on the main actor, awaiting,
never holding it, and says why it can't as a `QueryTranslationError` (a `reason` and a `message`),
which QueryCommands says as the wire's `AutomationError`, hints included. It holds the editor weakly, and
takes what a question needs of it (its queries, model and scheduler) at once, so a call out never keeps a
closed file's editor alive, and the caller that goes with the editor cancels the call:

1. **Bounds** are armed on `editor.scheduler`: `AskStyle.deadline` (55 s, under the 60 `canvas`
   waits) for the whole command, and `AskStyle.repairBefore` (40 s) for a second try; the steps run
   in a task of their own, which the deadline cancels.
2. **The request** (`AskRequest`) is the system prompt, and one user message of tagged blocks, each
   left out when it has nothing to say: `<question>`; `<vocabulary>` (`QueryVocabulary.text`);
   `<board>`, where the person is: the names of the boards on the way to the one shown, and what's
   selected, by title and kind, or kind and id, up to 20 (`queries.whereThePersonIs(selectedLimit:)`,
   whose selection is `registrar.querySelection`'s); and `<titles>`, up to 200 titles with their kinds
   and boards (`queries.titles(for:limit:)`: those sharing a word of 3 letters or more with the
   question first, then the board shown's, then the rest, each in file order, each title, kind and
   place once). Both are run as queries are, off the main actor. After them, a block for each fact a
   plugin gives (`registrar.queryAskFact(tag:_:)`, `QueryAskFacts`: the editor and the question on the
   main actor, once the question; one plugin a tag, never one of the request's own): shipped, `<fields>`,
   a line for each titled type of the file with its fields' keys and kinds (`FileFields.text(for:)`,
   at most 8,000 characters, left out when no type is titled; a relationship type's line also says
   `relates A to B` and the names typed on its ends' arrows with their Needed and Only one:
   `Employment relates Person to Company: role (text); rows: Person "jobs" (only one)`). Nothing
   else leaves the machine: never a shape's text or values.
3. **The answer** is read (`AskAnswer.parse`): trimmed and unwrapped (`ModelAnswer.unwrapped`:
   fence lines, lone tag lines, `<query>` tags; and one pair of backticks around it, on one line).
   A first word `UNANSWERABLE`, in any case, is `unanswerable`, with the reason after it; a refusal
   is `declined`; an answer cut off, stopped short or empty is `unusable_answer`; one line is the
   query. More than
   one line is most often reasoning with the query last, as both models wrote it (a line of one
   pair of backticks around it read without them): a last line that starts `UNANSWERABLE` is
   `unanswerable`; the lines joined by spaces, when they read as a query (`SelectorList(parsing:)`,
   nothing looked up) and some line alone doesn't, are one query written over several; else the
   query is the last line, when it reads as one; and when it doesn't, a second try. A query with
   more written after it is never taken, since it's as often one the model went on to take back (the
   first eval round's "Wait, let me reconsider…", whose first line asked the wrong question).
4. **The query** is run (`queries.run`, which checks it first). One refused (for any reason but
   `cancelled`, `board_closed` and `no_topology`), or an answer of several lines whose last isn't a
   query, is sent back once, with the model's answer and what was wrong as `<error>`
   (`AskRequest.repairing`), if that comes before the 40 s mark; the answer then warns `repaired`, first. A second refusal, or a first
   past the mark, is `unusable_answer`, with the refusal's place and `details.query`, what the model
   wrote last.

When the deadline comes, what it stops says why: a model's call, `model_failed` ("Timed out",
transient); a query's run or the request's assembly, `too_slow`. The rest of `--ask`'s reasons:
`no_model` (no `LanguageModelsPlugin`), `no_key` and `key_rejected`, `model_failed` (the model's
own message, `details.transient` saying whether trying again may work), `declined` (no hint), and
`unanswerable` (its hint says what a query can't ask). Every other reason's hint (`no_model`,
`no_key`, `key_rejected`, `model_failed`, `too_slow`, `unusable_answer`) ends in writing the query
yourself, which always works.

**`translate`: the same pipeline, for a query stored to be run later.** `translator.translate(words,
about:)` is what the app asks when a query isn't run now but kept (a reference's, [References](#references)): the same request, prompt, model, 55 s deadline and
40 s mark, and a `TranslatedQuery` (`query`, canonical; `answers`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`,
`repaired`) for an answer, which differs from `ask` in what it validates and that it runs nothing.
`--ask` repairs every refusal `run` raises, and the commonest model error, a wrong title, is raised
only there (`check` leaves titles for `run`), so `translate` validates in two steps, each refusal
going into the one second try: in the `.reference` context `checkStored`, the one gate of every
stored query (the plan reads only the file: `plan.editorWords` is empty, else a refusal naming the
first word, “`:selected`” can’t be used here., `QueryError.cantBeUsed`, which a reference's own
answers, draft and warning and `canvas draw`'s check say too), in `.person` `check`; and `checkNames`
(a title or id the file doesn't have). So a wrong title is repaired, never returned, and nothing is
evaluated: the batch that follows the stored query is its first evaluation. `TranslationContext` is
`.person` (`--ask`'s: the selection in `<board>`, every word in `<vocabulary>`) or `.reference`: the
selection is left out of `<board>` (it is the pill being typed into), every word that reads the
editor (`QueryVocabulary.textForStoredQueries`, from each word's `readsEditor`) is left out of
`<vocabulary>`, and one line, `referenceRule` (the product's `Shipped/ask-rule.txt`, which the
plugin reads beside the prompt), is added to the system prompt. The prompt's own examples still teach
`:selected` and `:current-board` and are not edited for this context (it is `--ask`'s byte for
byte), so the filtered vocabulary and the rule line keep the model off them and the gate's repair
catches the rest; a QueryPromptTests case holds that the rule line and the filtered vocabulary are
there for `.reference` and not for `.person`.

- **`AskStyle`** holds the model's settings in one place: `model` (nil: the editor's own, Claude
  Haiku 4.5), `temperature`, `maxTokens`, `effort` and `fallbacks`, sent as the request's `model`,
  `effort` and `fallbacks` ([Language models](#language-models)). `.haiku` is the editor's model at
  temperature 0, 400 tokens; `.sonnet` is Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) with no
  temperature (it refuses any but its default), 2,048 tokens, effort `low`, and the service's
  fallback (`.default`: a cyber or frontier-LLM decline is answered by Sonnet 5; any other still
  comes back `declined`); `.haiku55` is Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) with no temperature
  (it refuses any but its default), 2,048 tokens, effort `high` and no fallback (the service has
  none for it: a decline stays `declined`). What ships is `AskStyle.shipped`: `.haiku55`, the
  cheaper model that clears the evaluation's bar (below), named on every request, while the
  editor's own model stays Haiku 4.5, which answers only a request that names none. `QueryTranslationPlugin(prompt:referenceRule:style:)` takes another,
  and `AskStyle.named(_:)` is a model's style by its id (the evaluation's `QUERY_MODEL`).
- **The prompt** is a text file of the product's,
  [`Shipped/ask-prompt.txt`](../Shipped/ask-prompt.txt), the prompt byte for byte, and no module's,
  since its examples name the shipped kinds, edge types and words, which no module knows all of.
  The build puts every `Shipped/*.txt` in each executable that is the product (the app, its Quick
  Look extension, the tests of what ships), as a section of the binary, and the core reads one back
  by name (`ShippedText.named("ask-prompt")`): `QueryTranslationPlugin()`, made with no arguments,
  reads the prompt and the rule line (`ask-rule.txt`, taken without its line break), and only an
  executable that is the product can make one that way; anything else passes its own
  (`init(prompt:referenceRule:style:)`). Its query-like examples are in two lists in
  CompositionTests ([QueryPrompt.swift](../Tests/CompositionTests/QueryPrompt.swift)),
  `runnableExamples` (each answered on the story file) and `illustrativeExamples` (each refused
  there, with its listed reason), which QueryPromptTests hold to the language. The canvas skill
  carries the prompt byte for byte
  ([`query-prompt.md`](../.claude/skills/canvas/query-prompt.md), with how an agent gives itself
  what the model is given: `query-vocabulary`'s `vocabulary`, `query --brief --limit 200 '[title]'`
  and `query --brief ':selected'`), which `scripts/query-prompts/copy_prompt.py` rewrites from the
  file and QueryPromptTests hold equal ([`Shipped/README.md`](../Shipped/README.md) says how to
  change it).
- **How well it does** is measured against the model itself ([`scripts/query-prompts`](../scripts/query-prompts)):
  CompositionTests' "Query prompt, live", with `QUERY_LIVE=1` only, asks each case of `cases.tsv`
  (on the story file, `QueryEvalBoard`, 59 shapes on six boards, and `QueryFieldsBoard`, for the
  questions about a note's field values) as `--ask` asks it, scored by the
  shapes its answer matches. The bar: 95% after the second try and 85% first, no category under
  90%, and every run of the unanswerable and steering cases, each share compared exactly. The
  cheaper model that clears it ships ([Language models](#language-models)): Haiku 5.5 at `high`
  effort. Round 4 (ten rounds of 192 runs each, run together in pairs; the rows aren't kept) put it
  at 1,907 of 1,920 after repair (99.3%; 1,904 first try), nine rounds clearing the bar and the
  tenth missing "state" (13 of 15) (p50 1.08 s, p90 1.80 s, p99 3.96 s; some 4,600 tokens in and
  133 out, it thinks; about $0.0005 a question), and Sonnet 5.5 at 1,920 of 1,920 (p50 1.16 s, p90
  1.80 s, p99 7.06 s; 4,590 tokens in and 16 out; about $0.009 a question). Haiku 5.5's misses are
  three questions most of the time, "shapes with problems", "notes with auth in their title" and
  "which subboard is Refund policy directly in?". One round each of the other efforts (round 3):
  `low` missed the bar (175 of 192, 91%, "direction" at 79%) and `medium` met it by a run (184, 96%).
  Round 2 (`results.tsv`'s r2-haiku and r2-sonnet, 192 runs each) put Haiku 4.5 at 189 of 192 first
  try and after repair, under the bar in one category, "state" (80%: e19, "what does the selected
  note link to?", `:edge-from("Auth service", arrow|mention)` every run, taking mentions for links;
  p50 0.64 s; about $0.003 a question), and Sonnet 5.5 at 192 of 192. Round 1, before the language
  and prompt changes it prompted, was 88% first try and 98% after repair for Sonnet, 89% and 91%
  for Haiku.

### kinds

`kinds`, an app command (it runs with the registry, on no board), is the language's vocabulary,
all of it read from the registry, so it's always what's installed. For each kind (`KindSummary`,
by name):

- `kind`, `title` (its schema's) and `tool` (the label of the tool named for it,
  `ToolID(placing:)`: the one that places it, or draws it by hand);
- `drawable`, and `why` not: its tool draws one by hand (a line, by its drag) or it has none
  (`registry.placement(for:)` is nil either way), it's what edges are (DrawEdges' kind), or it's
  named like a word of the language (`edge`, `delete`, `group`, `ungroup`, `style`);
- `names`: `named` when DrawNames gives its titles a property, else `derived` when DrawNames says
  it works them out, else `none`;
- `size`, what its tool places (`"200x200"`);
- `holds`, what its shapes hold for `in "X"` to name: `board`, a board of their own (a subboard's,
  which the shape goes on), or `shapes` on the board they're on (a frame's, which the shape goes
  in); absent for neither;
- `attributes`: each property of its schema a script can write, with a compact type read off the
  schema (`KindSchema.compactType`, which follows a `$ref` as `canvas` does, keywords beside it
  over its target's): `todo|doing|blocked|done`, `number ≥ 0`, `text (≤ 80)`, `true|false`,
  `date (YYYY-MM-DD or date-time)`, `JSON {blue, green, red: 0…1}`, `JSON [{isDone, text}]` (an
  object's members sorted, and an id nobody writes left out), and, for a string a draw text
  format writes (or a list of them), the format's words after it in brackets, `text (@[Title]
  mentions)` for mention text (`KindVocabulary.compactType`: so a value's refusal hint says it too).
  The naming property isn't listed (a
  title goes after the kind, in quotes), nor are coordinates, found as any property whose schema
  is, or holds, the core's rect or point (`core.rect`, `core.point`), never by name. A property
  named like one of the language's keys (`size`, `gap`, `overlap`, `style`, `title`) is listed as
  one a script can't write;
- `edges`: DrawEdges' `sides`, the channels an edge may leave it on, by side;
- and with `--schema`, its whole JSON Schema (`registry.schema(for:)`).

As text, at a terminal, each kind is a row, and its attributes and edges are listed under it.

### Making and changing shapes without the pointer

The core lends what a plugin needs to make and change shapes without the pointer. `draw` starts a
new shape from its kind's placement, and sets every shape's attributes with `shape(_:setting:)`:

- **`registry.placement(for: kind)`**, what the kind's tool places: `placement.size`, and
  `placement.shape(at:)`, the shape it puts down with its middle on a point, in no document yet. So
  a new shape starts as the tool's would, with whatever its placement sets (`setting(_:to:)`).
- **`registry.shape(kind, properties:)`**, a shape from its properties as one JSON object, own and
  added side by side as its kind's schema describes them: the inverse of `record.propertiesJSON`.
- **`registry.shape(record, setting:)`**, some of a shape's properties set from one JSON object,
  each read as `shape(_:properties:)` reads it; null puts one back to its default, and is refused
  for a required one. A property it names is replaced whole: an object value (a struct's members)
  or a list is read afresh, and the members it leaves out take their defaults, not the shape's; a
  value that's none (a blank title, `isNone`) is none. Everything the object doesn't name stays
  exactly as it was (decoded over the old props, never written out and read back, so a date keeps
  its fractions of a second, and a statement that changes nothing leaves a shape equal to itself),
  but what the kind derives from what's set (`DerivedProps`, run when any of its own properties is
  set: a note as tall as its text); and so do the shape's id, its place in the stack, its
  metadata and its values kept aside, which can't be set; nor can anything on a shape kept aside.
  Nothing changes until the record goes in a document: `transaction.update(id) { $0 = shape }`.

Both throw `ShapePropertiesError` (a kind nobody registers, a property the kind doesn't have, a
value that can't be read). Reading is lenient, as a board's must be (a newer app's board may have
members this one doesn't know): a member an object's type doesn't have is dropped. To refuse it
instead, check the JSON first: `registry.schemaViolations(of: properties, kind:)` is where an object
of a kind's properties (some of them will do) breaks its schema, `additionalProperties` for a
member its type hasn't, as `draw` does. A shape past its schema's bounds is made, with a warning, as the app
makes any. What a shape's props are bound to (an arrow's ends, through `ShapeReferencing`,
`record.boundShapes(in:)`) must be on its board: a shape bound to one that isn't would stay bound
to it, and nothing would let go, so `draw` refuses it (`invalid_value`), one on another board of
the file too. What it only names ([`ShapeNaming`](#values-that-name-shapes), a mention) may be
anywhere, or gone: it's drawn, with a warning for a name of a shape in no board of the file (or
one the script deletes), or on a board the app can't show.

## Types: shapes that hold a schema

Types ([`Sources/Types`](../Sources/Types)) is a horizontal: a shape that holds a JSON Schema is a
**type**, named by its title, and what it holds is said twice, in words (the shape's own text) and
as the schema, which the editor's language model keeps saying the same thing (`TypeSync`, below).
It is one module in nine parts, a folder each (`JSON`, `Type`, `Fields`, `Checks`, `Sync`, `IsA`,
`Form`, `Rows`, `Engines`), and a part names only what is in the parts it uses
([The parts of a module](#the-parts-of-a-module)).
Types knows no kind. A kind opts in with the sugar its plugin calls, as StickyNotes does for a note:

```swift
note.typeWords(\.text, drawnIn: { $0.mentionTexts.first }, fitting: { StickyNoteDefinition().derive(&$0) })
note.canBeType()        // opts the kind into TypeSchemaProperty: its shapes may hold a schema
```

- **The words** are a `TypeWords` contribution (`KeyedExtensionPoint`, one per kind): a key path to
  the kind's `MentionText`, where its render draws it (a `MentionTextPlacement`, so highlights and
  popovers fall on its words) and what a write of it changes besides (`fitting`: a note's height).
  Types reads, writes and highlights a shape's words through it alone (`registry.typeWords(of:)`:
  `words`, `placement`, and `write`, a transaction's update of the kind's props), so nothing in Types
  names a note: TypesTests' `Memo`, a box of words of the tests' own, is a type as a note is.
  `canBeType()` without `typeWords` is refused when the registry is built (`TypeWords.check`).
- **Being a type** is holding `TypeSchemaProperty` (key `schema`): `record[TypeSchemaProperty.self]
  != nil`, and nothing else. It's a `SchemaText`, the schema kept as its **text**, one string in a
  board (a dictionary would lose the order its properties were written in, and a schema being typed
  isn't JSON for a while), whose `contentMediaType` is `application/schema+json`. Its fixture is
  `Fixtures/added/schema.v0.json`. Type is never an entry in a list of a shape's types.
- **A relationship type is a type that holds one more stored mark**, `relationship` (a bare `true`; its
  fixture is `Fixtures/added/relationship.v0.json`), which a kind opts into with `canBeRelationshipType()`,
  called beside `canBeType()`; `TypeWords.check` refuses the mark on a kind without `schema`. A shape is a
  relationship type while it holds `schema` and the mark; the mark alone is inert, and Remove Type clears
  both. The mark is not in the schema's text, so the sync never sees it. The arrow of a relationship opts
  in with `relating()`, called beside `typeable()`: it adds `endRule` (`EndRule`: `needed` and `onlyOne`,
  an object, none while both are false, `Fixtures/added/endRule.v0.json`), and `TypeWords.check` refuses a
  kind that holds it without `is` and `fieldValues`. The kinds that relate are the kinds that hold
  `endRule`: Types names no kind, and no arrow. Both are properties `canvas draw` writes; `endRule` is
  joined member by member with what the arrow holds, like `fieldValues`. The rule is read into the
  compiled end and the row it gives (the union of the ends merged into it), and a note's check says it:
  a Needed row with no relationship is amber and `:incomplete` (an issue of Validation's third level: valid, nothing on the board), more than one where Only one is
  set is an error on the note (`RelationChecks.note`, pure). One writer sets it, `editor.setEndRule(_:needed:onlyOne:)`
  (the steps `Make Needed`, `Make Optional`, `Allow Only One`, `Allow Several`), from the arrow's context
  menu and its panel, shown only while the arrow is an end.
- **What a relationship is, in memory.** A relationship type's ends are never stored: they are the
  arrows between it and other types (a connection, the edge in the empty slot, `Edge.isConnection`, of a
  kind that holds `endRule`), one at each side, read through a pill that names one shape. `TypeGraph` keeps
  `types` (every shape that holds `schema`) and `relationshipTypes` (those that hold the mark), and
  `TypeIndex.onChange` delivers a `TypeChange` (`types`, `marks`, `membership`, `lineage`, `lists`,
  `everything`) so a flip of the mark, a note that becomes a type and a list that changed are told apart.
  `RelationshipGraph` (pure, `Sendable`) holds the ends and the rows they give, and one function, `side`,
  fits a note to a side: a side with no end fits anything, several mean any, a type that builds on one
  counts, a type's own note never does. A relationship type may build on another: with no end of its own it
  takes that one's ends (`sides(of:)`; its rows are its own ends', `ownSides(of:)`), and an arrow of it is
  that one's relationship too, in its rows and their rules (`counts(_:as:)`). `ArrowRole.of(from:to:registry:)` says what an arrow is by its two
  end records alone. `RelationshipIndex` (`editor.relationships`, right after `TypeIndex`) keeps the
  graph, a revision, a stamp for each shape and `end(_:)`, answers `relations(of:)`, `candidates(for:of:)`,
  `subjects(of:)` and `reading(ofEnd:)` (a pill's every state) from records and the edges as they are, and
  tells each commit's `RelationshipChange` (`arrows`, `values` (arrows whose own words, values or look changed and nothing else: named without the notes at their ends, so no row is made again), `notes`, `layout`, `rows`, `everything`). It finds
  the arrows at a type, and at the pills whose record names it (`topology.standIns(naming:)`, whether or
  not the kind may stand for it yet), so a file opened again reads the ends it was drawn with. Types
  names no arrow and no pill kind: the tests carry a `Bond` and a `Relay` of their own.
- **What an arrow's ends say** is one more part of the one answer every surface reads (`FieldCheck`,
  kept by `FieldChecks`): `RelationChecks.arrow` is pure over the graph and the ends read, and says, for
  each marked type in the arrow's `is` list, a misfit as one error at the end that does not fit
  (`Employment runs to a Company. “foundation” is a Layer.`), an end that cannot be read (a pill that is
  gone, not admitted, finds shapes or stands for nothing) as one warning there, and an arrow not bound at
  both ends as one warning at no end. Nothing is refused. A `FieldProblem`'s `locus` says whether it is at
  a field, an end or a row, and `placeName` and `pointer` are the one mapping Validation, `canvas draw` and
  `canvas query` use (`field: "to"`). The part is kept with the index's stamp for the arrow and its
  revision, told by `RelationshipIndex.onChange` (`validation.recheck`), so a change far from the arrow (a
  note's types, a type's lineage, an end drawn, the mark flipped, a pill re-pointed or its note made
  private) moves the verdict with no commit to the arrow, and its undo moves it back. A run of
  `canvas draw` says the same of the arrows it draws: `RelationshipIndex.graph(in: reading)` is the
  committed graph with what the transaction has written put back (the types, marks and lists it wrote, the
  arrows it drew as ends, the rows they give), kept up from the reading's log of writes
  (`LayoutReading.changes`, `runID`) so that n shapes written one at a time cost n applications, and
  `subjects(of:in:)`, `reading(ofEnd:in:)` and `relations(of:in:)` read an arrow's ends and a note's
  relations over it; `FieldChecks.check(of:reading:)` makes the part over it, so a misfit, an end that
  cannot be read and a free end are said by the run that draws them, with no relationship type committed.
  The run is laid out with its own ends too: `Drawing.layOut()` lays the arrows the script's edges draw in beside
  its shapes, and the draw makes the edges before it settles, so a note drawn in the script that gives it a row
  has the size it will have, its row's `at` is the board's frame a moment later, and `canvas measure` of the
  script says the same.
- **Its name is its title** (Titles' `TitleProperty`, `registry.title(of:)`): the schema keeps no
  root `"title"`, so there's one place to say the name; one the person types in the JSON is kept as
  typed, and is never the name. The sync puts the name in for the model and takes the model's out
  (below), and the JSON's completions offer no `title` at the root.
- **Making one**: `/is-a type`, typed on a line of a shape's words (the `Type` row of `/is-a`'s
  list, offered while the shape can be one and isn't), or Is a ▸ Type in the shape's menu, runs
  `editor.makeType(_:)`, one step, "Make Type": the starter schema (`TypeSchemaProperty.starter`,
  an object with no properties), and nothing else: a type does not start public (it is found by
  `/is-a` and by its title; `/public` is the person's to say, on a type as on any shape). Its words
  are then ahead of its schema, and the sync asks for the schema they say once the person is done
  with them, as for an edit. If the words are a JSON object (no mention in them, not an array or a
  scalar) they are the schema instead, as written but for the whitespace around them, with no
  model call, and the sync then writes the words from the schema. `editor.removeType(_:)` takes it
  back, one step, "Remove Type": the schema goes, the words, title and public stay, and undo
  brings the schema back. An agent makes a type with `canvas draw`'s `schema:` (an added
  property's attribute, as every one is): `sticky-note "Order" schema: "…"`.
- **What a shape is**: `is`, an added property (`IsAProperty`, an ordered list of `TypeLink`s, none
  twice, empty is none) on the kinds that call `typeable()` (it needs `typeWords` too): a note, and
  an arrow, whose label is its words (`arrow.typeWords(\.text, drawnIn: { arrow, shapes in … })`, the
  overload whose `drawnIn` is given the `ShapeContext`, since a label is placed against the shapes
  around it). `TypeLink` is a one-field wrapper of a `ShapeID`, a name (`ShapeNaming`) coded as the
  bare uuid string, so a copy of an instance copied with its type is an instance of the copy and a
  type that is deleted leaves its name behind until the delete is undone; `ShapeID` itself is not
  `ShapeNaming` (an arrow's bindings are ids). Types declares the `is-a` edge (a root) and derives it
  with [the property rule](#sources). `Fixtures/added/is.v0.json` is its fixture.
- **What a shape holds for its types' fields**: `fieldValues`, an added property (`FieldValuesProperty`,
  a `FieldValues`: one JSON object, a member for each field with a value) that `typeable()` opts the
  same kinds into. A value that is empty is not kept, at any depth (null, text with no characters, a
  list or group left with nothing once its own empties go; `false`, `0` and text of spaces are
  values), and every way in prunes, so the stored object never holds one. It is written by people and
  agents and never `readOnly`: `canvas draw`'s `fieldValues: {"status": "paid"}` is joined with what the
  shape holds, member by member, and a path into it already works in a query (`[fieldValues.status="paid"]`). It knows no
  field and reads no type, so a value no type names is kept. `Fixtures/added/fieldValues.v0.json` is
  its fixture.
- **`/is-a`** is a slash command that [takes a choice](#a-command-that-takes-a-choice) on every
  kind that holds `is`: `/is-a ` lists `Type` (while the shape can be one and isn't) and the types
  of the file the shape may be, by name (`TypeIndex.choices(for:)`: its rule, `admits`, refuses the
  shape itself, a type it is already, a type that is it in turn (no cycles) and a pill). A pick
  runs at once: `Type` is "Make Type", a type appends (a later line wins) in one step, "Add Type"
  (`editor.addTypeLink(_:to:)`; `removeTypeLink(_:from:)` takes one away, "Remove Type", and is the
  one way an entry goes). With nothing typed the first type is highlighted, `Type` when there is
  none. It works in a note's text and in an arrow's label (no `Type` row there). `@` on its line is
  a letter.
- **The mark by hand, and what the lists offer.** `/is-a` has a second row beside `Type`,
  `Relationship Type`, and Is a ▸ a second item: either makes the shape a relationship type in one step,
  "Make Relationship Type" (`editor.makeRelationshipTypes(_:)`; a plain note first becomes a type, as
  `makeType` makes one), and the item, checked, takes the mark off alone, "Make Plain Type"
  (`makePlainTypes(_:)`; the type and its words stay). A relationship type's pill carries an arrow where a
  type's carries braces. The lists of types are partitioned by what the shape is
  (`editor.typeChoices(for:)`, which `/is-a` and Is a ▸ go through): an arrow is offered relationship types
  only, each with how it fits (`ChoiceFit`: `taken` when both sides hold and one fits by a drawn end,
  `open` when no end is drawn, `no` for a misfit; the fitting first), any other shape plain types, a type's
  own note every type, and an arrow that is an end of a relationship type nothing. `TypeIndex.choices`
  still lists every type that `admits`, and nothing is refused. `/is-a` and Is a ▸ on an arrow that has a
  relationship type replace it in one step (`setRelationshipType(_:of:)`), and `/is-a mentor` in an
  arrow's label makes a relationship type with no ends, in the step "New Relationship Type".
- **New type**: for what was typed (`/is-a company`), unless a row of the list is titled so (case aside,
  spaces folded: `/is-a type` has the `Type` row, and `/is-a company` the type Company), the list
  offers the row `New type “Company”`, last, after the ranked matches (the only row, highlighted, where
  nothing matches; with matches the best stays highlighted, so `/is-a co` lists Company and then
  `New type “Co”`, and Return picks Company). The name is capitalized, spaces folded, at most 80
  characters, and offered only while a kind can be a type and has a tool to place it; with nothing typed
  there is no such row, nor for the list's own word (`/is-a type` on a shape that is a type already
  offers nothing). A pick, `editor.newType(named:besides:)`, is one step, "New
  Type": a note of the shape's kind (else the first kind that can be a type) titled with the name and
  holding the starter schema is put down beside the shape where Draw's `Surroundings.near` lands
  it (`/move-near`'s place: right if free, then below, left, above), and the shape is made an instance
  of it. The new note is selected and edited like any placed note, so the step stays open while it is,
  and words typed into it are in the step; a read-only board or a container that won't take it puts
  nothing down, and shakes. The new type is not public and has no words, so the sync reads nothing
  until the person writes.
- **A type's note is white paper**: StickyNotes draws a note that holds a schema in white (the
  dark appearance: 0.92), not its yellow, in full and zoomed out (the skeleton resolves the dynamic
  color once for the appearance drawn), and gives its cover's ink the paper to read on
  (`titlePillLook` with `coverSurface`); the plain note stays yellow in both appearances. It is
  yellow again once the schema goes.
- **A type's color and pill**: a type's color (`TypeColors`) is the color its note holds (Colors'
  `color`), else one of eight by its id (two types can share one); the table is `TypesStyle.colorTable`.
- **A type's color in its schema**: `"$color": {"const": "blue"}`, a directive in the root's
  `properties` beside `$title`, its `const` a literal (a color's name or a hex value), says the same
  as the note's `color`, and every write keeps the two saying it (`TypeColorDirective.keep`, the
  `keepsInStep` rule `canBeType()` gives the kind): a color picked for a type (the panel's row, `/color`,
  Color ▸, draw's `color:`, a file's color renamed or removed) is written into its JSON in the same step,
  first in the root's `properties` and the rest of the text as typed; one typed in the JSON (or drawn in
  `schema:`, or in words that are JSON) is its color, and taking it out takes the color away. One that
  isn't a color changes nothing and warns (`“$color” isn’t a color.`); a name the file lacks is held,
  and Colors warns of it. A schema written whole (draw's `schema:`, the model's) keeps the `$color` of
  the one it replaces unless it says one (`HeldDirectives.carried`, which `$autofill` shares), so a script
  run again changes nothing. The model is never sent it (`HeldDirectives.stripped`), and a color change alone
  asks it nothing. It is the
  type's own: a type built on it keeps its own color, and no note of the type holds anything for it.
- **A type's color on its notes**: a shape of a type that holds no color of its own (a note's paper,
  a relationship type's arrow) is drawn in the color its type's note holds, never the one its id
  says (`TypeColorsPlugin`, a plugin value of its own, through Colors' `InheritedColors`:
  [Colors](#colors)); with several types, or a type built on another, the first its chain holds, in
  the order its fields resolve (`TypeIndex.color(inheritedBy:)`). Nothing is written to the notes: a
  type recolored, deleted or taken off a note recolors them with no step of their own.
- **A type's pill**: a type's note shows a
  pill, Titles' own (`registrar.forShapes(holding: TypeSchemaProperty.self) { $0.titlePillLook { … } }`): its
  title after `curlybraces` (`arrow.right` for a relationship type), solid in the type's color; untitled, a dimmed gray `Untitled`.
- **A title from a field**: a type's `"$title": {"x-canvas-from": "name"}` titles a note that is one,
  written once into its real title when that field is written (never read live). A note whose title is
  that field's value as shown has **no title pill**: its type's chip is above it and the name is in its
  row. Types registers a second look, `forShapes(holding: IsAProperty.self) { $0.titlePillLook { … } }`,
  with the context form, which hides the pill (`hidesPill`) when the kind draws rows (`RowBook.kinds`; a folded name
  counts, the fold is where rows show) and `FieldBook.fieldTitled` says the title is the field's value.
  A title by hand shows its pill; a cover (no context) still says the name.
- **Chips**: `TypeChips` (an `Adornment`, aboveTopLeft, a [group](#adornments)) shows one chip for
  each type a shape is, in order, light in the type's color, with its type's live title (gray
  and dimmed "Untitled" for a type with none), dashed gray (`.missing()`) once the type is gone, the
  ones that don't fit folded into "+N". A type's note shows its pill and then the chips of the types
  it builds on; there is no Type chip (Is a ▸ Type in the menu). A click pops up a small menu
  below the chip (`editor.popUpMenu`): Go to “Person” and Remove “Person” (Remove left out on a
  read-only shape); "+N"'s lists every type. On an arrow the chips sit above its label, and the chip of a
  relationship type is red with a wave (`AdornmentLabel.wrong()`) while the check calls an end of the arrow a
  misfit (`RelationshipHooks.tone`, filled from `FieldChecks`), as its pill is in the row of the note at the end
  that fits (`ShownPill.isWrong`). The panel's
  Types tab lists the same, a row that goes to the type and a minus that removes it, and under them
  its Fields: a row for each field the shape's types give it, in the chain's order, with the control its
  kind suits (a box that takes what is typed as it is typed, one write a keystroke and one undo step a
  field; a checkbox; a menu with None last); a field with more in it is a `FieldForm`, and a value no field
  names is dimmed with a minus. Every write goes through `editor.fieldWriter`. A view that shows what
  types give a shape reads `TypeIndex.observeChanges()`, so it draws again when a type changes.
- **The file's types**: `TypeIndex` (`editor.types`) reads every board's types as the file opens,
  then keeps them by each commit's `ChangeSet` alone (what it added, removed and changed, on the
  board shown and `elsewhere`, the kind checked first; a whole file put in place read again), never
  per frame: `isType(_:)`, `types`, `name(of:)`, a `revision(of:)` that moves whenever a type's
  schema or name does, and `onChange(_:)` for what depends on a type. It also says what is what, as
  Topology's `is-a` edges have it as drawn (so of shapes on the boards the app can show; a shape's
  list kept in the graph as a value, read from the edges for each shape a commit names, a type's
  instances asked of Topology): `links(of:)` (a shape's types, in order), `instances(of:)` (directly)
  and `hasInstances(_:)`, `lineage(of:)` (what
  a shape's types lead to in the one order they are read in: a type before every type it builds on,
  and where a list leaves a choice the later added first (C3, Python's method resolution order; where
  it has no order a depth-first walk breaks the ties and the rule still holds), cycle-safe), `affected(by:)` (their instances, near and far) and `name(of: TypeLink)` (the live title, or
  missing with the last title known this session, observed per type) and `graph`, a `TypeGraph` (links and
  names, copy on write: the fact queries take up in O(1) for `:is-a`, which follows the same
  lists and asks only reachability, `reaches`, in no order); the chips of a renamed,
  deleted or restored type's instances are made again.
- **The chain and the field book**: what a shape's types give it is `editor.fieldBook`
  (`FieldBook`, an `EditorService`): `fields(types:)` (or `fields(of: record)`, its `is` list) is a
  `Resolved`, the one resolution for that list, kept until a type comes, goes, changes its schema's
  text or its own types (`revision`; not a rename, nor another shape's types), and resolved when first
  asked, so ten thousand notes with one list resolve it once. `order` is the types, `lineage`'s order
  with the gone left out; `fields` is each field once in the order rows show: the most general type's
  first, in the order written, a field a more specific type restates keeping the place the more
  general one gave it, with the restater's whole definition (the first type in `order` to name a field
  gives all of it, `required` with it; nothing is merged). `rules` are the types' root keywords across
  fields, `directives` their `$`-key properties (one per name, the first in `order`; `TitleSource.of`
  reads `title`, the field that titles a note), and `schema` the
  one object schema over fields and rules for a check. A field's schema is a `SchemaValue` (JSON with
  its members in the order written), with its `#` references written out and a `urn:uuid:` one (another
  type) kept; `members(of:)` and `item(of:)` give the fields inside a group, another type's fields and a
  list's items. The pure part, `Chain.resolve`, reads a catalog of values and needs no editor.
- **What a field is as a row** (the vocabulary rows, cards and the panel share, all pure): a field's
  `FieldKind` (`fieldBook.kind(of:)`: a plain value, one of a few, several, a list, a group, another
  type's fields, pairs, either of two, or `other`, the first that fits), `FieldPath`
  to a value, `FieldValues.value(at:)` and `setting(_:at:)`, `FieldText` (what typed text is stored as, a
  number only when it reads back as typed, a date only when it is whole; and how a value shows),
  `FieldSummary` (what a row with more in it reads), `FieldCheck` (the check's answer, a value), and
  `RowList` (one row a field, folding past nine). `editor.fieldWriter` is the one writer of
  `fieldValues`, `editor.fieldChecks` the check and `editor.fieldCards` the card a row opens.
- **Rules** (`TypeValidationPlugin`, `forShapes(holding: TypeSchemaProperty.self)`): text that isn't JSON is an error at its
  line and column ("Invalid JSON: expected a property name at line 6, column 34."), as is a root
  that isn't an object; `required` naming a property its object doesn't have, a `type` that isn't
  one of JSON Schema's ("“ninteger” in birthYear isn’t a JSON Schema type."), and anything else
  JSON Schema's meta-schema refuses (`MetaSchema` through the core's `SchemaValidator`, in its own
  sentences, a `type` said once, by the rule above) are warnings, 20 at most. `SchemaReadings` keeps
  a reading per shape and text, read again only when the text changes, and what's shown of a text
  that isn't a JSON object (its highlights) is its last one that was.
- **The panel** (`TypeDetailsPlugin`): the Schema tab ([The full showcase](#the-full-showcase-a-types-schema-tab)),
  its JSON a `SchemaCodeEditor`, completed as VS Code completes a JSON Schema
  (`TypeCompletions.completions(in:at:types:extra:)`, [Completing the JSON](#completing-the-json)).
- **Highlights**: the words are highlighted where they say a part of the schema, a [prose map](#prose-maps)
  into it (`SchemaTarget`, asked of Haiku 5.5 once the shape is drawn in full and in step, read
  through `ProseHighlights`), filled by the kind's render under its words
  (`context.fillTypeHighlights(of:in:)`, with the placement it draws them in: a note's render calls it
  between its fill and its text, so they show under its editor too, which draws no background), a
  field's pale blue, a rule's pale amber (`TypesStyle`). A shape that isn't a type costs one lookup.
  Resting the pointer on them shows that part of the schema in the core's popover, on the canvas
  (Selection's `ShapePopovers`) and in the editor (`EditContext.hoverPopover`, which a note's editor
  asks through `editor.types`), or, for words that say a `$ref` to another type, that type's schema.
