  ([`setDrawingOffset`](#the-cores-part-drawing-offsets): a shaking shape, away from where it is,
  with its outline), in full or, zoomed out, as its [skeleton](#skeletons) (a shape's shadow,
  `fillWithShadow`'s, is left out where its fill hides it: an opaque color over all the context
  draws into, a shape zoomed in past the view's edges, where its blur, 48 points at 800%, took some
  24 ms of a frame on the CPU, a bitmap's or a headless window's; on screen the GPU blurs it, and
  frames held 60 fps); every plugin's outlines
  (`registrar.outlines`: selection, the box around several; none while the session
  `hidesOutlines`) and the hint, in one pass at a constant screen width, over the faint ones
  (`Outlines.faintShapes`: the hover), drawn before them, wider and lighter, and those over the
  tinted groups (`Outlines.tinted`: a plugin's own colors, drawn first of all, [Outlines](#outlines)),
  each asked for its path and
  stroked only if its shape's kept extent meets the area the shapes were drawn for, grown by what
  an outline [stands off its shape](#outlines) by (a plugin's rects too; zoomed out, a skeleton's
  outline, and a rect filled as a ring: [Skeletons](#skeletons));
  world overlays; the running session's `draw(in:)` (the marquee, Snapping's guides); view overlays
  (Selection's handles first). Each shape, overlay and session draws with a fresh graphics state.
  Sizes meant as view points are divided by `zoom` in world space. So outlines cost what's in view
  in strokes, and each outlined shape a look at its kept extent a frame, with nothing copied or
  allocated: `editor.outlines` hands the first source's list (⌘A's, every shape) over as it is, and
  leaves out a faint shape outlined in full without a set of the whole selection; a pan works
  [Selection](#selection)'s box around them out again too, a pass over their kept bounds. With all
  10,000 selected and none in view, a frame took about half a millisecond more than with none
  selected (0.56 ms at 100%, 0.62 at 10%, as measured; `./build.sh bench` holds it to 1 ms).
- **The camera** is `editor.camera`, which anyone may set; setting it stops any camera motion
  running. `editor.animateCamera(to:duration:)` moves it there, eased (tldraw's cubic), a frame
  every 16 ms, and `Camera(fitting:in:inset:minZoom:maxZoom:)` (Geometry) makes one that shows a rect, in
  a view's size or a rect of it.
  `editor.cameraTarget` is where an animation is headed while it runs, else the camera: what to
  remember a view as mid-motion (Selection's steps back do).
  `editor.viewportSize` is the view's size in view points, zero until it has one, and
  `editor.unobscuredViewport` the part of it nothing the host puts over the canvas covers (the view
  less `coveredTop`, host API, how far down the host's views reach on a board: the path's pill
  inside a subboard, `BoardPath.coveredHeight(on:)`, which a board's window tells it from [the host's slots](#host-slots)), what
  a fit fits shapes into: a board's first visit, Zoom to Fit, Selection's `reveal`, and `canvas
  draw`'s `--reveal`, whose `view` is that part of it too.
- **Zooming** is the core's commands, which View's items run (through
  the board's window controller, dimmed while they can't run) and Keyboard gives keys: `.zoomIn`
  and `.zoomOut` (⌘= and ⌘-) go to the next of the stops (`Camera.zoomStops`: 10, 25, 50, 100,
  200, 400 and 800%) past the zoom where the camera's headed, around the view's center, dimmed at
  the last; `.zoomToActualSize` (⌘0, ⇧0) goes to 100%, dimmed there; `.zoomToFit` (⇧1, tldraw's)
  fits every shape of the board shown into view with a first visit's margin, as close as the zoom
  goes, dimmed on an empty board. Each eases the camera over 320 ms (tldraw's animationMediumMs),
  from where it's headed, so pressing again before it lands goes on from there. Zoom to Fit again,
  while the camera is still where the fit left it (at it, or headed for it), goes back to the camera
  from before the fit (Terminal Graph's), and once more fits; any other camera change (a pan, a
  zoom, a stop on the way) forgets it, and so does showing another board. `editor.zoomPercentage`
  is that zoom in whole percent, observed apart from `camera` and set only when it changes: the
  canvas shows it ("44%") above the minimap while it changes, and fades it out a second after
  (`ZoomIndicator`, CanvasUI); a pan never shows it. There's no zoom menu: pinching and
  ⌘-scrolling are how the app zooms. `.zoomToSelection` (⇧2) is Selection's.
- **The view.** `CanvasView` (CanvasUI) is the only AppKit in the loop. It converts events, reports
  its size, hosts the editing view over its shape, hands AppKit the menu for a secondary click, and draws the editor, all through the editor's `@_spi(Host)`
  API. It also hosts the minimap, in its bottom-left corner (`showsMinimap`; View › Show Minimap):
  every shape as a silhouette of its geometry (a container's, a frame's, its outline, so what it
  holds shows on it), the part of the board the canvas shows outlined, and the selection in the
  accent color, a hover's faintly, and what a plugin outlines in colors of its own
  ([`Outlines.tinted`](#outlines): Neighbors' lights) in those, under both, so what's lit off
  screen shows there: while anything is lit the rest of the picture dims (the minimap's background
  laid over it at 40%) and what's outlined is drawn over the part out of view's veil, not under it,
  and a shape in several groups shows each, one inset inside the other. It shows the board shown: on another board it starts a
  picture afresh (never over the old board's), and back on a board whose picture it kept, it shows
  that one at once. On a board with nothing to show (`shapeBounds` null) it's hidden, and the
  corner is the canvas's, with View › Show Minimap still on; it fades in with the first shape (a
  first shape placed under it by a press, or edited as it's placed, isn't covered as it arrives:
  the minimap waits for the press and the editing to end), and on another board shows or hides at
  once. It moves the camera as tldraw's minimap does, and knows
  no shape or plugin. Above it, the canvas shows the zoom while it changes (`ZoomIndicator`). Only the app, its Quick Look extension and tests can import CanvasUI, and no
  plugin can see the host API, so no plugin can reach around the editor.
- **The views the canvas hosts have the pointer where they are.** Over the minimap or the editing
  view the pointer isn't over the canvas, though AppKit tells the canvas it moved (its tracking
  area covers them): the tool hears it leave (`pointerExited`), once, as it moves there or is
  released there (the press that began editing: a double-click, or a click on a face that edits
  its shape), and nothing more until it moves
  back onto the canvas. So the select tool hovers no shape under them (over a note's text,
  `editor.hovered` is only what another plugin sets, a table of contents row's), and
  `editor.pointerOverCanvas` is nil there (a note being edited hides its port dots while the
  pointer is over its text). The canvas leaves their cursor alone meanwhile. Once editing ends,
  where the editing view was is the canvas again, for the next move.

### Services hear a change

A commit and another board shown are the two changes every service hears, in two rounds. In the
first, each takes the change in (`documentDidChange`, `boardDidChange`), told in the order the
services were made (plugin order, a service another one's `make` looks up first), each once. A
service looked up in that round takes the change in first, if it hasn't yet, so what reads a
service as services take a change in reads it as of that change, wherever the two are in the list:
Validation's rule asks Titles' index, which takes the commit in as it's asked; a layout provider
reads the service it answers from through `reading.service(_:)`; a first visit's camera fit lays the
board out before the switch is told. The service then isn't told again in its turn. What a service
looked up as it was made takes each change in before it does, so a reference it kept from its `make`
(for a frame's sake) reads as of the change whenever it hears, with no lookup.

```swift
extension NameRows: EditorService {
    func documentDidChange(_ changes: ChangeSet, in editor: CanvasEditor) {
        // Wherever NameIndex is in the list, looking it up has it take this commit in first.
        guard let index = editor.service(NameIndex.self) else { return }
        for id in changes.edited { rows[id] = index.name(of: id) }
    }
}
```

A service is busy while its own hook runs: asking for it then (it asks for itself, or what it read
or told asks for it back) is a mistake, which stops a debug build and names the services busy (the
app carries on, the service as it is, part way). What a service tells others of a change it tells
once it has taken the change in (`editor.onceHeard { … }`: as its hook returns, at once outside a
delivery), so they may read it then: Topology's followers, the type index's observers.

In the second round every service settles (`documentDidSettle`, `boardDidSettle`, nothing by
default), with every service holding the change and none busy, and then what waited for that runs
(`editor.onceSettled { … }`, in the order asked, at once outside a delivery). What asks what a
change affected, reads around the file, looks at what others laid out or tells the window waits for
the second round: Validation asks its rules' `affected` as it settles, the table of contents its
rows' and marks', Find's index follows; the select tool's look for a button under a still pointer,
Adornments' look at the pills whose room may have changed, and the cards' following of the
relationships wait with `onceSettled`. `setNeedsDisplay()` asked during a delivery is the change's
own redraw, which comes once services have settled; `refreshCursor()` reaches the host then.

Nothing may change the file while services hear or settle: a transaction (`transact`,
`transact(on:)`), a board shown, a file put in place or Delete Hidden Shapes then is a precondition
failure, so a service that writes in answer waits a turn (`editor.scheduler`), and no commit is
heard before the one that came before it. The other hooks (`didRefuseChanges`,
`shapeTintsDidChange`, `editingDidEnd`, `didPlace`, `toolDidChange`, `drawsSkeletonsDidChange`,
`boardWillChange`) are told in order, in one round. CanvasTests' DeliveryTests hold it.

### Outlines

The canvas outlines shapes in the accent color: the selection's, a hover's (wider and fainter), and
the hint, a target outlined whatever the tool (the shape an arrow's end is aimed at, the container a
drag would drop into); and groups of shapes in colors of a plugin's own, under all of those. Every
plugin's `registrar.outlines` and the hint go through one pass of the core, which draws a closed
shape's outline off its edge rather than on it, whatever its kind.

- **Stood off.** A closed shape's outline is its kind's `indicatorPath` grown outward by
  `editor.outlineStandoff` view points (`Style.outlineStandoff`, 4), all the way round, its corners
  concentric: a rounded rect of radius r is outlined by one of radius r + 4 about the same centers,
  and a plain rect's outline has corners of radius 4. A kind does nothing and can't opt out, which is
  the point: a line on the edge lies over whatever the shape draws there (a subboard's indigo border,
  a frame's hairline, a note's shadow), a different amount for each kind, and a gap of the canvas
  between the shape and the line makes every kind read as outlined at once, and alike. It's not
  tldraw's or the proof of concept's, whose outlines are on the edge (an intended deviation: the
  hint on a shape an arrow's end is aimed at, [Arrows](#the-connector-arrows), stands off too).
- **In view points.** The gap is divided by the zoom where it's drawn, so it's 4 points on screen at
  every zoom, as the line's width is. An outline's path, `editor.outlinePath(of:)`, is in world
  units at the zoom the camera has.
- **Open outlines aren't stood off.** An arrow's or a line's (its kept geometry isn't closed) has no
  inside to stand off from, and is stroked on its own path, as tldraw strokes it.
- **The box around several shapes** (`Outlines.rects`, Selection's) stands off the same way, so it
  encloses the shapes' own outlines where they're outermost.
- **What it costs.** A frame costs what's in view, and ⌘A outlines thousands, so a rect or a rounded
  rect, which is what every box kind's `indicatorPath` is, is grown directly: the core reads the
  path twice, over its end points and with nothing made (its straight edges lie on the sides of the
  kept geometry's bounds and leave the same room at both ends, which is the corner radius, whatever
  the corners' curves are made of), and adds a rounded rect in its place. Any other closed outline (a
  polygon, an ellipse, a path of your own) is grown by path arithmetic, `CGPath.grownOutward(by:isClosed:)`,
  the same Validation's rings are grown with, which costs far more than a rounded rect, for every shape
  every frame it's outlined: a kind with thousands of shapes outlined together keeps its `indicatorPath` a rect
  or a rounded rect of its box, or says nothing and takes the cost (debug builds count it,
  `outlinesGrownByArithmetic`).
- **Zoomed out** an outline is the [skeleton's](#skeletons), a ring on the frame, and nothing stands
  off: below 35% it's on the edge, and from 35% up it stands off, so a selected shape's line steps
  out 4 points as the zoom crosses the level, as its text and shadow come in. The shape being
  edited, drawn in full at any zoom, is stood off.
- **Around it.** What draws along an outline goes by the same gap, never the number. Validation's
  ring is 3 view points outside the outline, so 7 out of a closed shape's edge, and outside its
  tinted rings ([Validation](#a-horizontal-plugin));
  Ports outlines the shapes a connection could end on along `editor.outlinePath(of:)`, as a hover
  is. Resize handles are on the box itself, not the outline, drawn over it: the line runs under
  them, as it did when it lay on the edge they sit on. A title's pill (9 points above the top edge)
  and Locking's lock stay clear of the line; port dots are 12 points out.
- **Tinted groups.** `Outlines.tinted` is a list of `TintedOutlines` (a `color`, its `shapes` and a
  `ring`): a plugin's own colors, such as the lights [Neighbors](#neighbors) outlines a hovered
  shape's neighbors with. The core strokes each group before the faint outlines and the full ones
  (the groups in the order the plugins gave them), so a selected or hovered shape's own line shows
  over its tint; each is `Style.tintedIndicatorWidth` wide (2 view points, a little wider than the
  selection's 1.5, and opaque) and, in ring 0, where the selection's line stands: centered 4 off a
  closed shape's edge. A ring past the first stands a line and a gap further out
  (`Style.tintedRingGap`, 2): ring 1 is 4 view points more off the edge (8 in all), ring 2 four
  more, so the rings' centers are whole pixels at 1× and 2×, corners concentric, and a shape in two
  groups shows both, one ring round the other. Zoomed out the ring is on the shape's frame, grown by
  the same. A shape that's outlined in full too (selected, or the hint) has its tint one ring
  further out, clear of the selection's line, which would otherwise lie over most of ring 0, at
  every zoom: looked up only for the shapes in view, a few outlined in full compared one by one
  and many through one set, and not at all while nothing is tinted or nothing outlined in full.
  An open outline (an arrow's) is stroked on its own path, whatever its ring: of a kind drawn as a
  line ([`StrokedShape`](#capabilities), the arrow's 3.5), in full, it's covered, `max(2, the line's
  width × the zoom + 1)` view points wide, round, over its line and its heads, so it's the line in
  the tint's color and not a stripe along it; zoomed out, 2 wide. A hover's faint outline beside
  tinted ones is the shape they're about, and is stronger, 85% where it's 60% alone. A group costs
  what any outline does: a look at each shape's kept extent, and only those in view stroked, in one
  path of its own. `Outlines` and `TintedOutlines` are `Equatable`, so a plugin that keeps what it
  hands the core tells whether it changed and asks for a frame (`editor.setNeedsDisplay()`) only then.
  The core knows no meaning of a color or a group; the minimap fills the same shapes in the same
  colors under the faint ones and the selection's, a shape in two groups showing both (the second's
  fill inset 1.6 minimap points inside the first's, the accent of a selected one inside its
  tints), the rest of the picture dimmed and what's lit over the viewport's veil while anything is
  lit, so what's lit off screen shows there. CanvasTests' outline tests hold them: the line's color
  and place at 100% and 200%, a second ring further out (a gap of whole pixels), a selected
  shape's tint a ring out (the hint too, a hover not, a few selected and many, zoomed out),
  under the selection's and a hover's line, the faint line's strength beside tints, a skeleton's
  ring, an open shape's path whatever the ring, a line covered at 50%, 100% and 200% (and
  2 wide zoomed out, the selection's and a hover's thin), none while a session hides outlines, and
  groups merged from two plugins in order.
- **Beyond the rings.** An overlay that decorates a closed shape outside its outline stands outside
  the tint too: `OverlayContext.tintedOutset(of:)` is how far, in view points, the outermost tinted
  ring round the shape stands beyond ring 0 this frame (4 for each ring past the first, counting
  the one further out of a selected shape's tint; 0 with none or one, and for an open shape), worked
  out for every shape the groups name when first asked, one pass over what's tinted, and not for a
  frame that doesn't ask; `greatestTintedOutset` is the most it could be, a pass over the groups, for
  an overlay that culls shapes by how far its decoration reaches. Validation's ring is the one that
  asks.
- **Hosts and tests.** `editor.outlineStandoff` is host API: 0 outlines every shape on its own path,
  as the proof of concept drew, which its goldens are drawn with (CompositionTests' ParityTests) and
  CanvasTesting's `EditorHarness` draws with, so pixel tests that read an outline on a shape's
  edge go on measuring it; a test of the standoff sets it to what ships. Plugins read
  `editor.outlineGap`, which is it, and `editor.outlinePath(of:)`.

## Skeletons

Zoomed out over a big board, thousands of shapes are in view and nothing on them reads: below 35%
a note's 16-point text is under 6 points on screen, texture rather than words, yet drawing it, the
shadows and the pills is most of such a frame. So there the canvas draws each shape as its
**skeleton**: what the shape is and where, less than the real view, its fills and bars where its
text would be, never text, shadows or pictures of its own. Zoomed back in past the level, each
shape is itself again. At 10,000 shapes zoomed out as far as the zoom goes (10%, some 1,700 in
view), the first frame took 166.9 ms before skeletons, and each after 89.1; with them, and
[adornments](#the-label) drawn blank too (since left off, with a title said on a shape big enough on
screen instead), 13.4 and 11.2 (at 1,000 shapes, all in view at 11%, 96.9 and 50.0 before, 9.2 and
7.8 after).

- **One level for the canvas.** `editor.drawsSkeletons` is true while the camera's zoom is under
  `editor.skeletonZoom`, 35%. It's the zoom's, frame by frame, with no hysteresis or debounce
  ([not built yet](#not-built-yet)). The shape being edited is drawn in full whatever the zoom,
  since its editing view is over it (`editor.drawsSkeleton(of:)` says whether one shape is a
  skeleton now), and a frame decides once (`OverlayContext.drawsSkeletons`, and its
  `drawsSkeleton(of:)`). What an overlay draws, or hit testing finds, of a shape's content goes by
  the shape's own level (`drawsSkeleton(of:)`), so what's shown and what answers the pointer agree,
  and the shape being edited keeps its faces and its adornments' text: Selection's
  [faces](#faces-clickable-parts-of-a-shape), Adornments' [labels](#the-label). A shape's
  geometry isn't told the level (`ShapeContext` has no `drawsSkeletons`, and `skeletonZoom` is host
  API), so hit testing, the marquee, arrows' ends, snapping and the minimap go by each shape as they
  always did, and Ports' dots show from 25% as ever, over skeletons too.
- **The host's switch.** `skeletonZoom` is host API (`@_spi(Host)`), so no plugin moves the level or
  reads the number. 0 draws every shape in full at every zoom, for a test held to pictures drawn
  before there were skeletons ([the POC's renders](#testing-plugins)) or about what a shape draws in
  full far out; a value above 1 draws skeletons at 100%, for a test module that can't make a
  `Camera` (it has no Geometry). Setting it redraws, when it changes.
- **The default**, for a kind without a skeleton of its own, is its geometry as the index keeps it,
  drawn as a rough picture of the board draws it (`context.drawSkeleton(of:color:)`, on
  `RenderContext`): a closed outline filled, an open one stroked a view point wide with round caps,
  in one neutral gray (a board preview's, on the light canvas; as far from the dark canvas in the
  dark), with no shadow and nothing inside. It follows [Silhouettes](#the-cores-part-board-previews)'
  rule in device pixels: under 4 pixels both ways a shape is its bounds (a line from its first point
  to its last, if it's open), and under one, the whole device pixel its middle is in, as the
  minimap's silhouettes are, so a far-off shape still shows wherever it lies (a square a pixel wide
  around its middle would be spread over as many as four at a quarter each). A shape with no outline
  (nothing drawn) draws nothing.

A kind's own is `CustomSkeleton` ([Capabilities](#capabilities)): `renderSkeleton` draws in the
default's place, given the `RenderContext` a render gets. Patches' fills its frame in its pink
([your first plugin](#your-first-plugin)); a freehand line's is the default in a color of its own, so a
line drawn by hand still tells from an arrow:

```swift
extension PolylineDefinition: CustomSkeleton {
    func renderSkeleton(_ shape: ShapeRecord<Polyline>, in context: RenderContext) {
        guard let geometry = context.shapes.geometry(of: shape.id) else { return }   // kept, never worked out again
        context.drawSkeleton(of: geometry, color: PolylineStyle.color)
    }
}
```

The registry finds each kind's once (`registry.customSkeletons`), so a frame asks a shape nothing
but its kind. `drawSkeleton` saves and restores the graphics state and paints as `fillPath` does,
so call it with no path of your own under way.

- **Keep it cheap.** Zoomed out a frame draws thousands, so a skeleton is a few fills that cost
  about the same whatever the shape holds. It reads the shape, its kept geometry
  (`context.shapes.geometry(of:)`) and `context.zoom`, never anything that parses or lays out text:
  a line's bar is as long as its columns at an average advance (`SkeletonText`, below), not as its
  measured width, and its text is read only as far as the shape shows it (a note's paragraph until
  it fills the lines left); what a plugin keeps of a shape it uses only if it's there, making
  nothing. A picture it may still draw, as the render would, through `RenderContext` (a
  subboard's board preview). A plugin can't read `skeletonZoom`, so a kind that simplifies further,
  farther out, goes by `context.zoom`.
- **Greeked text**: `context.fillSkeletonText(bars)` fills the rects where text would be (world
  units, a line's worth each) in one fill of the canvas's text-bar color, a translucent dark (black
  at 20%, 26% in the dark) that takes the hue of the light body under it, so every kind's greeked
  text looks alike, and overlapping bars are no darker than one. It takes any `Sequence<CGRect>`, so
  a kind hands its bars over as it works them out, with no array per shape per frame: a
  paragraph's lines through the core's `SkeletonTextBars` (a note's text: `SkeletonTextBars(text, in: box, metrics:)` for plain text, or over a kind's own runs,
  each a `SkeletonTextRunConvertible`, text or something set inline as wide as some columns, a
  mention's pill), counted as a note's lines are ([a vertical plugin](#a-vertical-plugin)).
- **How long greeked text is**, without laying it out:
  [`SkeletonText.columns(of:)`](../Sources/Canvas/Rendering/SkeletonText.swift), the core's, pure,
  counts it in columns, a narrow character's width each, as a terminal does (Markus Kuhn's
  `wcwidth`, approximated by the Unicode blocks that hold most of each): 2 for a character set a
  full em wide (East Asian Wide and Fullwidth: CJK, kana, Hangul, fullwidth forms) or drawn as an
  emoji, 0 for one drawn on another or not at all (combining marks, Hangul's trailing jamo,
  variation selectors, skin tones, zero-width spaces and joiners, direction marks), else 1, a
  regional indicator too (a flag is two); and a scalar a zero-width joiner joins to the one before
  it counts nothing, since the sequence draws one emoji (a family is two columns). One pass over the
  text's UTF-8, a byte at a time while it's ASCII. A bar is its columns at an average narrow
  advance: a note's lines and a subboard's title at 0.52 em a column
  (calibrated against string drawing, `SkeletonTextMetrics.systemFontColumn`), and a title's cover
  sized by them, at an advance measured once from a sample. So every kind's bars count alike, and text in Japanese or in emoji is about as
  long greeked as in full, where a column a character would make it half. A script set wider or
  narrower than two columns' 1.04 em is off by the difference: in a subboard's 15-point title,
  Hangul measured about 0.85 em a character and emoji about 1.3.
- **Its outline** (selected, hovered, the hint) is its skeleton's, not its `indicatorPath`: its
  kind's own if the kind adopts `CustomSkeletonOutline` (`skeletonIndicatorPath(of:in:)`, nil for
  its kept geometry's), else its kept geometry's outline, the default skeleton's, with no
  [standoff](#outlines); the shape being edited keeps its own, stood off. The registry finds the kinds that adopt it once
  (`registry.skeletonOutlines`), so no other kind's shape is asked. ⌘A zoomed out outlines every
  shape in view each frame, and stroking a path costs far more than filling one, so there a rect
  (most shapes' geometry, and a plugin's rects, the box around several) is filled as a ring, what
  the stroke would paint but for its square corners; the rest is stroked, round. A shape a few
  pixels across is outlined by its bounds, as its default skeleton is drawn, and isn't asked its
  `skeletonIndicatorPath`. A translucent color (the hover's faint outline) with both rings and
  strokes goes into a layer, so it's no darker where they meet. So `skeletonIndicatorPath` costs
  what the skeleton does, made from the shape and its kept geometry; a kind whose skeleton fills its
  geometry or differs from a rect only by corners rounded a pixel or two (notes, cards, subboards)
  leaves `CustomSkeletonOutline` out, and its ring costs less. An arrow's kept geometry is only
  three points, so it adopts it, and its outline is its arc and its heads, each a closed triangle. The rings took ⌘A's outlines at 10,000
  shapes zoomed out from about 8.1 ms to 4.2, as measured; a pan's frame with all 10,000 selected
  measured 14.4 ms at 10% and 9.4 at 100%, against 11.2 and 7.7 with none selected, each shape
  outlined out of view costing a look at its kept extent
  ([drawing](#the-editor-the-document-and-drawing)).
- **Hearing the level change**: `EditorService.drawsSkeletonsDidChange(in:)`, when
  `drawsSkeletons` changes, and only then: the camera's zoom across the level (a pinch, a zoom
  command; a pinch changes the camera on every event, and services hear only the crossing), the
  host moving the level across the zoom, or a board shown with its camera at the other level, heard
  after `boardDidChange`. Never as editing begins or ends: the shape being edited draws in full
  either way. A pointer held still says nothing, so a service whose hit testing goes by what a
  shape shows lets go here of what the level doesn't show now: Selection looks again at what the
  pointer rests on, buttons first, as a move does, so a button that comes or goes with the level (a
  lock chip, shown only in full) takes or gives up the hover without its plugin saying so;
  Adornments lets go of what it made as skeletons start, and looks for nothing itself, its
  layouts answering at the new level whichever service hears first.
- **Batch what's drawn per shape**, in an overlay too, since zoomed out a frame draws it thousands
  of times: Core Graphics fills many rects, or lines, in one path for a fraction of what filling
  each alone costs, while a path of many curves costs more than each filled alone. So Validation, as
  the core's outlines do, fills square-cornered rings, where rounded ones stroked together cost ten
  times what each stroked alone does. Keep the order where it shows: a run of one look at a time,
  in paint order, so what's over what doesn't change. And make nothing per shape a frame, no array
  or boxed value: the core builds its rings and lines point by point, and Adornments lays each
  shape's labels out into one buffer a frame. Look at a shape's kept bounds before anything that
  costs more, as Titles' covers do (a shape too small on screen is passed over before its title
  is looked up), so only the shapes big enough lay text out.

What each shipped plugin shows zoomed out is in its own section: a [note](#a-vertical-plugin) (its
yellow, its text greeked, and no [mention text](#drawing) or [faces](#on-the-canvas-faces)), a
[subboard](#subboards) (fills and its preview), an [arrow](#a-shape-without-a-frame)
(its arc and heads, a label left off);
[faces](#faces-clickable-parts-of-a-shape) (none on a skeleton), [adornments](#the-label) (none on a
skeleton: a title's [pill](#a-horizontal-plugin) and a [lock](#locking)'s chip are left off, and a
title is said on the shape, its [cover](#a-cover-zoomed-out)), and
[Validation](#a-horizontal-plugin)'s outlines (rings).

## Boards in a file

A file holds a tree of boards: the root, and a board for each shape of a kind that owns one, a
subboard. Owning a board is a capability, `BoardOwning`, with nothing to implement: the core holds
the boards, saves them, takes them out and brings them in with their owners, and shows one at a
time;
[Boards](#boards) gets you around them, whatever kind owns them; and [Subboards](#subboards) is the
shipped kind, a card that opens onto its board.

- **The file is a value.** `CanvasFile` is the root board (`root`, a `CanvasDocument`) and
  `children`, a board for each owner, keyed by the owner's `ShapeID`. A board is named by a
  `BoardID`: `.root`, or `BoardID(owner:)`, written "root" or the owner's id. Keying a board by its
  owner makes the tree a function: a board's parent is whichever board holds its owner
  (`parent(of:)`, `path(to:)`, root first), so a board has one owner, deleting the owner can take
  its board, and a copy (a new id) has a board of its own; nothing done in the app can make a loop
  or give two shapes one board, and only a file edited by hand can have them, which reading keeps
  and reports ([Boards on disk](#boards-on-disk)). Shape ids are unique across the file
  (`board(containing:)`, `record(_:)`). `shape(on: board, holding: id)` is the shape on a board
  that holds another shape: `id` itself if it's on `board`, else the owner, on `board`, of the board
  it's on or of one above it, so a shape on a board that isn't shown is drawn as the card that holds
  it, at any depth (nil for a shape on a board above or beside `board`, or not in the file; a
  container is on its contents' board, so the owners are the whole answer). A board with no shapes
  isn't kept, so placing an owner makes nothing but the shape. Walks over the tree (`path(to:)`,
  `shape(on:holding:)`, `subtree(ownedBy:)`) are loops that stop at a board they've met.
- **Each board has a revision** (`file.revision(of:)`) that changes with its shapes and never comes
  back (a file put in place keeps it only for a board whose shapes are as they were). What's kept
  about a board (its index, its rows, its issues, its locks, its preview) is taken back only while
  its revision is the one it was kept at, so whatever writes a board, shown or not (an undo, a
  model's answer, someday an agent or sync), nothing stale is used.
- **The board is the owner's, never its props'.** A kind's props don't name its board, and its
  schema is marked `x-canvas-board`.

The smallest kind that owns boards is CanvasTesting's pocket, which core and horizontal tests nest
boards with ([Pockets.swift](../Tests/CanvasTesting/Pockets.swift)):

```swift
public struct Pocket: BoxShapeProps {
    public static let kind: ShapeKind = "pocket"
    public static let properties = Properties<Pocket> { Property("frame", \.frame).required() }
    public var frame: CGRect
}

struct PocketDefinition {}

extension PocketDefinition: ShapeDefinition {
    func render(_ shape: ShapeRecord<Pocket>, in context: RenderContext) {
        context.fillWithShadow(CGPath(rect: shape.frame, transform: nil), .systemGray)
    }
}

extension PocketDefinition: BoardOwning {}          // each pocket owns a board
```

That's all: a pocket deleted takes its board and every board under it, a pocket copied takes what
it holds, the file saves them, and `editor.showBoard(BoardID(owner: pocket))` shows one. A
double-click, Return and ⌘↓ opening it, Open in its menu, ⌘↑ back up and a name on the path come
from one more line, Boards' `x.opensBoard(placeholder:systemImage:)`.

### The editor and the file

One editor holds a whole file and shows one board of it, so every host that has `let editor` (a
window, the command line's server, a test's harness) keeps it. The editor holds every board
(`editor.file`) and shows one (`editor.board`; the root until another is shown, below):
`document` is that board, what every tool, drawing, hit test and service works on, so read what's
shown from `document`, and never list shapes from `file`. `editor.contents(of: board)` is any
board's shapes, and `editor.owner(of:)` the shape that owns it, wherever it is.

A transaction is on the board shown (`transaction.board`) and never holds the file: it reads it
through the editor, so a commit, a drag's every event, costs what it changed, not the file. Four
things reach past it, all in the one commit:

- **Deleting a shape takes the board it owns, and every board under that** (the cascade), whatever
  its kind, since the file keeps a board by its owner's id (`ChangeSet.boardsRemoved`), with no
  handlers run inside them, as nothing outside a board is bound to a shape in it. It's one undo
  step, and undoing it puts back every board under the shape, every id as it was. An owner whose
  board, or a board under it, holds a read-only shape (a locked one) isn't deleted, and shakes
  ([read-only shapes](#the-cores-part-read-only-shapes)).
- **A shape can go in with its boards**, `transaction.insert(record, contents:)`, its board under
  its id and those below under theirs (a paste; `boardsAdded`): a board it doesn't reach, or whose
  owner can't go in (a frame that isn't finite, deleted in the same transaction), is left out.
  `transaction.contents(of: board)` is any board as the transaction leaves it (its own `document`,
  one it staged, none for one it took, else the file's), and `contents(ofBoardOwnedBy:)` the board
  a shape owns.
- **Shapes can move onto any other board of the file**, `transaction.move(ids, to: board)`, up, down
  or across the tree: shapes of this board go onto that board, under their ids (so whatever names
  them still does), in their order, on top of what it holds as the transaction leaves it, with what
  a container among them holds at any depth and the boards they own (a board goes with its owner,
  wherever that is), where they were (world coordinates kept); `transaction.translate(ids, by:
  delta, on: board)` moves them there, as `translate` does on the board shown (what a container
  holds goes along; what the transaction brought there isn't held), so a shape can go somewhere
  else there after its bindings were let go where it was drawn ([Moving](#moving)).
  `transaction.rodeAlong` names what the move took along though it was not asked for (the arrows
  below), which the caller that puts the shapes down there translates with them, so the free end of
  an arrow that rode along keeps its place against its note. A shape stays in
  a container that moves with it, and is in none there otherwise, until
  `transaction.settle(ids, on: board)` puts it down there by the in-or-out rule, as a drop puts
  shapes down on the board shown ([Containers](#containers)). The board is new to the
  file (`boardsAdded`) or, if the file held shapes there, changed (`boardsChanged`, as the root
  always is); the shapes are removed from this one. Bindings
  ([`ShapeReferencing`](#values-that-name-shapes)) are to shapes on the same board, so what's bound
  across the edge is let go of, both ways, as a deletion lets go: a shape that stays lets go of what
  moves (an arrow's end stays where it's drawn), and one that moves of what stays, locked or not;
  but a shape that binds only to shapes that move (an arrow between two notes moved together, named
  or not; judged against what moves before any such shape joins, so a binding of one to another of
  them, being bound to what is not moving yet, lets go, whichever is lower in the stack) isn't across
  the edge: it moves with them, unless it's locked, which stays and lets go like any other (the move
  is not refused for it; a caller that must leave nothing locked behind, Transform's container
  channel for a frame turned into a subboard, names it among the movers, and the turn is refused); names (a mention) are kept. It's all or nothing for [read-only
  shapes](#the-cores-part-read-only-shapes): if the board's owner (held as `setContainer` holds a
  container, on its own board), or a shape that would move, is read-only or in a read-only
  container, nothing moves, `move` returns false, and `transaction.refusedShapes` says which. It's
  false too for a board the editor couldn't show once the transaction commits (`canShow`'s rule,
  each owner where the transaction leaves it, so a pocket it moved is where it moved it, and a
  corral it turned into a pocket owns a board). The board can't be the transaction's own, one going
  with a shape it deleted, or the board of a shape that moves or one under it (preconditions), and a
  shape that owns a board it moved shapes onto, or is above one, can't be deleted in the same
  transaction (another; no flow does). `transaction.move(ids, toBoardOwnedBy: owner)` is the board a
  shape on this board owns, false for an owner that isn't here or owns no board, so a plugin that
  turns it first moves only once `turn` took: with `turn` it's a frame turned into a subboard that
  holds what the frame held, in one step.
- **And off any board**, `transaction.move(ids, from: source, to: board)`: as `move(_:to:)`, from a
  board that isn't the transaction's, as the transaction leaves it (a transaction over that board,
  reading every other board as this one leaves it), onto any other, the board shown too, where they
  come on top of what it holds, `added` there (`changed`, if this transaction had taken them off it);
  the board they leave is `boardsChanged`, what left it `elsewhere`, and one they empty goes from the
  file. A shape dropped in the table of contents from a subboard's board open under its row comes
  off it this way ([Moving](#moving)). `move(_:above:on:)` and `move(_:below:on:)` restack shapes on
  another board, as `move(_:above:)` and `move(_:below:)` do on this one (what a container holds goes
  along; a read-only shape that was there is refused). A commit writes every board it changed, its
  own among them, together (`CanvasFile.set` of several), each letting go of what leaves it before
  any takes in what comes, so a shape moved either way between two is on one at a time.

- **And shapes can be written to on any board**, `transaction.update(id, on: board) { record in … }`
  (typed, with `as:`; `update(inFile: id)` on whichever board the shape is on, which
  `transaction.board(containing: id)` says, as the transaction leaves the file): as `update` changes
  one on this board, on that board as the transaction leaves it, so a shape moved onto it, or in with
  its owner, is found there. The change is part of this transaction's commit, so it is in the same
  undo step as the rest, and undo and redo put every board back, and again, exactly. The board is
  `boardsChanged` and the shape in `elsewhere`, so a service that follows a change set (the index,
  the table of contents, validation, Mentions) hears the shapes it wrote to as it hears the rest. A
  `willDelete` handler uses it to take back, on every board, what the deleted shape gave: one ⌘Z
  brings everything back. Nothing happens for a shape that isn't on that board, a board the editor
  couldn't show once the transaction commits, or one that goes with a shape the transaction deleted
  (a handler's write on a board the same deletion takes leaves no trace, and undo brings the board
  back as it was). Read-only shapes and boards are held as on this board (refused, noted in
  `refusedShapes`, unless the change leaves a shape no longer read-only), except inside the
  deletion keeping the board whole: a `willDelete` handler's writes go through a lock, on every
  board, as its writes on this one do (a locked shape that depended on what is deleted is taken back
  too). A transaction on a board that isn't shown (`transact(on:)`) may write to a third board the
  same way, in its own step; one that would write to the board shown commits nothing, as when it
  moves shapes onto it.
- **And shapes can be deleted on any board**, `transaction.delete(ids, on: board)`
  (`delete(inFile: ids)` on whichever boards they are on, the deepest board first, so a board's
  owner named beside shapes on its board goes after them and their handlers run, the same on every
  call): as `delete` takes shapes from this
  board, over that board as the transaction leaves it, in this transaction's commit and so its undo
  step. The `willDelete` handlers run there with `transaction.board` that board and every shape as
  it was (bound, in place, in its container), bindings to the deleted shapes are let go of on that
  board, a container released, and the boards under a deleted shape go with it
  (`boardsRemoved`), one undo bringing every id back. The board is written but not held, as
  `update(_:on:_:)` writes it, so deleting its owner in the same transaction is allowed and takes
  the board with it; what a handler there wrote on other boards, this one's too, comes in. A
  read-only shape there stays, refused (`refusedShapes`), as `delete` keeps one here, except in a
  handler. The owner of the board this transaction is on, and of each board above it, stays
  whoever asks for it, a handler there included; and `transact(on:)` commits nothing that deleted
  an owner on the way to the board shown, on whichever board and whether or not the transaction
  had brought it there. `Transaction.mayReachBoardShown` is false in such a step and in what it does on
  other boards: a handler that would delete or write on the board shown leaves that part out, or the
  step is lost. A shape brought onto the board (moved, or put in with its boards) and
  deleted there, named or reached by a handler, is on no board and takes its boards with it, as any
  deleted owner does (one put in with them and deleted never was); the boards of a shape a handler
  moved off the boards it was under are not taken with them. Each shape's handlers run once
  however the boards cross: a handler of such a delete that deletes back a shape whose deletion is
  under way, on this board or another, is passed over. `board(containing:)` is nil for a shape the
  transaction deleted, on whichever board, which it can put in again (`insert`) as it can one it
  deleted from its own. The board shown isn't touched, unless a handler of the delete changed it:
  then its stack is changed (`ChangeSet.reordered`) whenever the order of its shapes is not what it
  was, a shape removed, moved off or on, put in, or restacked, and the commit names each shape for
  what it is against the board as it was (one that came and had not been there: `added`; one that
  was there and went away and came back, or was restacked: `changed`), and undo doesn't switch boards. A board the
  file held no shapes on, and holds none on when the transaction ends, isn't added. A step recorded
  on a board (`transact(on:)`) while an open step holds any board that step reaches (its own, or one
  it changes, adds or removes: a card's that wrote there) closes the open one first, so each undoes
  and redoes exactly.

Delete Hidden Shapes does the same for a `willDelete` handler's writes on other boards: the boards
it wrote on, or brought, are in the one step and in what services hear.

Shape ids are unique across the file: an insert's must be on no board (unless the transaction
deleted it from its own). An undo step holds the boards a commit takes out, brings in or changes,
whole, as they were before the step and are after it ([Undo](#undo)).

The host's whole-file operations are `replaceFile(with:showing:)`, `replaceDocument(with:)` (a file
of that board alone) and `discardKeptAside(shapes:boards:)`. `replaceFile` is opening and
reverting: it cancels a running session, ends editing and camera motion, fills in defaults on every
board, gives every board a new revision (but one whose shapes are as they were: a reload after a
change on disk keeps the previews of boards it didn't change) and clears the undo history, so it
doesn't edit the file, nor does what the session, services or an editing view commit as they end,
which goes to the file replaced. It stays on the board shown if the new file can show it, else goes
to the nearest board above it, or the root, unless `showing:` names one it can show, as a switch
does (and `CanvasEditor(registry:file:showing:)` opens on one). `discardKeptAside` is Delete Hidden
Shapes: shapes kept aside wherever they are, with their boards, and the boards kept; one undo step,
"Delete Hidden Shapes", whatever boards it took them from, whose undo puts back the file as it was.

### Showing a board

`editor.showBoard(board)` shows another board of the file: it becomes `document`, and
`editor.boardPath` is the boards from the root down to it. It isn't an edit, nor an undo step (it
closes the step under way), and it can't happen mid-press: it returns false while a session runs,
and for a board `canShow` refuses (one whose owners, from the root down, aren't all in the file,
each of a `BoardOwning` kind and none kept aside; the board itself may have no shapes; the rule is
the file's, `file.canShow(_:boardOwningKinds:)`, nonisolated, so what reads a file off the main
actor, a query, draws the same line). In order:

1. Services hear `boardWillChange(from:to:)` while the old board is still shown: save what's its (a
   draft, state kept per board).
2. Editing ends, so an editing view that saves as it closes saves on its own board; the default
   tool comes back (an armed tool doesn't carry over; a tool that wasn't in the middle of something
   isn't cancelled); camera motion stops, and the old board keeps the camera it was headed to.
3. The new board takes back the geometry, paint order, bounds and damage the editor worked out for
   it, if its revision hasn't changed since (for the 8 boards shown last, those on the path kept
   longest), and otherwise works them out afresh; `revision` bumps once; and the camera is the one
   the board was left with, else the one the host remembers (`rememberedCameras`, host API, from
   the view memory; `boardCameras` is every board's, to save), else, on a first visit, its shapes
   fitted into view no closer than 100% (into what the host leaves clear of the view on that board,
   `coveredTop`: below the path's pill), else `Camera()`.
4. Services hear `boardDidChange(_ change: BoardChange)`, delivered as a commit is ([services hear a
   change](#services-hear-a-change)), so a service read there has heard it: `from`, `to`, `leftCamera`,
   `isFileReplaced` (a whole file was put in place as it went, `replaceFile`: what a service keeps
   across the file by shape id it takes afresh, since what it keeps by a board's revision is no
   longer taken back anyway), and `changes`, the switch as a commit's change set (every shape of
   one board gone, every shape of the other come, the stack changed; a shape on both, which only a
   file put in place can have, changed), worked out only if something reads it.
5. If the new board's camera draws [skeletons](#skeletons) where the old one's didn't, or the other
   way round, services hear `drawsSkeletonsDidChange`: only now, once they've heard the switch.
6. The host hears `editorBoardDidChange`, and redraws.

**Warm state.** By default a service hears nothing of the switch. One that keeps state per shape of
the board shown follows it as a commit, `documentDidChange(change.changes, in: editor)`, at the cost
of both boards' shapes; one that keeps state per board takes it back from a `BoardStash<State>`
(kept in `boardWillChange`, taken in `boardDidChange`, given back only while the board's revision
is unchanged, at most 8 boards, the path's longest), and may read another service there, which
hears the switch first. In the shipped plugins, the table of
contents, Validation and Grouping keep each board's rows, issues and grouped shapes in a stash (the
table of contents and Validation drop theirs when a file put in place shows another board, since that
switch doesn't say what the file changed on the boards kept, which a row or a rule may read);
Selection makes the board left a step back and lets go of the press, hover and buttons; Boards
makes the path again; Adornments drops its labels (made again only for the shapes a frame draws,
and a label kept would miss an open lock that Locking let go of); Types' index and sync keep
every type of the file by id (and takes them afresh when `isFileReplaced`), and Topology's index
and Mentions' resolutions and catalog are the file's, so a switch changes nothing for them (a file
put in place is read afresh); Ports lets go of the
dots it showed; the panel commits a number being typed in `boardWillChange`, and arrows stop aiming
there; and the context menus, the keyboard, the clipboard and the language model keep nothing per
shape, and hear nothing of it. So no shipped service works out the change set (CompositionTests'
BoardsTests hold them to it), and going back to a board shown lately costs the editor, the canvas and the services a frame
(`./build.sh bench`). Not the panel's list: with the table of contents showing, a switch replaces
every row of its `List`, which AppKit sizes one by one, some 120 ms at 1,000 rows and a second at
10,000, however warm the board ([Not built yet](#not-built-yet)).

Damage marks name the index they were taken on (`DamageMark`, `editor.isCurrent`), so a picture kept
for a board (the minimap keeps 8) is current only while the editor kept that board's index, and a
mark from another board's is damage everywhere. Of a kind's definition only its render reads another
board: `context.shapeCount(inBoardOwnedBy:)` and `context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy:in:)`
([previews](#the-cores-part-board-previews)), and `context.shape(inFile:)`, a shape anywhere in the
file on a board the editor can show (a mention's pill names one, [across
boards](#mentions-across-boards); `editor.shape(inFile:)` outside a render), on `RenderContext`
alone, so geometry and hit tests never depend on another board. A render may also read the
editor's services, `context.service(_:)` (as `EditContext.service(_:)` lends an editing view's), the
lender made once per frame; nothing observes a render, so a lending service calls
`editor.setNeedsDisplay()` when what it lends changes, or what's drawn goes stale (a shape out of
view, or drawn as a skeleton, doesn't read it). Going into and out of boards are [commands](#commands)
their plugins declare: Selection's `.openSelection` (⌘↓; [opening a shape](#selection)) and
[Boards](#boards)' `.enclosingBoard` (⌘↑) and `.goUpBoard`; and going back crosses boards.

### Boards that aren't shown

A commit says what it did beyond the board it's on: `ChangeSet.elsewhere` is every shape of the
boards it took or brought, and those it changed, or moved onto, on a board it kept (and, for a file
put in place over the board shown, the shapes its other boards don't have as they were). No shape
there stays on the board shown (one moved off it is removed from it too), so what a service keeps of
the board shown needn't follow them; what reads shapes anywhere in the file does (a row showing the
name of a shape on another board, gone with the board its owner took). `changes.before(id)` is a
shape's record as the commit found it, wherever it was (a shape moved onto a board is found as it was
on the other; nil for one the commit brought into the file), so a service that keeps what follows from one value of a shape (whether it's locked, public, grouped)
compares the record now with it rather than keep a copy. What reads every board the app can show
walks `editor.showableBoards` (the root, then down the tree the boards each one's shapes own, in
their owners' order, each once, O(the boards)); what reads the file whole, `file.everyBoard`.

Two things edit a board that isn't shown: Delete Hidden Shapes (`discardKeptAside`, [the editor
and the file](#the-editor-and-the-file)), which takes shapes kept aside from whatever boards hold
them, and `editor.transact(on: board, "Name") { … }`, for what lands after its board was left (a type's sync, whose answer comes back seconds later). On
the board shown it's `transact`; on another, the transaction's `document` is that board's shapes as
the file has them, and its commit changes that board in the file without showing it, as an undo
step of its own made on that board, so undoing it from anywhere shows that board first. A step open
on the board shown (a press, a field typed into) stays open and comes after it. Services hear it as
a commit that changed that board (`boardsChanged`, its shapes in `elsewhere`), the board shown as it
was, and the canvas redraws, so an owner's card on the board shown shows what it holds now. Nothing
shows what it refused (a read-only shape isn't shown to shake), and a transaction that would take
the board shown, or one above it, or reaches it (shapes moved onto it, which would leave `document`
stale), commits nothing. It returns nil for a board the editor can't show. Every other change to a
board is made while it's shown, or with a shape on the board shown (a deletion takes the boards
under it, a paste brings them, a move takes shapes onto one).

### Boards across the plugins

Every plugin that reads `document` is local to the board shown with no code of its own: drawing,
hit testing, Select All, the minimap, arrows, Reordering. What the others do with boards is with
each of them:

| Where | Boards |
|---|---|
| [Selection](#selection) | Opening a shape (`ShapeOpening`); Back crosses boards, and showing another board is a step; nothing is selected on arrival; `showBoard(_:selecting:)`; `goTo` goes to a shape on any board. |
| [Boards](#boards) | Opening a kind's boards, ⌘↑, a board's name and symbol, and the path over the canvas. |
| [The table of contents](#whats-listed-and-selecting) | Lists the board shown, keeps each board's rows, and takes its header from the plugin that names boards (Boards: the board's crumb). A row may read shapes on other boards ([`elsewhere`](#rows-read-from-more-than-their-shape)). |
| [Validation](#a-horizontal-plugin) | Checks the board shown, keeping each board's issues; a board never shown isn't checked, and a rule's lookups (`MentionValidationPlugin`'s targets) find shapes there alone; a rule over a service's state (`TitleValidationPlugin`'s titles, the file's) names the shapes a commit changes the issues of on any board, checked once their board is shown. |
| [Locking](#locking) | A shape whose board holds a locked shape isn't deleted; a locked owner is entered as any other. |
| [Mentions](#mentions-across-boards) | A mention names a shape on any board, live and followed there (`goTo`, or `goInto` for a kind followed by opening it: a subboard); who mentions whom (Topology's), what each mentioned shape shows and the `@` picker's catalog are the file's (the board shown's first on a tie), so showing another board reads no mention text; so are the Connections tab's and Show What Mentions' mentioners (the tab's in the file's order, Show What Mentions' the board shown's first). |
| [Topology](#topology) | The file's edges, and containment (a shape's parent is its container, else its board's owner), whatever board is shown; showing another board reads nothing. |
| [The clipboard](#the-clipboard) | Copies what a shape holds, all the way down, and pastes the tree with new ids; what a cut took, onto any board, under the ids it had (a move). |
| [Undo](#undo) | One history per file; a step holds every board it reached, and undoing one made on another board shows that board first. |
| [Boards on disk](#boards-on-disk) | Format 4 saves every board, in one flat map; the camera on each board, and the board left open, are remembered per file on this Mac. |
| [The command line](#the-command-line) | A draw works out its board from the titles it names (`in "X"`, the board X holds), whichever the window shows; `canvas show` moves the window. |

## Containers

A board's shapes can be in containers on that board: a container (a frame, [Frames](#frames)'
kind) holds the shapes there that name it, moves them with it, paints them above it, holds them read-only while it's read-only,
and keeps what's put down from sitting across its edge. Containers nest, to any depth. Being one is
a capability, `ShapeContaining`, of a box kind, with nothing to implement, so the core does all of
it, whatever kind contains ([Model/Containment.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Model/Containment.swift),
[Settling.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Model/Settling.swift), [Enclosing.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Model/Enclosing.swift)).
Core and horizontal tests contain with
CanvasTesting's corral ([Corrals.swift](../Tests/CanvasTesting/Corrals.swift)), apart from
`FixturesPlugin`:

```swift
public struct Corral: BoxShapeProps {
    public static let kind: ShapeKind = "corral"
    public static let properties = Properties<Corral> { Property("frame", \.frame).required() }
    public var frame: CGRect
}

struct CorralDefinition {}

extension CorralDefinition: ShapeDefinition {
    func render(_ shape: ShapeRecord<Corral>, in context: RenderContext) { … }
}

extension CorralDefinition: ShapeContaining {}       // its shapes hold shapes on its board
```

- **A shape keeps its container.** `AnyShapeRecord.container` is the container on its board it's
  directly in, nil on the board directly: structural, as its stacking key is, in no schema, and
  compared in `==`, so undo and every change set carry it with nothing more. It's set only in a
  transaction: `setContainer(_:to:)` (of a list of shapes too, which rise together, one look at what
  the container holds for them all; one at a time, a transaction keeps where each container tops out
  in the stack while nothing moves in it, so a loop of them costs as much), or an insert of a record
  that comes with one
  (`copy(as:container:)`, what a paste makes of a shape copied with its container), which the insert
  takes if that's a container on the board by then (inserted before it, as back to front puts it)
  that can take it, and on a board going in with its owner (`insert(_:contents:)`), one below it
  there. A plain `copy(as:)` is in no container until something puts it in one, and `update` never
  changes one. Only a box shape is in a container, never in itself or in what it holds.
- **What the core goes by.** A container the app can't use (kept aside, of a kind not installed, or
  of one that holds nothing) is kept as written, and saved back, and the shape counts as on its
  board directly; so does a shape kept aside. `document.container(of:containingKinds:)` is what the
  core goes by, and `contents(of:containingKinds:)` (back to front), `hasContents`, `descendants` (at
  any depth, back to front) and `containers(of:)` (the nearest first) read the document's index of
  who names whom, kept by every change and by `apply`, so each costs what it returns, never the
  board. They're nonisolated, for what reads a file off the main actor; `ShapeContext` lends
  `container(of:)`, `contents(of:)` and `hasContents(_:)` with the registry's kinds
  (`registry.containingKinds`): a frame's hit test reads whether it holds anything (a geometry that
  reads them is worked out again on every change, as one that reads `document` is).
- **A container is never laid out past its box.** A kind that is `ShapeContaining` and `LaidOutBox` is
  refused by the registry, so a container's edge is always its stored box. What is put down in one is
  judged by its laid-out frame, not its box (a shape grown by a layout input is not settled again).
- **Moving.** `translate`, and a drag (`TranslatingSession`), move what a container holds with it, at
  any depth, each shape once however it's asked for, read-only or not: a lock stops changes to a
  shape, not its container carrying it. The translation adjuster is given what's carried with the
  rest (`TranslationStart.ids`), so none of it is a snap target. Moving never changes what's in
  what; arrow keys' nudges (`translate`) settle nothing.
- **Deleting** a container lets go of what it holds, which stays where it is, now in the
  container's own container (the nearest one up that isn't deleted too), read-only or not, as letting
  go of a binding is; undoing the deletion puts it back in. A container holding a locked shape is
  deleted, and the shape stays, let go.
- **Turning.** `transaction.turn(id, into: record)` (or `into:` props) makes a shape another kind
  under its id: the record's kind and props in place of its own, the same shape otherwise, so
  whatever binds or names it (an arrow's end, a mention), its place in the stack, its container, its
  metadata and the values of the added properties both kinds hold (a title) go on as they were, and
  the record's added values (defaults, or what a placement set) fill in the rest. A container turned
  into a kind that holds nothing lets go of what it holds, as deleting it does: those shapes stay
  where they are, in its own container; turned into another container kind, it keeps them. A kind
  with no box can't be in a container, so a shape turned into one is on the board directly. It
  returns false, and changes nothing, for a shape that isn't on the board or is kept aside and for a
  frame that isn't finite, and a [read-only](#the-cores-part-read-only-shapes) shape (or one in a
  read-only container) is refused as `update` refuses it. A shape of a kind that owns boards whose
  board holds shapes can only become a kind that owns boards, or the board would have no owner: a
  precondition (`move(_:toBoardOwnedBy:)` takes the shapes out first). A corral turned into a
  pocket, with what it held moved onto the pocket's board in the same transaction, is a frame
  turned into a subboard ([Transform](#transform) does it for the app, with the menu item and the command).
- **Read-only.** A shape in a read-only container, at any depth, is read-only:
  `editor.isReadOnly(_:)` says so, on the board shown (`editor.isReadOnly(inFile:)` on any board:
  [the core's part](#the-cores-part-read-only-shapes), which also makes the shapes on a locked
  subboard's board read-only), and `registry.isReadOnly(_:)` stays the rules', for what reads one
  record alone. It changes not at all, not even its own lock;
  nothing joins or leaves its container (`setContainer` refuses the container, which shakes); and
  editing it ends.
- **The stack.** A container's contents paint above it: a shape that joins one rises, with what it
  holds, just above what the container holds already, if it was below that; restacking a container
  takes what it holds along, in its order (`bringToFront`, `sendToBack`, `bringForward`,
  `sendBackward`, `move(_:above:)`, `move(_:below:)`, keys halving between two shapes, so a big
  frame's grow with the logarithm of what it holds), and a shape in one goes no lower than just
  above it. A step past a shape a container holds does nothing. So Reordering's Arrange works as
  it is.
- **Settling** is the in-or-out rule: nothing sits across a container's edge.
  `transaction.settle(ids)` judges shapes put down (a drop, a placement, a paste, a draw) by area:
  more than half of a shape's box inside a container puts it in that one (where containers nest,
  the innermost holding most of it that it fits in), nudged fully in if it hangs over the edge;
  otherwise it's in none of them, nudged fully out of any it reaches into, the shortest way clear of
  them all that keeps it in the container it is in. A nudge ends 16 world units from the edge
  (`Style.containerGap`), so the edge stays clear to grab. Shapes put down together from one
  container are judged as one, by their summed area, and nudged by one translation, keeping their
  arrangement, with what can't be in a container (an arrow) riding along; those from different
  containers, container by container, so a small drag of a selection across two frames leaves each
  in its own; a group that doesn't fit the container holding most of it is judged shape by shape,
  and a shape too big for a container can't be in it. A shape over all of a container is over it,
  neither in it nor across its edge (a frame's copy pasted on its original stays beside it). Read-only
  shapes stay as they are, in or out, and a read-only container takes nothing: if anything would go
  into one, nothing changes, services hear that container refused (`didRefuseChanges`: Locking
  shakes it), and the answer names it (`Settlement.refused(by:)`), for the caller to send what was
  dropped back, or to give up what it was doing: in an `editor.transactWhole`, as Clipboard's paste
  is, the refusal gives the whole up, no step is left, and the container shakes.
  Each container put down then takes in what it lands on, `settle(container:)`, which is also what's
  called after a container is resized: what's in it hanging over its edge is nudged in, or leaves,
  mostly outside; what's at its level that it reaches is taken in, mostly inside, or nudged out;
  each alone, read-only ones skipped, and a shape a read-only container would take staying as it is,
  even one the transaction put down (a locked frame's copy, pasted, takes nothing it lands on).
  A shape is judged by its laid-out frame (`context.frame(of:)`: a `LaidOutBox` kind's box origin at
  the size its layout inputs say, larger or smaller, else its box), read before anything changes, and a container's own
  edge is always its stored box (a kind that holds shapes can't be a `LaidOutBox`). One that grows
  later, by an input changing, is not settled again: it stays where it is and may overlap a
  neighbor or hang over an edge. Create Frame's frame goes around the laid-out frames too.
  Both hand back what they nudged, by how far, what that carries included (`Settlement.nudges`), for
  the glide. O(the board), at a gesture's end. `transaction.settle(ids, on: board)` is the rule on
  another board of the file, against that board as the transaction leaves it: what `move(_:to:)`
  took there is put down as a drop puts it down on the board shown, a container among it taking in
  what it lands on there, and what the transaction brought there isn't held, as what it adds isn't.
  A refusal changes nothing there, and the caller throws, dropping the move; the nudges are that
  board's, where nothing glides. On the transaction's own board it's `settle(_:)`.
- **A drag**, once past the drag threshold, outlines the container what it moves would go into as
  the hint (`hintedShapeID`), never a read-only one, finding the containers once and costing what
  they are on each event; its release settles what was dropped, in the press's step (a click, short
  of the threshold, settles nothing), and glides what's nudged. A read-only container refusing the
  drop sends what was dragged back where it was, gliding from where it was dropped, and the press
  leaves no step; Escape puts it back at once, settling nothing. A shape placed (`editor.place`)
  settles on its release, or at once with no press under way, in the placement's step; refused, it's
  taken away; one placed to be edited isn't glided, since its editing view is laid out where it is.
- **Putting one down around shapes** (`editor.place(_:around:padding:minimumSize:)`, Frames' Create
  Frame) puts a new container (a record of a `ShapeContaining` kind, its id new) down around shapes
  on the board shown, holding them: those with a box, but what's in another of them (it goes with
  that one). Its frame is theirs, and an arrow's among them that's bound to some of them and to
  nothing else (`isBound(onlyTo:in:)`, as a move of shapes takes arrows along), grown by `padding`,
  kept the gap inside the innermost container they're all in, which it goes in, unless what it holds
  is nearer that one's edge, then grown to `minimumSize` about its middle as far as that room allows;
  a far edge flush with one of them is never an ulp short of it (an origin plus a size rounds, and
  settling would read the shape as hanging over). In the stack it goes just below the lowest of them,
  so they keep their places, and what was under them all, a big note behind them, stays under it. What
  it lands on beside them is settled as what a container drawn over shapes is (`settle(container:)`;
  what comes in rises above what it holds); those it took out of a container that it then took in are
  put down again with the others from it (`settle(_:)`), so they go back in rather than lying under
  it, and those from a container it didn't take in (one with no room to move clear) stay in it. One step, named as a placement's ("Add" and the kind's label, unless a group
  it's in names it); the default tool comes back, services hear `didPlace` (selected), and what was
  nudged glides. All or nothing: a read-only one among them (locked, in a read-only container, or on
  a read-only board) leaves it all as it was, with no step, and is heard refused. It returns the new
  shape's id, nil when it put nothing down (nothing with a box, a refusal, a kind that holds nothing).
- **The glide** (`editor.glide(_:)`, Glide.swift) eases shapes that just moved from where they were
  drawn to where they are, over 250 ms, going a little past and back (`Style.glideDuration`,
  `glideOvershoot`), through their [drawing offsets](#the-cores-part-drawing-offsets) on
  `editor.scheduler`, so hit testing and pictures of the board go by where they are, as with a
  shake. A new press, a session starting, a commit that touches a gliding shape, or another board
  shown ends its glide there.

Without a `ShapeContaining` kind installed none of this runs, and with no container on the board a
drop commits nothing more and glides nothing: the transcript and renders CompositionTests hold to
the proof of concept are as they were. A file is written as it always was until a shape is in a
container ([format 5](#boards-on-disk)).

### Cards

A card is a plugin's view shown under a rect of the board: white, like a menu, 4 points under the rect
it hangs from, sized in view points (zooming doesn't scale it), following the camera, taking clicks
and keys. A shape's row that holds more than a row can show (a list, a group of fields) opens into
one. The core knows nothing of what is in it: it hands the host an `NSView` and a size to ask for.

```swift
let card = CanvasCard(id: "tags", about: note, anchor: rowRect, view: listView, firstResponder: listView,
                      stepName: "Change Tags",
                      size: { room in listView.fittingSize(in: room) },     // at most `room`, in view points
                      didClose: { reason in … })                            // .pressedElsewhere, .undo, …
editor.showCard(card)                                                       // false: its shape is drawn as a skeleton
editor.transact(nil, coalescing: card.id) { … }                             // one step, "Change Tags", until it closes
editor.moveCard(to: newRowRect)                                             // its row moved
editor.closeCard()                                                          // .asked
```

One card shows at a time; a second replaces the first. It sits above the editing view and everything
the canvas hosts but the hover popover, and never nearer than 8 points to the canvas's edge or under
what the host covers of its top (`unobscuredViewport`): above its rect when there is no room below, and
cut to the room, its view scrolling itself. The keyboard goes to its `firstResponder`; a key or a menu
command its view does not take stops at the card (no tool letter, no Delete, no Select All reaches
the board), and Edit › Undo is still the window's. It closes, each time with its reason
(`CanvasCardClosing`, heard by `didClose` after the host has taken it down and the keyboard is back):

- a press anywhere in the window outside it and the rect it hangs from, a pan's too (`.pressedElsewhere`);
  a press on that rect is left to the plugin that showed the card, which hears its own click;
- editing beginning or ending (`.editing`; a plugin that begins editing and shows a card shows the
  card after), another board or file shown (`.board`), Undo or Redo (`.undo`);
- the zoom taking its shape to skeletons (`.skeleton`; a shape being edited is drawn in full, so its
  card stays), its shape deleted by a commit (`.shapeGone`), and its rect leaving the view
  (`.leftView`, as the caret list closes when its anchor leaves the visible text).

A scroll or a pinch over it does not move the board, and neither closes it. A commit from elsewhere
leaves it open.

**A card's step.** With a `stepName` its commits are one undo step, that name, from the card showing
until it closes: `transact(nil, coalescing: card.id)`, from outside any action (inside a press or a
`group` the commit is that action's). The panel's `seal()` and the window's mouse-downs do not end it;
any other commit does, and is a step of its own, and the card's next commit is another step by the
same name. Closing the card closes the step. `editor.setCardStep(_:)` changes the name (nil holds
none), which closes the step held.

A card made with `adoptsPress: true` and shown inside a press (or a `group` or a command: any
action) takes that action's step on: the step stays open when the action ends, as a placed note's
editing session keeps its step, so the changes the press made and the card's commits are one step,
named as the press named it. One Undo takes them all back once the card is dismissed (while a
card's text field has the keyboard, the board's Undo is the field's own). The step splits as any
card's does: a save (`breakStep`), a commit from elsewhere, a new press; the card's next commit is
a step of its own by its name. The card must be shown inside the action, not a turn later, and a
card shown outside one, or closed before the action ends, is as any card. Only `showCard` adopts:
`setCardStep` inside a later action closes the step held and keeps under the new name, never taking that
action's step.

## Undo

Undo is the core's ([`UndoHistory.swift`](../Sources/Canvas/Editor/UndoHistory.swift),
[`CanvasEditor+Undo.swift`](../Sources/Canvas/Editor/CanvasEditor+Undo.swift)), since every change
already goes through `transact`: each commit is recorded, as the records it touched were before it
and are after, into the step it's part of. A plugin does nothing to be undone. It only names its
steps, and says what one gesture is when the editor can't see it. It's tldraw's model, not
`NSUndoManager`'s: a board's history is its editor's (`editor.undoHistory`), one per board file.

**A step is one action.** Commits go into the step that's open, which opens with the first of them:

| What | Its step |
|---|---|
| A press on the canvas: from the press to the release, its whole drag (a place, its follow and the editing it begins on the release, a translate, a handle, a lock chip's click) | One. |
| A key on the canvas; a command (`editor.perform`: every menu item's, ⌘Z's and Delete's); `editor.undoHistory.group("Name") { ... }` | One each. These actions nest; the outermost is the step. A key's step takes what its repeats commit while it's held (`KeyStroke.isRepeat`, the same key with the same keys held), until it's let go (`editor.keyUp`, or `keysReleased`: the canvas lost the keyboard) or anything else happens (another key, a press, a commit, `seal()`, undo, a save), so a held arrow key's nudges are one step. |
| An editing session (a note typed into): its view's commits (`EditContext`) until editing ends, with what the view saves as it closes | One, "Typing"; with the action that began it, if one did (placing a note and typing into it are one step, as tldraw's one mark). |
| A run of commits under one key at no action's depth: `transact(coalescing: key)` (a panel field typed into, a slider dragged) | One, until another commit, an action, or `editor.undoHistory.seal()`. |
| A [card](#cards)'s commits, `transact(coalescing: card.id)`, while it shows with a step name | One, named by the card, from it showing until it closes; `seal()` does not end it, any other commit does. |
| Any other commit | One. |

Any other commit while a shape is being edited closes the editing step first; an action that
commits nothing of its own (Undo itself) leaves it open, so Undo, from a key or a menu, ends editing
and undoes the whole session, what the view saves as it closes included. Opening a step clears
what there was to redo. A step whose records all end where they began (a drag put back with Escape,
an arrow drawn and cancelled, a field typed into and undone) is dropped, and so is a transaction
all of whose changes were refused: nothing's recorded. Selecting, hovering, the camera and Go Back
aren't changes, and make no step.

**Naming.** A step takes its outermost named group's name, else its first named transaction's
(`editor.transact("Move") { ... }`), else "Typing" for an editing step (or what its kind's
`Editable.editingStepName` says); Edit › Undo shows it ("Undo Move"), or plain "Undo"; while the
open step has come back to where it began, Undo names, and undoes, the step before it. The core
names placing ("Add" and the placing tool's label, "Add Note"; a container put down around shapes,
its kind's, "Add Frame"), moving ("Move") and typing; Selection "Delete" and "Resize";
ContextMenus every item by its title; SlashCommands every command by its name in words ("Set
Title"), or its `step:`; Clipboard "Cut" and "Paste"; Locking "Lock" and "Unlock"; Publishing
"Make Public" and "Make Private"; Arrows "Add Arrow", "Move Arrow End", "Bend Arrow" and "Toggle
Arrowhead"; the detail panel "Change" and the section's title
